title: Rational analytic prismatization
summary: Build Gelfand analytic geometry over ℚ_p — bounded solid ℚ_p-algebras, Gelfand rings and their Berkovich spectra, Gelfand stacks, derived Berkovich spaces, analytic de Rham stacks, cones, deformation theory, Fargues–Fontaine curves and Hyodo–Kato stacks as Gelfand stacks — and on it the rational analytic prismatization of Anschütz–Le Bras–Rodríguez Camargo–Scholze: rational δ-spaces and analytic δ-stacks, the prismatization X^Δ of a Gelfand stack, its perfection, the p-adic twistor stack X^{Div¹} and the analytic Hodge–Tate stack X^HT, with the Breuil–Kisin twist, the prismatic logarithm and Faltings' extension. Independently, prove the decompletion theorem for Berkovich spaces with a continuous action of a p-adic Lie group and verify it in arithmetic, geometric and mixed Sen theory. The end theorems are: for a smooth partially proper rigid space X over a finite extension of ℚ_p, pullback along FF_{X^⋄} → X^{Div¹} is fully faithful and an equivalence on perfect complexes, also over every Berkovich-étale Y → X^{Div¹} (ALRS Theorem 6.3.1), with its perfectoid-base and arithmetic variants; Γ(X^{Div¹}, O) is pro-étale ℚ_p-cohomology; Hodge–Tate stacks recover v-perfect complexes with their arithmetic and geometric Sen operators and the inverse Faltings' extension; pro-étale torsors under p-adic Lie groups decomplete; Div¹ and twistor stacks of smooth maps satisfy Poincaré duality with the Breuil–Kisin twist; the prismatic first Chern class satisfies the projective bundle formula; and formal Hodge–Tate stacks recover Scholze's Riemann–Hilbert functor.

layers.title: Bounded solid ℚ_p-algebras and Gelfand rings

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsBounded
targets.statement: For an animated commutative algebra A over the light solid analytic ring ℚ_{p,■}, define the power-bounded subring A° by its values on light profinite sets S, A°(S) = Map(ℤ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩, A), where ℤ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩ is the p-adic completion of the free solid ℤ_p-algebra on S, and the bounded subring A^b = A°[1/p]. Call A bounded when A^b → A is an equivalence. Prove that A ↦ A^b is right adjoint to the inclusion of bounded algebras into solid ℚ_p-algebras, so that bounded algebras are closed under all colimits computed in solid ℚ_p-algebras (ABLB Definition 2.1.1, p. 12, ABLB line 609; ABLB Lemma 2.1.2, p. 12, ABLB line 622). Boundedness is a property and not extra structure, because ℤ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩ is idempotent over ℤ_{p,■}[ℕ[S]].
hypotheses: A is an animated commutative algebra in light solid ℚ_p-vector spaces with the induced analytic ring structure from ℚ_{p,■}

locator.where: Definition 2.1.1 and Lemma 2.1.2, p. 12; ABLB line 609

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.bounded_iff
api.statement: For bounded A and every light profinite S and map f: S → A there is n ≥ 0 such that p^n·f extends to an algebra map ℤ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩ → A; conversely this condition for all S implies boundedness.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.boundedPart_adjoint
api.statement: Maps from a bounded algebra B to a solid ℚ_p-algebra A factor uniquely through A^b → A; A^b is bounded and (A^b)^b = A^b.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsBounded.colimit
api.statement: Colimits of bounded algebras computed in solid ℚ_p-algebras are bounded; in particular pushouts and filtered colimits are.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.powerBounded_functorial
api.statement: Every algebra map A → B sends A° into B° and A^b into B^b.

tests.name: bounded_Qp
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p the point values are A°(*) = ℤ_p and A^b(*) = ℚ_p, so ℚ_p is bounded; replacing ℤ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩ by the uncompleted free algebra would make every element power-bounded.

tests.name: notBounded_polynomial
tests.statement: For the discrete polynomial algebra A = ℚ_p[T] with induced structure, no p^n·T extends to ℤ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p[T], since the image of Σ_k p^k T^k would be a non-terminating sum in ⊕_k ℚ_p T^k; hence A^b = ℚ_p and A is not bounded.

tests.name: bounded_Tate
tests.statement: The Tate algebra ℚ_p⟨T⟩ is bounded with T ∈ ℚ_p⟨T⟩°(*) = ℤ_p⟨T⟩.

tests.name: bounded_zero
tests.statement: The zero ring is bounded, with A° = A^b = 0.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.normFiltration
targets.statement: For r ∈ ℝ_{≥0} and a light profinite set S, let ℚ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩_{≤r} be the solid subring of ℚ_{p,■}⟦ℕ[S]⟧ of power series converging on the polydisc of radius r (ABLB Definition 2.2.3, p. 13, ABLB line 686). For a solid ℚ_p-algebra A define A_{≤r}(S) = Map(ℚ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩_{≤r}, A), A_{<r} = ⋃_{r′<r} A_{≤r′} and the †-nilradical Nil†(A) = A_{≤0} (ABLB Definition 2.2.8, p. 14, ABLB line 746). Then A_{≤1} is a solid animated ℤ_p-algebra, each A_{≤r} is a solid A_{≤1}-module, and A = ⋃_r A_{≤r} when A is bounded (ALRS §2.1, p. 13, ALRS line 640). Define the †-reduction A^{†-red} = A/Nil†(A), a static solid ℚ_p-algebra (ABLB Definition 2.2.19, p. 19, ABLB line 974). Prove that A_{≤1} → A^{†-red}_{≤1} over A → A^{†-red} is a pullback square, similarly for A_{≤r} and A_{<1}, and that Nil†(A^{†-red}) = 0 (ABLB Proposition 2.2.20, p. 19, ABLB line 981).
hypotheses: A is a bounded solid ℚ_p-algebra

locator.where: Definitions 2.2.3, 2.2.8, 2.2.19 and Proposition 2.2.20, p. 14; ABLB line 746

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.normFiltration_mono
api.statement: For r ≤ s one has A_{≤r} ⊆ A_{≤s}, and A_{≤r}·A_{≤s} ⊆ A_{≤rs}; multiplication by p maps A_{≤r} into A_{≤r/p}, matching |p| = p^{-1}.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.nil_dagger_ideal
api.statement: Nil†(A) is an ideal of A contained in A_{<r} for every r > 0, and every nilpotent element of A(*) lies in Nil†(A).

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.daggerReduction_universal
api.statement: Every algebra map from A to a †-reduced bounded algebra factors uniquely through A → A^{†-red}.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.normFiltration_functorial
api.statement: An algebra map A → B sends A_{≤r} into B_{≤r} for every r.

tests.name: normFiltration_Tate
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ one has A_{≤1} = ℤ_p⟨T⟩, A_{≤p^{-k}} = p^k ℤ_p⟨T⟩ and Nil†(A) = 0.

tests.name: nilDagger_dualNumbers
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p[ε]/ε² the element ε lies in A_{≤r} for all r, so Nil†(A) = ℚ_p·ε and A^{†-red} = ℚ_p.

tests.name: nilDagger_overconvergentGerm
tests.statement: For A = colim_n ℚ_p⟨T/p^n⟩, the functions on the overconvergent neighbourhood of 0, the element T lies in A_{≤p^{-n}} for all n, hence in Nil†(A), although T is not nilpotent; the †-nilradical is not the nilradical.

tests.name: topNilpotent_vs_lessOne
tests.statement: For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧[1/p] the element T is topologically nilpotent but lies in no A_{≤r} with r < 1 (ABLB Remark 2.2.9(2)), so A_{<1} is strictly smaller than the topologically nilpotent elements.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.uniformCompletion
targets.statement: For a bounded solid ℚ_p-algebra A define its uniform completion A^u = (lim_r A_{≤1}/A_{≤r})[1/p] = (A_{≤1})^∧_p[1/p], with the analytic ring structure induced from A (ABLB Definition 2.3.1, p. 20, ABLB line 1037). Prove: A^u is bounded and static; A_{≤1} → A^u_{≤1} over A → A^u is a pullback square (and likewise for A_{≤r}, A_{<1}); the map A^{†-red} → A^u is injective and (A^{†-red})^u = A^u; (A^u)^u = A^u and Nil†(A^u) = 0; an element f ∈ A is invertible if and only if its image in A^u is (ABLB Proposition 2.3.6, p. 21, ABLB line 1080). The inclusion of uniform bounded algebras has left adjoint A ↦ A^u, which commutes with colimits (ABLB Corollary 2.3.7, p. 22, ABLB line 1143).
hypotheses: A is a bounded solid ℚ_p-algebra

locator.where: Definition 2.3.1, Proposition 2.3.6 and Corollary 2.3.7, p. 20; ABLB line 1037

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.uniformCompletion_universal
api.statement: Every map from A to a uniform bounded algebra B factors uniquely through A → A^u.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.uniformCompletion_daggerRed
api.statement: A^u depends only on A^{†-red}: the map A → A^u factors through A^{†-red} and induces (A^{†-red})^u ≅ A^u.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.isUnit_iff_uniform
api.statement: f ∈ A(*) is a unit if and only if its image in A^u(*) is a unit.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.uniformCompletion_huber
api.statement: For a Banach ℚ_p-algebra B with induced structure, B^u is the uniformization of B in the sense of AdicSpacesPartII §R0.4 (the completion for the spectral seminorm).

tests.name: uniform_Tate
tests.statement: ℚ_p⟨T⟩^u = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, since ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is p-adically complete and A_{≤0} = 0.

tests.name: uniform_dualNumbers
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p[ε]/ε², A^u = ℚ_p; the unit 1 + ε maps to the unit 1 and the non-unit ε maps to 0, as the unit criterion requires.

tests.name: uniform_overconvergent
tests.statement: For the overconvergent algebra A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1} = colim_{r>1} ℚ_p⟨T/r⟩ one has Nil†(A) = 0 and A^u = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, so A^{†-red} → A^u is injective but not surjective; A is †-reduced and not uniform.

tests.name: uniform_zero
tests.statement: The zero ring has zero uniform completion, and A^u = 0 forces A = 0 by the unit criterion applied to 0.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsGelfand
targets.statement: Call a bounded solid ℚ_p-algebra A a Gelfand ring if A/A_{≤1} is a discrete condensed set (ABLB Definition 3.1.1, p. 23, ABLB line 1162). Prove that A is Gelfand if and only if A^u is a Banach ℚ_p-algebra, and that Gelfand rings are closed under colimits in bounded algebras (ABLB Proposition 3.1.4, p. 23, ABLB line 1176). Call A separable if A^u is a separable Banach algebra (ABLB Definition 4.2.6(1), p. 42, ABLB line 2190) and quasi-finite-dimensional (qfd) if moreover A^u is qfd, that is, Marc(A^u) → Marc(ℚ_p) is quasi-pro-étale over a relative affine space (ABLB Definition 4.1.11, p. 39, ABLB line 2061; ABLB Definition 4.2.14(1), p. 43, ABLB line 2261).
hypotheses: A is a bounded solid ℚ_p-algebra

locator.where: Definition 3.1.1 and Proposition 3.1.4, p. 23; ABLB line 1162

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.isGelfand_iff_banach
api.statement: A is Gelfand if and only if A^{†-red} is Gelfand if and only if A^u is a Banach ℚ_p-algebra.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsGelfand.colimit
api.statement: Pushouts, finite products and filtered colimits of Gelfand rings computed in bounded algebras are Gelfand; separable Gelfand rings are closed under pushouts and finite products.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsGelfand.ofBanach
api.statement: Every Banach ℚ_p-algebra B with its induced analytic ring structure is a Gelfand ring; Nil†(B) consists of the elements of spectral seminorm zero, so B is †-reduced exactly when its spectral seminorm is a norm.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.qfd_baseChange
api.statement: The qfd condition is stable under pushouts along maps of qfd separable Gelfand rings and under finite products.

tests.name: gelfand_examples
tests.statement: ℚ_p⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩, its overconvergent version ℚ_p⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩_{≤1}, ℚ_p[ε]/ε² and the completed algebraic closure C_p are separable qfd Gelfand rings.

tests.name: notGelfand_freeMeasures
tests.statement: For an infinite light profinite set S, A = ℚ_{p,■}⟨ℕ[S]⟩_{≤1} is bounded but not Gelfand: A_{≤1}/A_{≤1/p} contains 𝔽_{p,■}[S] as a direct summand, which is not discrete (ABLB Example 3.1.3).

tests.name: notQfd_infiniteVariables
tests.statement: The separable Gelfand ring ℚ_p⟨T_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ is not qfd: its spectrum contains the Hilbert cube [0,1]^ℕ through the Gauss points of prescribed radii |T_n| = r_n, so it has infinite covering dimension, whereas a qfd ring is quasi-pro-étale over a finite-dimensional polydisc and its spectrum has finite covering dimension.

tests.name: gelfand_zero
tests.statement: The zero ring is a separable qfd Gelfand ring.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichSpectrum
targets.statement: For a Banach ℚ_p-algebra B let M(B) be the set of continuous multiplicative seminorms |·| on B with |p| = p^{-1}, with the topology of pointwise convergence; for a Gelfand ring A put M(A) := M(A^u) (ABLB Definition 3.1.5, p. 23, ABLB line 1189). For f_1,…,f_n, g ∈ A generating the unit ideal define the rational subspace M(A)(f/g) = {|f_i| ≤ |g| ≠ 0}, a closed subset. For x ∈ M(A) define the stalk A_x as the colimit of the rational localizations containing x and the Berkovich residue field κ(x) = (A_x)^u, the completed residue field of A^u at x (ABLB Definition 3.1.15, p. 26, ABLB line 1335). Prove that M(A) is compact Hausdorff, metrizable when A is separable (ABLB Remark 3.1.6), nonempty when A ≠ 0, functorial (ABLB Lemma 3.1.8) and that M(colim A_i) = lim M(A_i) for filtered colimits (ABLB Lemma 3.1.12). Prove that M(A) is the Berkovich spectrum `Spectrum` of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic §0.1 and the Gel'fand spectrum `Huber.GelfandSpectrum` of AdicSpacesPartIII §R3.9 of the Banach ring A^u with its gauge norm.
hypotheses: A is a Gelfand ring

locator.where: Definitions 3.1.5 and 3.1.15, p. 23; ABLB line 1189

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichSpectrum_map
api.statement: A map A → B of Gelfand rings induces a continuous map M(B) → M(A), functorially.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichSpectrum_eq_empty
api.statement: M(A) = ∅ if and only if A = 0.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichSpectrum_colim
api.statement: For a filtered colimit A = colim A_i of Gelfand rings, M(A) → lim M(A_i) is a homeomorphism.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichSpectrum_eq_tropical
api.statement: M(A) equals TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic `Spectrum` and AdicSpacesPartIII `Huber.GelfandSpectrum` of A^u, compatibly with evaluation and with induced maps.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.residueField_isField
api.statement: κ(x) is a complete nonarchimedean field extension of ℚ_p, equal to the completed residue field of A^u at x (TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic §0.15).

tests.name: spectrum_point
tests.statement: M(ℚ_p) is a point and M(ℚ_p × ℚ_p) is two points; M(0) = ∅.

tests.name: spectrum_disc
tests.statement: M(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) contains the Gauss point with |T| = 1 and the rigid point T = 0 with |T| = 0; the Gauss point is not a maximal ideal, so M is not the maximal spectrum.

tests.name: spectrum_thickening
tests.statement: M(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²) = M(ℚ_p) and M(ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1}) = M(ℚ_p⟨T⟩): the spectrum sees only the uniform completion.

tests.name: spectrum_trivialNorm
tests.statement: The trivial absolute value on ℚ_p is not a point, since points satisfy |p| = p^{-1}.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.daggerRationalLocalization
targets.statement: For a Gelfand ring A and f_1,…,f_n, g ∈ A(*) generating the unit ideal define the †-rational localization A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1} = A⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩_{≤1}/L(gT_i − f_i), where A⟨T⟩_{≤1} = A ⊗_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1} and L denotes the derived quotient, and the Tate-rational localization A⟨f/g⟩ = A⟨T⟩/L(gT_i − f_i) with A⟨T⟩ = A ⊗_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨T⟩ (ALRS Notations and conventions, p. 11, ALRS line 590). Prove that A → A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1} is an idempotent morphism of Gelfand rings, that a map A → B factors through it if and only if M(B) → M(A) lands in M(A)(f/g), and that M(A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1}) → M(A) is a homeomorphism onto M(A)(f/g) identifying rational subspaces (ABLB Proposition 3.1.9, p. 24, ABLB line 1260). Define Berkovich-étale maps of Gelfand rings as maps which locally for strict closed covers are composites of †-rational localizations and finite étale maps (ABLB Definition 3.2.8, p. 32, ABLB line 1658), and prove that Berkovich-étale maps of A, A^{†-red} and A^u correspond (ABLB Proposition 3.2.11, p. 33, ABLB line 1712).
hypotheses: A is a Gelfand ring
f_1,…,f_n, g ∈ A(*) generate the unit ideal

locator.where: Proposition 3.1.9, Definition 3.2.8, Proposition 3.2.11, p. 24; ABLB line 1260

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.daggerRationalLocalization_universal
api.statement: A map A → B factors (uniquely) through A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1} if and only if the image of M(B) → M(A) lies in M(A)(f/g).

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.daggerRationalLocalization_spectrum
api.statement: M(A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1}) → M(A) is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset M(A)(f/g).

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.berkovichEtale_uniform
api.statement: Base change along A → A^u induces an equivalence between Berkovich-étale A-algebras and Berkovich-étale A^u-algebras.

tests.name: localization_wholeDisc
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, the †-rational localization at {|T| ≤ 1} is A itself, because T already lies in A_{≤1}.

tests.name: localization_smallDisc
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and the locus {|T| ≤ |p|}, the localization is colim_{r>1/p} ℚ_p⟨T/r⟩, whose spectrum is the closed disc of radius p^{-1}, a closed and not open subset.

tests.name: localization_empty
tests.statement: For f = 1, g = p·1 on A = ℚ_p the locus {|1| ≤ |p|} is empty and the localization is the zero ring.

tests.name: tate_vs_dagger
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and the locus {|T| ≤ |p|} the Tate-rational localization is ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩, which differs from the †-rational one; both have the same spectrum.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.isFredholm
targets.statement: Prove that every Banach ℚ_p-algebra B with the analytic ring structure induced from ℚ_{p,■} is Fredholm, and that a bounded affinoid ℚ_p-algebra whose uniform completion is Fredholm is Fredholm; hence every Gelfand ring A is Fredholm: every dualizable object of D(A) is discrete, that is, it lies in the image of the fully faithful embedding of perfect complexes over the abstract ring A(*) (ABLB Definition 3.3.1, p. 33, ABLB line 1724; ABLB Proposition 3.3.5, p. 35, ABLB line 1828, whose proof takes the Banach case from And21 Theorem 5.50, p. 39, And21 line 2733, stated there for (B, B⁺)_■ with (B, B⁺) a sheafy Huber pair).
hypotheses: B is a Banach ℚ_p-algebra with the analytic ring structure induced from ℚ_{p,■}
A is a Gelfand ring

locator.where: Proposition 3.3.5, p. 35; ABLB line 1828

tests.name: fredholm_Qp
tests.statement: Over A = ℚ_p the dualizable objects are the bounded complexes of finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces.

tests.name: fredholm_product
tests.statement: Over A = ℚ_p × ℚ_p a dualizable object is a pair of finite-dimensional complexes; its ranks at the two points of M(A) may differ, so Fredholm does not force constant rank.

tests.name: fredholm_notDualizable
tests.statement: The solid ℚ_p-vector space ℚ_p⟨T⟩ is not dualizable over ℚ_p, consistent with the Fredholm property since it is not a perfect ℚ_p-complex.

tests.name: fredholm_twoStructures
tests.statement: On the Banach algebra ℚ_p⟨T⟩ the structure induced from ℚ_{p,■} and (ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩)_■ are different analytic rings, T being solid only in the second (AnalyticStacks §3.6); both are Fredholm, the first by this target and the second by AnalyticStacks §4.4(6), and only the first is the structure the uniform completion of a Gelfand ring carries, so the Huber-pair case alone does not give 1.7.

tests.name: fredholm_dualNumbers
tests.statement: Over the non-uniform Banach algebra B = ℚ_p[ε]/ε² the residue field ℚ_p = B/ε is not dualizable, its minimal free resolution being infinite; a notion of Fredholm asking only that dualizable objects have finite-dimensional fibres at the points of M(B) would wrongly allow it, while perfectness excludes it.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsNilperfectoid
targets.statement: Call a Gelfand ring A totally disconnected if M(A) is profinite, strictly totally disconnected if moreover every Berkovich residue field κ(x) is algebraically closed, nilperfectoid if A^{†-red} → A^u is an isomorphism and A^u is perfectoid, and uniformly perfectoid if A^u is perfectoid (ALRS Definition 2.1.5, p. 15, ALRS line 785; ALRS Proposition 3.4.7, p. 48, ALRS line 2501). Prove that a strictly totally disconnected Gelfand ring with A^{†-red} = A^u is nilperfectoid (ALRS Remark 2.1.6, p. 15, ALRS line 793), via the statement that a Gelfand ring with profinite spectrum and perfectoid residue fields has perfectoid uniform completion (ABLB Lemma 3.1.17, p. 27, ABLB line 1428).
hypotheses: A is a separable Gelfand ring

locator.where: Definition 2.1.5 and Remark 2.1.6, p. 15; ALRS line 785

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.nilperfectoid_iff
api.statement: A is nilperfectoid if and only if Nil†(A) → A → A^u is a fibre sequence and A^u is a perfectoid Banach ℚ_p-algebra.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.IsNilperfectoid.uniformlyPerfectoid
api.statement: Nilperfectoid rings are uniformly perfectoid; perfectoid Banach ℚ_p-algebras are nilperfectoid.

api.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.strictTD_basis
api.statement: Among Banach ℚ_p-algebras, the strictly totally disconnected Banach rings of MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII §BM.0 (strict-basis) are exactly the uniform strictly totally disconnected Gelfand rings.

tests.name: nilperfectoid_Cp
tests.statement: C_p and C(S, C_p) for a light profinite S are nilperfectoid; the latter is strictly totally disconnected with M = S.

tests.name: nilperfectoid_thickening
tests.statement: C_p[ε]/ε² is nilperfectoid: its †-reduction C_p equals its uniform completion.

tests.name: notNilperfectoid_cyclotomic
tests.statement: The uncompleted cyclotomic field ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is uniformly perfectoid but not nilperfectoid, because its †-reduction is itself and differs from its completion.

tests.name: notNilperfectoid_Qp
tests.statement: ℚ_p is totally disconnected (M is a point) but not nilperfectoid, since ℚ_p is not perfectoid.

layers.title: Gelfand stacks, perfect complexes and derived Berkovich spaces

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack
targets.statement: Let GelfRing_{ω₁} be (an essentially small model of) the category of separable Gelfand rings, stable under pushouts and finite products. Define the ∞-category of Gelfand stacks GelfStk = AnStk(GelfRing_{ω₁}^op), the full subcategory of presheaves of anima on affinoid Gelfand stacks GSpec(A) which invert countably presented !-equivalences, where a map is a !-equivalence when every base change of every iterated diagonal induces an equivalence on !-categories D^! (ABLB Definition 4.2.1, p. 40, ABLB line 2109; ABLB Definition 4.2.6, p. 42, ABLB line 2189). Define qfd Gelfand stacks GelfStk^qfd likewise on separable qfd Gelfand rings (ABLB Definition 4.2.14, p. 43, ABLB line 2261). Construct the morphisms of ∞-topoi AnStk → GelfStk → GelfStk^qfd, whose left adjoints preserve finite limits and colimits; the right adjoint of the first, the Gelfandification (−)^Gelf, sends an analytic stack X to A ↦ X(AnSpec(A)) (ABLB Lemma 4.2.7, p. 42, ABLB line 2198; ALRS §2.1, p. 13, ALRS line 662). From §2.4 of ALRS onwards, and from Layer 3 of this roadmap onwards, every Gelfand ring, Gelfand stack and arc-stack is separable and qfd.
hypotheses: separable Gelfand rings carry the analytic ring structure induced from ℚ_{p,■}

locator.where: Definitions 4.2.1, 4.2.6, 4.2.14 and Lemma 4.2.7, p. 42; ABLB line 2189

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.gspec
api.statement: A separable Gelfand ring A defines the representable Gelfand stack GSpec(A), and A ↦ GSpec(A) is fully faithful on separable Gelfand rings (the site is subcanonical).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.descendable_isCover
api.statement: A descendable map A → B of separable Gelfand rings induces an epimorphism GSpec(B) → GSpec(A) of Gelfand stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.gelfandification
api.statement: The functor (−)^An: GelfStk → AnStk is left exact and colimit-preserving with right adjoint (−)^Gelf, and (−)^An is fully faithful on affinoid Gelfand stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.isTopos
api.statement: GelfStk and GelfStk^qfd are ∞-topoi, and the restriction GelfStk → GelfStk^qfd is the inverse image of a geometric morphism.

tests.name: gspec_terminal
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p) is the final Gelfand stack and GSpec(0) is the initial one; any sheaf takes value a point on GSpec(0).

tests.name: gspec_product
tests.statement: GSpec(A × B) = GSpec(A) ⊔ GSpec(B) for separable Gelfand rings A, B, because D(A × B) = D(A) × D(B).

tests.name: gelfandification_notFF
tests.statement: The !-cover ℚ_p → ℤ_p((x))^∧_p[1/p] of analytic rings is not refined by a !-cover from Gelfand rings, which is why (−)^An is not claimed fully faithful on all Gelfand stacks (ABLB footnote 28).

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.sixFunctors
targets.statement: Pull back the quasi-coherent six-functor formalism D(−) of analytic stacks over AnSpec(ℚ_{p,■}) along (−)^An to a six-functor formalism on Gelfand stacks, and call its class of !-able maps E₂ (ABLB Remark 4.2.8, p. 42, ABLB line 2209). Enlarge it as in ALRS Construction 2.1.2 (p. 14, ALRS line 704): every map of affinoid Gelfand stacks is !-able with f_! = f_*, so transmutation gives a conservative morphism of ∞-topoi Gest((−)_D): GelfStk → Gest/Gest(D(ℚ_p)), and a map of Gelfand stacks is called n-affine, n-prim or n-proper when its image is. The 0-proper maps contain all maps of affinoid Gelfand stacks, are stable under composition and base change and satisfy left cancellation, and pullback along them has a linear right adjoint satisfying base change, so D is a 3-functor formalism on Corr(GelfStk, 0-proper) (HM Proposition 3.3.3, p. 37, HM line 1924) and extends uniquely to a six-functor formalism on Corr(GelfStk, E₁) for the minimal class E₁ of HM Theorem 3.4.11 and Lemma 3.4.13; these are the six functors of this roadmap. Prove that every 0-proper map f is prim with a natural trivialization δ_f ≅ 1 of its codualizing complex, so f_! ≅ f_* (ALRS Remark 2.1.4, p. 15, ALRS line 780). Prove the comparison with E₂: the class E₀ generated by the maps of affinoid Gelfand stacks under HM Theorem 3.4.11 lies in E₁ ∩ E₂, the two formalisms agree on Corr(GelfStk, E₀), and a map in E₀ that is suave, prim, cohomologically proper or cohomologically étale for E₂ has the same property for E₁; E₀ contains every map of Betti stacks coming from a ℚ-fine map of condensed anima, every map of derived Berkovich spaces with finite-dimensional underlying space, and the de Rham stacks of arc-locally lqfd maps of qfd arc-stacks (ALRS Remark 2.1.3, p. 15, ALRS line 751). Define suave, prim, cohomologically smooth (D-smooth), cohomologically proper (D-proper) and cohomologically étale maps by HM Definitions 4.5.1 and 4.6.1 for E₁.
hypotheses: the six-functor formalism on analytic stacks of the contract `qcoh-six-functors`, enlarged through the Gestalten of the contracts `gestalten-transmutation` and `gestalten-affine-proper`

locator.where: Remark 4.2.8, p. 42; ABLB line 2209

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.lowerShriek_affinoid
api.statement: For a map f: GSpec(B) → GSpec(A) of affinoid Gelfand stacks, f is 0-affine and 0-proper and f_! ≅ f_* is the forgetful functor D(B) → D(A).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.baseChange
api.statement: For a cartesian square of Gelfand stacks with f !-able, g^* f_! ≅ f′_! g′^*, and the projection formula f_!(M ⊗ f^*N) ≅ f_!M ⊗ N holds.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.zeroProper_stable
api.statement: 0-affine and 0-proper maps are stable under composition and base change, 0-affine maps also under diagonals and retracts; for maps Z → Y → X with Y → X 0-proper, Z → Y is 0-proper if and only if Z → X is; and both properties are local on the target for !-covers (Gest Propositions 6.6, 6.13 and 7.9).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.zeroProper_prim
api.statement: A 0-proper map f is !-able and prim with δ_f ≅ 1, so f_! ≅ f_*; if f is moreover truncated, it is D-proper. 0-properness can be checked along a !-cover of the source that is cohomologically proper and 0-proper (HM Remark 4.4.11(iii), whose argument applies to 0-proper maps, ALRS footnote 58, p. 165, ALRS line 8962).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.proper_local
api.statement: D-properness and D-smoothness of a truncated map are local on the target for !-covers, and D-properness can be checked on a universal D-proper !-cover of the source (HM Lemma 4.6.3).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.proper_iff
api.statement: If the diagonal of f is D-proper, then f is D-proper if and only if the natural map f_! → f_* is an equivalence (HM Lemma 4.6.4(ii)).

tests.name: proper_closedDisc
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → GSpec(ℚ_p) is 0-affine, hence 0-proper, with f_! = f_* the forgetful functor; its global sections of O are ℚ_p⟨T⟩.

tests.name: smooth_openDisc
tests.statement: The open unit disc over ℚ_p is cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex Ω¹[1] but is not 0-proper: f_!O is compactly supported cohomology, concentrated in cohomological degree 1 for this one-dimensional Stein space, while f_*O is its ring of functions in degree 0, so f_! ≇ f_*. The closed disc GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) is 0-proper and is neither Berkovich-smooth nor rigid smooth (ALRS Warning 2.6.13): properness and smoothness separate the two discs.

tests.name: proper_identity
tests.statement: The identity of any Gelfand stack is 0-affine, 0-proper, D-proper, D-smooth and D-étale with trivial dualizing and codualizing complexes.

tests.name: compare_affinoid
tests.statement: For a map f: GSpec(B) → GSpec(A) of affinoid Gelfand stacks, which lies in E₀, the lower-shriek functors of E₁ and of E₂ are both the forgetful functor D(B) → D(A), as the comparison requires; a comparison that also identified the two !-able classes would be stronger than what ALRS Remark 2.1.3 proves, which is E₀ ⊂ E₁ ∩ E₂.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.perf_eq_dualizable
targets.statement: Since every Gelfand ring is Fredholm (1.7), AnalyticStacks §4.5 applied to C₀ = GelfRing_{ω₁}^op gives, for integers a ≤ b, the sheaf of categories Perf^{[a,b]}(−) on GelfStk extending A ↦ Perf^{[a,b]}(A) and inverting !-equivalences, a module being perfect of amplitude [a, b] when its pullback to every affinoid is (ABLB Lemma 4.2.11 and Definition 4.2.12, p. 43, ABLB line 2235, ABLB line 2253, stated there for Gelfand rings). Prove that for every Gelfand stack X the category Perf(X) ⊂ D(X) is exactly the full subcategory of dualizable objects (ALRS §2.1, p. 16, ALRS line 809). Prove that locally eventually connective modules D^+(−) and nuclear modules Nuc(D(−)) form sheaves of categories on GelfStk (ALRS Lemma 2.1.8, p. 16, ALRS line 820; ALRS Lemma 2.1.10, p. 17, ALRS line 861), and prove the criterion used for D^+ and Nuc: a sheaf of categories on an ∞-topos descends to a cotopological localization if and only if it is fully faithful along the localizing maps (ALRS Lemma 2.1.9, p. 16, ALRS line 841).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack
a ≤ b are integers

locator.where: §2.1 and Lemmas 2.1.8–2.1.10, pp. 16–17; ALRS line 809

tests.name: perf_point
tests.statement: Perf(GSpec(ℚ_p)) is the category of bounded complexes of finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces, and Perf(∅) = 0.

tests.name: perf_descent
tests.statement: For the descendable map ℚ_p → ℚ_p^cyc (it has a ℚ_p-linear retraction), a perfect ℚ_p^cyc-complex with descent datum for the Čech conerve descends to a perfect ℚ_p-complex of the same amplitude.

tests.name: perf_notAll
tests.statement: The object ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ∈ D(GSpec(ℚ_p)) is eventually connective and nuclear but not dualizable, so the three sheaves of categories are distinct.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.nilperfectoid_basis
targets.statement: Prove: (1) every separable Gelfand ring A admits a descendable map A → A′ with A′ separable nilperfectoid, quasi-pro-étale after uniform completion; (2) every separable qfd Gelfand ring admits a descendable map to a separable qfd strictly totally disconnected nilperfectoid ring; (3) for an arc-hypercover A → A^• of qfd perfectoid rings, colim_Δ GSpec(A^•) → GSpec(A) is a !-equivalence (ALRS Theorem 2.1.7, p. 15, ALRS line 797; ABLB Proposition 4.6.4, p. 55, ABLB line 2916; ABLB Corollary 4.4.10, p. 50, ABLB line 2641).
hypotheses: A is a separable Gelfand ring; in (2) and (3) everything is qfd

locator.where: Theorem 2.1.7, p. 15; ALRS line 797

tests.name: basis_Qp
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p the map ℚ_p → ℚ_p^cyc is descendable and lands in a nilperfectoid ring.

tests.name: basis_identity
tests.statement: A nilperfectoid ring is its own cover; for A = 0 the empty family covers.

tests.name: basis_notTD
tests.statement: ℚ_p is totally disconnected but not strictly totally disconnected, since its residue field ℚ_p is not algebraically closed; (2) requires passing to C_p-type covers.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.betti
targets.statement: Construct the colimit-preserving Betti realization (−)^Betti: CondAni → GelfStk^qfd, left adjoint in a morphism of ∞-topoi, sending a light profinite set S to GSpec(C^lc(S, ℚ_p)), the spectrum of the solid ℚ_p-algebra of locally constant functions (ABLB Lemma 4.2.9, p. 42, ABLB line 2214; ALRS §2.1, p. 13, ALRS line 671). For a qfd Gelfand ring A construct the natural map GSpec(A) → M(A)^Betti, and for a qfd derived Berkovich space X the map X → |X|^Betti (ALRS §2.2, p. 18, ALRS line 925).
hypotheses: S is a light profinite set; A is a qfd separable Gelfand ring

locator.where: Lemma 4.2.9, p. 42; ABLB line 2214

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.betti_profinite
api.statement: For a light profinite S, S^Betti = GSpec(C^lc(S, ℚ_p)).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.betti_exact
api.statement: (−)^Betti preserves colimits and finite limits.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.toBetti
api.statement: For a qfd Gelfand ring A there is a natural map GSpec(A) → M(A)^Betti, compatible with rational localizations, which on the open subset U ⊂ M(A) recovers the open subspace GSpec(A)_U.

tests.name: betti_finite
tests.statement: The Betti realization of a two-point set is GSpec(ℚ_p × ℚ_p) and that of the empty set is GSpec(0).

tests.name: betti_notContinuous
tests.statement: For S = ℕ ∪ {∞}, C^lc(S, ℚ_p) consists of eventually constant sequences and is not the Banach algebra C(S, ℚ_p) of convergent sequences; GSpec(C(S, ℚ_p)) is the continuous incarnation S^cont, distinct from S^Betti.

tests.name: betti_point
tests.statement: The point realizes to GSpec(ℚ_p), the final Gelfand stack.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace
targets.statement: Define the analytic topology on affinoid Gelfand stacks: a cover of GSpec(A) is a finite family of †-rational localizations whose spectra form a strict closed cover of M(A), that is, one refined by an open cover. A derived Berkovich space is a sheaf for this topology admitting an open cover by open subspaces of affinoid Gelfand stacks; it has an underlying topological space |X| = colim |GSpec(A)| (ABLB Definition 4.3.1, p. 44, ABLB line 2295; ALRS §2.2, p. 17, ALRS line 894). Prove that the left Kan extension BerkSp → GelfStk is fully faithful (ABLB Proposition 4.3.3, p. 44, ABLB line 2330). A †-rigid space over a separable nonarchimedean field K is a derived Berkovich space locally represented by a static quotient of an overconvergent Tate algebra K⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩_{≤r} (ABLB Definition 4.3.6, p. 45, ABLB line 2384). For a rigid space X over a qfd Banach field define X′ = colim GSpec(A) over open affinoids Spa(A, A^+) ⊂ X; prove that X ↦ X′ sends rational covers to epimorphisms, depends only on the canonical compactification of X, and its restriction to partially proper rigid spaces is a fully faithful embedding into derived Berkovich spaces, with Spa(A, A^+) ↦ GSpec(A) on affinoids (ALRS Example 2.2.2, p. 17, ALRS line 910).
hypotheses: K is a separable nonarchimedean field over ℚ_p for †-rigid spaces; rigid spaces are over a qfd Banach field

locator.where: Definitions 4.3.1, 4.3.6 and Proposition 4.3.3; ALRS Example 2.2.2, p. 44; ABLB line 2295

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace.underlying
api.statement: Every derived Berkovich space X has a topological space |X|, with |GSpec(A)| = M(A), functorial in maps.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace.openImmersion
api.statement: Open subsets U ⊂ |X| define open subspaces X_U → X, and these are exactly the open immersions.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace.toGelfand_ff
api.statement: BerkSp → GelfStk and BerkSp^qfd → GelfStk^qfd are fully faithful.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace.ofPartiallyProper
api.statement: Partially proper rigid spaces over K embed fully faithfully into derived Berkovich spaces, and dagger spaces in the sense of AdicSpacesPartIV §F1.7 give †-rigid spaces.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.BerkovichSpace.compareTropical
api.statement: For a K-affinoid algebra A in the sense of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic §0.17, |GSpec(A)| is its Berkovich spectrum, and affinoid and rational domains (§0.19) correspond to †-rational localizations with the same spectra.

tests.name: berk_openDisc
tests.statement: The open unit disc is a partially proper rigid space whose derived Berkovich space has |X| the open Berkovich disc.

tests.name: berk_compactification
tests.statement: The rigid closed disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and its canonical compactification have the same Gelfand stack GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), so X ↦ X′ is not injective on rigid spaces that are not partially proper.

tests.name: berk_overconvergent
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1}) and GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) have the same underlying space and different Gelfand stacks: the first is a †-rigid space and is Berkovich-smooth, the second is the canonical compactification of the closed disc and is not Berkovich-smooth (ALRS Warning 2.6.13).

tests.name: berk_empty
tests.statement: The empty sheaf is a derived Berkovich space with empty underlying space.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.relativeSpec
targets.statement: For a qfd Gelfand stack X and A ∈ CAlg(D(X)) define GSpec_X(A) as the functor on Gelfand rings f: GSpec(R) → X with value Map_{CAlg(D(R))}(f^*A, R) (ALRS Definition 2.2.3, p. 18, ALRS line 937). Prove that it is a qfd Gelfand stack, compatible with base change, that GSpec_X(f_*O_Y) = Y for a map f: Y → X of affinoid Gelfand stacks, and define the relative affinization and Toën-affine maps (prim maps for which Y → GSpec_X(f_*O_Y) is an equivalence), a property local on the target (ALRS Remark 2.2.4, p. 18, ALRS line 941). Prove that for a qfd derived Berkovich space X the map h: X → |X|^Betti is Toën-affine and 0-affine, in particular 0-proper, so that X = GSpec_{|X|^Betti}(h_*O_X) (ALRS Lemma 2.2.5, p. 18, ALRS line 964).
hypotheses: X is a qfd Gelfand stack; in the last statement X is a qfd derived Berkovich space

locator.where: Definition 2.2.3, Remark 2.2.4, Lemma 2.2.5, p. 18; ALRS line 937

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.relativeSpec_baseChange
api.statement: For g: Y → X, Y ×_X GSpec_X(A) ≅ GSpec_Y(g^*A).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.relativeSpec_affinoid
api.statement: For f: GSpec(B) → GSpec(A), GSpec_{GSpec(A)}(f_*O) = GSpec(B).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.toenAffine_local
api.statement: Toën-affineness is local on the target for epimorphisms of Gelfand stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.betti_toenAffine
api.statement: For a qfd derived Berkovich space X, h: X → |X|^Betti is Toën-affine and 0-affine (hence 0-proper), and h_*O_X is the sheaf U ↦ O(X_U) on |X|.

tests.name: relSpec_affinoid
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), h_*O is the sheaf on the Berkovich disc assigning to a †-rational closed subset its overconvergent function ring, and GSpec_{|X|}(h_*O) recovers X.

tests.name: relSpec_empty
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p[u^{±1}] with u of homological degree 2, GSpec_X(A) = ∅ although A ≠ 0, because a homogeneous unit of positive degree cannot map to a connective ring (ALRS Remark 2.2.4(4)).

tests.name: relSpec_unit
tests.statement: GSpec_X(O_X) = X for every qfd Gelfand stack X.

targets.name: TauCeti.ArcStack.perfectoidization
targets.statement: Define the ∞-category ArcStk_{ℚ_p} of light arc-stacks over Marc(ℚ_p) as hypersheaves of anima on the arc-site of separable perfectoid spaces over ℚ_p, and its qfd variant on separable qfd perfectoid spaces (ABLB Definition 4.1.8, p. 39, ABLB line 2023; ABLB Definition 4.1.11(3), p. 39, ABLB line 2067). For a separable Banach algebra A let Marc(A) be the arc-sheaf of pairs (R^♯, A → R^♯) of an untilt and a map of Banach algebras; tilting identifies ArcStk_{ℚ_p} with arc-stacks over Marc(ℚ_p) on perfectoid spaces of characteristic p (ALRS §2.3, p. 19, ALRS line 996). Construct the perfectoidization functor (−)^⋄: GelfStk → ArcStk_{ℚ_p} by restriction along totally disconnected perfectoid affinoids, colimit-preserving, with GSpec(A)^⋄ = Marc(A^u), and its left adjoint X ↦ X̂ which preserves fibre products but not the final object (ABLB Proposition 4.5.4, p. 51, ABLB line 2729; ABLB Proposition 4.5.5, p. 52, ABLB line 2737; ALRS §2.3, p. 19, ALRS line 1005). Compare Marc(A) with the Banach arc-site of MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII §BM.0.
hypotheses: separable perfectoid spaces over ℚ_p with the arc-topology (surjections on Berkovich spectra)

locator.where: Definition 4.1.8, Propositions 4.5.4–4.5.5, p. 39; ABLB line 2023

api.name: TauCeti.ArcStack.marc_uniform
api.statement: GSpec(A)^⋄ = Marc(A) = Marc(A^u) for every separable Gelfand ring A.

api.name: TauCeti.ArcStack.perfectoidization_colim
api.statement: (−)^⋄ preserves colimits and finite limits, and is itself the inverse image of a geometric morphism of ∞-topoi (ALRS §2.3, ALRS line 1016).

api.name: TauCeti.ArcStack.hat_perfectoid
api.statement: For a qfd nilperfectoid A, the left adjoint sends Marc(A^u) to GSpec(A^u).

api.name: TauCeti.ArcStack.compareBM0
api.statement: For a separable Banach ℚ_p-algebra A, Marc(A) agrees on separable perfectoid spaces with the arc-sheafified representable of MotivesAndAlgebraicCyclesPartII §BM.0 arc-site.

tests.name: perfectoidization_thickening
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²)^⋄ = Marc(ℚ_p) = GSpec(ℚ_p)^⋄: perfectoidization forgets †-nilpotent thickenings.

tests.name: perfectoidization_dagger
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1})^⋄ = GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩)^⋄ = Marc(ℚ_p⟨T⟩).

tests.name: hat_notFinal
tests.statement: The left adjoint X ↦ X̂ preserves fibre products but not the final object (ALRS line 1015): the final arc-stack Marc(ℚ_p) is not sent to the final Gelfand stack GSpec(ℚ_p), so X̂ is not the inverse image of a geometric morphism into GelfStk; it is one into the slice of GelfStk over the image of Marc(ℚ_p) (ABLB Proposition 4.5.5, p. 52, ABLB line 2737).

layers.title: Analytic de Rham stacks, analytification and Cartier divisors

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham
targets.statement: Define the analytic de Rham stack (−)^dR: ArcStk^qfd_{ℚ_p} → GelfStk^qfd as the right adjoint of perfectoidization; explicitly, for a qfd nilperfectoid ℚ_p-algebra A, X^dR(A) = X(Marc(A^u)), and for a qfd Gelfand stack X put X^dR = (X^⋄)^dR, so that X^dR(A) = X(A^u) (ALRS Definition 2.3.1, p. 19, ALRS line 1017; ALRS Remark 2.3.2, p. 20, ALRS line 1027). For a map Y → X define the relative de Rham stack Y^{dR/X} = X ×_{X^dR} Y^dR. Prove that for a qfd derived Berkovich space X, X^dR is the !-sheafification of A ↦ X(A^{†-red}), that for a map Z → X of qfd derived Berkovich spaces whose map of arc-stacks is an immersion Z^{dR/X} is the overconvergent neighbourhood X^†_Z, and that for a †-rigid space X over a qfd field K, X → X^{dR/K} is prim and descendable with Čech nerve (X^{×_K (n+1)})^†_Δ (ABLB Proposition 4.7.12, p. 59, ABLB line 3155; ABLB Theorem 4.7.15, p. 61, ABLB line 3248).
hypotheses: X is a qfd arc-stack over ℚ_p or a qfd Gelfand stack

locator.where: Definition 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.2, p. 19; ALRS line 1017

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_adjunction
api.statement: Maps Y → X^dR of qfd Gelfand stacks are equivalent to maps Y^⋄ → X of arc-stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_value
api.statement: For a qfd nilperfectoid A and a qfd Gelfand stack X, X^dR(A) = X(A^u); in particular X^dR(A) depends only on A^u.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_idempotent
api.statement: The unit X → X^dR induces (X^dR)^dR ≅ X^dR, and X^dR → GSpec(ℚ_p) is †-formally étale.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_immersion
api.statement: For an immersion Z → X of qfd derived Berkovich spaces on arc-stacks, Z^{dR/X} = X^†_Z.

tests.name: deRham_affineLine
tests.statement: For A¹, (A¹)^dR(A) = A^u-points = A/Nil†(A) on nilperfectoids, so (A¹)^dR = A¹/G_a^† with G_a^†(A) = Nil†(A) = GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤0})(A) acting by translation (ABLB Theorem 4.7.15).

tests.name: deRham_thickening
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²)^dR = GSpec(ℚ_p)^dR = GSpec(ℚ_p), since both have perfectoidization Marc(ℚ_p).

tests.name: deRham_notIdentity
tests.statement: A¹ → (A¹)^dR is not an isomorphism: over A = C_p[ε]/ε² the points ε and 0 of A¹(A) have the same image.

tests.name: deRham_empty
tests.statement: The empty arc-stack has empty de Rham stack: ∅^dR(A) = ∅(Marc(A^u)) is empty for every nonzero nilperfectoid A.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_colimits
targets.statement: Prove that (−)^dR: ArcStk^qfd_{ℚ_p} → GelfStk^qfd is left exact and commutes with all colimits, hence is the inverse image of a geometric morphism; in particular, for an arc-hypercover X_• → X of qfd arc-stacks, |X^dR_•| → X^dR is an equivalence, and epimorphisms go to epimorphisms (ABLB Theorem 5.6.6, p. 90, ABLB line 4799; ABLB Theorem 5.6.1, p. 87, ABLB line 4629; ABLB Theorem 4.8.7, p. 64, ABLB line 3384). Prove that (−)^dR and the left adjoint of perfectoidization are fully faithful (ABLB Proposition 4.5.7, p. 52, ABLB line 2752).
hypotheses: all arc-stacks and Gelfand stacks are qfd

locator.where: Theorem 5.6.6, p. 90; ABLB line 4799

tests.name: deRham_classifying
tests.statement: For a locally profinite group G with classifying arc-stack BG, (BG)^dR = BG^sm, where G^sm has the locally constant ℚ_p-valued functions (ABLB Remark 1.2.6).

tests.name: deRham_coproduct
tests.statement: The de Rham stack of a disjoint union of two qfd arc-stacks is the disjoint union of their de Rham stacks.

tests.name: deRham_bigVersion
tests.statement: Without the qfd restriction the big de Rham stack satisfies the other assertions but is not known to commute with colimits (ABLB Remark 1.2.6), which is why the qfd setting is imposed.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_sixFunctors
targets.statement: Prove: (1) if a map f: Y → X of qfd arc-stacks over ℚ_p is arc-locally on X locally of quasi-finite dimension (lqfd: strict closed covers by pieces qcqs and quasi-pro-étale over a relative affine space), then f^dR is !-able, and cohomologically proper if f is proper (ABLB Proposition 5.1.4, p. 67, ABLB line 3512); (2) if f is smooth (arc-locally on X and analytically on Y étale over a relative affine space) of pure dimension d, then f^dR is cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex O[2d], and cohomologically étale when f is étale (ABLB Theorem 5.1.7, p. 68, ABLB line 3567); (3) for the open punctured pre-perfectoid unit disc X = lim_{x↦x^p} D̊^{×,⋄}, X^dR → GSpec(ℚ_p) is cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex O[2] (ABLB Proposition 5.7.1, p. 91, ABLB line 4860).
hypotheses: f is a map of qfd arc-stacks over ℚ_p; in (2) f is smooth of pure dimension d

locator.where: Proposition 5.1.4, Theorem 5.1.7, Proposition 5.7.1, p. 67; ABLB line 3512

tests.name: deRham_dualizing_dim
tests.statement: For A^{d,⋄} → Marc(ℚ_p) the dualizing complex is O[2d]; for d = 0 it is O.

tests.name: deRham_noTwist
tests.statement: The dualizing complex of a smooth de Rham stack carries no Frobenius twist; the Tate twist O⟨1⟩[2] of 6.3 appears only after passing to Hyodo–Kato stacks.

tests.name: deRham_notProper
tests.statement: The open disc is smooth and not proper over Marc(ℚ_p), so its de Rham stack is cohomologically smooth but f^dR_! ≠ f^dR_*.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.locallyAnalyticPoints
targets.statement: For a rigid space X over ℚ_p, viewed as a Gelfand stack, define X(ℚ_p)^la := X ×_{X^dR} (X(ℚ_p))^dR, where X(ℚ_p) is the locally profinite set of ℚ_p-points (ALRS Definition 2.3.3, p. 20, ALRS line 1032). When X is a rigid analytic group, X(ℚ_p)^la is a group object in Gelfand stacks; for a p-adic Lie group G define G^cont = GSpec(C(G, ℚ_p)) locally and G^sm with the locally constant functions, so that there are group maps G^cont → G^la → G^sm (ALRS footnote 6, p. 6, ALRS line 326).
hypotheses: X is a rigid space over ℚ_p

locator.where: Definition 2.3.3, p. 20; ALRS line 1032

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.locallyAnalyticPoints_group
api.statement: If X is a rigid analytic group then X(ℚ_p)^la is a group object and X(ℚ_p)^la → X is a group map.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.locallyAnalyticPoints_deRham
api.statement: The de Rham stack of X(ℚ_p)^la is X(ℚ_p)^dR = X(ℚ_p)^sm, the Betti realization of the locally profinite set X(ℚ_p).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.locallyAnalyticPoints_value
api.statement: For a nilperfectoid A, X(ℚ_p)^la(A) is the set of points x ∈ X(A) whose image in X(A^u) comes from a locally constant map M(A) → X(ℚ_p).

tests.name: laPoints_affineLine
tests.statement: A¹(ℚ_p)^la = ℚ_p^la, and ℚ_p^la(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²) = ℚ_p ⊕ ℚ_p·ε while ℚ_p^sm(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²) = ℚ_p; the extra tangent direction distinguishes locally analytic from locally constant.

tests.name: laPoints_thickenedCp
tests.statement: ℚ_p^la(C_p[ε]/ε²) = {a + bε : a ∈ ℚ_p, b ∈ C_p}, because the reduction modulo the †-nilradical must be a constant in ℚ_p.

tests.name: laPoints_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), X(ℚ_p)^la = GSpec(ℚ_p).

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.analytification
targets.statement: For an affinoid Gelfand stack S = GSpec(R) and an affine derived scheme Spec(R′) over Spec(R(*)) define (Spec R′)^an(A) = Map_{R(*)}(R′, A(*)). Prove that this extends uniquely to a colimit-preserving and finite-limit-preserving functor (−)^an from étale sheaves on affine derived schemes over Spec(R(*)) to Gelfand stacks over S, the !-sheafification of A ↦ X(A(*)) (ALRS Lemma 2.4.1, p. 20, ALRS line 1053). Define Tannakian, strongly Tannakian and perfect étale algebraic stacks (ALRS Definition 2.4.2, p. 21, ALRS line 1092). Prove that for a perfect strongly Tannakian X over Spec(R(*)) the presheaf A ↦ X(Spec A(*)) is already a Gelfand stack equal to X^an, and that maps Y → X^an from a Gelfand stack Y over S are the Perf(R)-linear symmetric monoidal functors Perf(X) → Perf(Y) whose extension to QCoh(X) carries connective pseudo-coherent objects to objects that are locally connective (ALRS Proposition 2.4.5, p. 22, ALRS line 1143).
hypotheses: S = GSpec(R) is an affinoid Gelfand stack over ℚ_p; X is an étale algebraic stack over Spec(R(*)); for the Tannakian statement X is perfect and strongly Tannakian

locator.where: Lemma 2.4.1, Definition 2.4.2, Proposition 2.4.5, p. 20; ALRS line 1053

tests.name: an_line
tests.statement: (A^{1,sch})^an = A¹ with A¹(A) = A(*), and (G_m^{sch})^an = G_m with G_m(A) = A(*)^×; A¹ is the increasing union of the discs GSpec(ℚ_p⟨p^n T⟩), not the closed disc GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩).

tests.name: an_BGm
tests.statement: B G_m^{sch} and A^{1,sch}/G_m^{sch} over a field of characteristic zero are perfect and strongly Tannakian (ALRS Example 2.4.4(3)), so their analytifications have the functor-of-points description.

tests.name: an_point
tests.statement: The analytification of Spec(R(*)) is S itself.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cartierDivisor
targets.statement: Prove that for a Gelfand stack X the anima Map(X, BG_m) is equivalent to the anima of line bundles in D(X), the objects that are ∗-locally perfect of amplitude 0 and rank 1 (ALRS Lemma 2.5.2, p. 22, ALRS line 1178), and that Map(X, A¹/G_m) is equivalent to the anima of generalized Cartier divisors (L, s: L → O_X) with L a line bundle; if X is a derived Berkovich space this is also the anima of maps Z → X which are analytically locally the derived zero locus of a function. The correspondences send g: X → A¹/G_m to its pullback along {0}/G_m → A¹/G_m, f: Z → X to L = fib(O_X → f_*O_Z), and (L, s) to the descent of the G_m-equivariant map V(L)^× → A¹ (ALRS Proposition 2.5.3, p. 23, ALRS line 1197). In this roadmap "Cartier divisor" always means generalized Cartier divisor in this sense.
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; for the zero-locus description X is a derived Berkovich space

locator.where: Lemma 2.5.2 and Proposition 2.5.3, p. 22; ALRS line 1178

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.lineBundle_equiv
api.statement: Map(X, BG_m) ≅ line bundles on X, compatibly with pullback and tensor product.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cartierDivisor_equiv
api.statement: Map(X, A¹/G_m) ≅ pairs (L, s: L → O_X), compatibly with pullback; tensor product of pairs corresponds to the multiplication A¹/G_m × A¹/G_m → A¹/G_m.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cartierDivisor_zeroLocus
api.statement: The divisor Z = X ×_{A¹/G_m} BG_m attached to (L, s) has O_Z = cofib(s), and the divisor is empty if and only if s is an isomorphism.

tests.name: cartier_point
tests.statement: Over GSpec(ℚ_p) there are two isomorphism classes of Cartier divisors: s ≠ 0 gives the empty divisor and s = 0 gives the derived zero locus GSpec(ℚ_p ⊕ ℚ_p[1]), which is neither empty nor GSpec(ℚ_p).

tests.name: cartier_disc
tests.statement: On GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), (O, T) has zero locus GSpec(ℚ_p) at the origin; (O, T²) has zero locus GSpec(ℚ_p[T]/T²), and (O, 1) is empty.

tests.name: cartier_universal
tests.statement: The universal Cartier divisor on A¹/G_m has ideal sheaf the line bundle I of weight −1, and its divisor is BG_m = {0}/G_m; this fixes the sign of the G_m-weights used for cones in Layer 5.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.IsDaggerFormallyEtale
targets.statement: Prove that for a map f: Y → X of Gelfand stacks the following are equivalent: (1) Y → Y^{dR/X} is an isomorphism; (2) for every Gelfand ring A, Y(A) → X(A) ×_{X^⋄(Marc(A^{†-red}))} Y^⋄(Marc(A^{†-red})) is an isomorphism; (3) for every nilperfectoid A, Y(A) → X(A) ×_{X(A^u)} Y(A^u) is an isomorphism; call such f †-formally étale (ALRS Lemma 2.6.1, p. 24, ALRS line 1248; ABLB Definition 4.7.2, p. 57, ABLB line 3051). Define f to be †-formally smooth (the map in (3) is an epimorphism for nilperfectoid A), weakly †-formally smooth (Y → Y^{dR/X} is an epimorphism), strongly †-formally smooth (Y(A) → X(A) ×_{X(A^{†-red})} Y(A^{†-red}) is an epimorphism for every Gelfand ring A), and †-formally étale locally †-formally smooth (†-formally smooth after †-formally étale epimorphisms on source and target), with the implications strong ⇒ †-formally smooth ⇒ étale-locally ⇒ weak (ALRS Definition 2.6.4, p. 24, ALRS line 1275). Prove that a weakly †-formally smooth map is an epimorphism if and only if f^⋄ is (ALRS Lemma 2.6.5, p. 24, ALRS line 1293).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of Gelfand stacks

locator.where: Lemma 2.6.1, Definition 2.6.4, Lemma 2.6.5, p. 24; ALRS line 1248

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.daggerEtale_stable
api.statement: †-formally étale maps are stable under base change and composition and satisfy cancellation; †-rational localizations of Berkovich spaces are †-formally étale.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.deRham_relative_etale
api.statement: For every map Y → X, Y^{dR/X} → X is †-formally étale.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.daggerSmooth_implications
api.statement: Strongly †-formally smooth ⇒ †-formally smooth ⇒ †-formally étale locally †-formally smooth ⇒ weakly †-formally smooth.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.weaklySmooth_epi_iff
api.statement: A weakly †-formally smooth map is an epimorphism of Gelfand stacks if and only if its perfectoidization is an epimorphism of arc-stacks.

tests.name: daggerEtale_localization
tests.statement: A †-rational localization GSpec(A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1}) → GSpec(A) is †-formally étale (ABLB Proposition 3.1.9).

tests.name: notDaggerEtale_point
tests.statement: The zero section 0 → A¹ is not †-formally étale: for A = C_p[ε]/ε² the target set X(A) ×_{X(A^u)} Y(A^u) is Nil†(A) = C_p·ε, while Y(A) is a point.

tests.name: notDaggerSmooth_closedDisc
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → GSpec(ℚ_p) has cotangent complex ℚ_p⟨T⟩dT (formally smooth in 4.6) but is not †-formally smooth (ALRS Remark 2.6.6; ABLB Example 4.7.7).

tests.name: daggerEtale_identity
tests.statement: Isomorphisms are †-formally étale.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.IsBerkovichEtale
targets.statement: For a map f: Y → X of Berkovich spaces define: f is an open (closed, locally closed) immersion if |Y| → |X| is one and Y → |Y|^Betti ×_{|X|^Betti} X is an isomorphism, equivalently f is †-formally étale and f^⋄ is an open (closed, locally closed) immersion of arc-stacks (ALRS Definition 2.6.8, p. 25, ALRS line 1321); finite étale maps (ALRS Remark 2.6.7, p. 25, ALRS line 1309); rigid étale maps (analytically locally composites of open immersions and finite étale maps) and rigid smooth maps (analytically locally rigid étale over A^n_X) (ALRS Definition 2.6.10, p. 25, ALRS line 1332); Berkovich-étale maps (locally on strict closed covers composites of †-rational localizations and finite étale maps) and Berkovich-smooth maps (locally Berkovich-étale over A^n_X) (ALRS Definition 2.6.12, p. 25, ALRS line 1344). Prove that rigid smooth maps are analytically locally strongly †-formally smooth (ALRS Lemma 2.6.11, p. 25, ALRS line 1339) and that smooth partially proper rigid spaces over a nonarchimedean field are rigid smooth (ALRS Warning 2.6.13, p. 25, ALRS line 1351).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of derived Berkovich spaces

locator.where: Definitions 2.6.8, 2.6.10, 2.6.12, Lemma 2.6.11, p. 25; ALRS line 1321

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.rigidEtale_isBerkovichEtale
api.statement: Rigid étale maps are Berkovich-étale and rigid smooth maps are Berkovich-smooth; Berkovich-étale maps are †-formally étale.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.openImmersion_local
api.statement: Being an open or closed immersion is local on the target for !-covers, which therefore defines open and closed immersions of Gelfand stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.rigidSmooth_ofAdic
api.statement: A smooth morphism of partially proper rigid spaces (AdicSpacesPartII §R0.16, AdicEtaleGeometry §A2.4) is rigid smooth on the associated Berkovich spaces.

tests.name: rigidSmooth_openDisc
tests.statement: The open unit disc is rigid smooth over ℚ_p.

tests.name: berkSmooth_daggerDisc
tests.statement: The overconvergent closed disc GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩_{≤1}) is Berkovich-smooth but not rigid smooth.

tests.name: notSmooth_closedDisc
tests.statement: The closed disc GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), the canonical compactification, is neither Berkovich-smooth nor rigid smooth.

tests.name: berkEtale_notRigid
tests.statement: A †-rational localization onto a closed subdisc is Berkovich-étale but not rigid étale, since its image is not open.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.pushout_zariskiClosed
targets.statement: Call a map f: Z → X of Berkovich spaces Zariski closed if it is Toën-affine and locally on a strict closed affinoid cover X_i = GSpec(A_i) the map A_i → f_{i,*}O_{Z_i} is surjective on π_0 with connective target (ALRS Definition 2.7.1, p. 26, ALRS line 1366). Prove: (1) for Zariski closed f: Z → Y and g: Z → X the pushout X ⊔_Z Y exists in Berkovich spaces, with |X ⊔_Z Y| = |X| ⊔_{|Z|} |Y| and, in the affinoid case with π_0-surjective maps, X ⊔_Z Y = GSpec(O(X) ×_{O(Z)} O(Y)) (ALRS Lemma 2.7.3, p. 26, ALRS line 1375); (2) for g: GSpec(A) → GSpec(A′) inducing an isomorphism on uniform completions and f: GSpec(A) → X Zariski closed, X ⊔_{GSpec A} GSpec(A′) exists with space |X| and structure sheaf O_X ×_{O_Z} O_{Z′} (ALRS Lemma 2.7.4, p. 27, ALRS line 1441); (3) for connective solid ℚ_p-algebras A → B ← C with A → B surjective and D = A ×_B C, the functor D(D) → D(A) ×_{D(B)} D(C) is fully faithful, an equivalence on D^+, and an equivalence on Perf when A, B, C are Gelfand (ALRS Lemma 2.7.5, p. 27, ALRS line 1461).
hypotheses: Z, X, Y are Berkovich spaces; in (3) A, B, C are connective solid ℚ_p-algebras with A → B surjective on π_0

locator.where: Definition 2.7.1, Lemmas 2.7.3–2.7.5, p. 26; ALRS line 1366

tests.name: pushout_node
tests.statement: The pushout of two copies of GSpec(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) along their origins is GSpec(ℚ_p⟨S, T⟩/(ST)).

tests.name: pushout_counterexample
tests.statement: ALRS Lemma 2.7.5 fails for full module categories: for A = C = ℚ_p[T], B = ℚ_p, the pair (⊕_{n even} B[n], ⊕_{n odd} B[n]) lies in D(A) ×_{D(B)} D(C) but not in the image of D(D) (ALRS Example 2.7.6).

tests.name: zariski_noDescent
tests.statement: Zariski closed immersions do not satisfy !-descent: the inclusion of a disc of radius 1/2 into a disc of radius 1 becomes Zariski closed after base change to a strictly totally disconnected cover but is not Zariski closed (ALRS Example 2.7.2).

tests.name: pushout_emptyZ
tests.statement: For Z = ∅ the pushout is the disjoint union X ⊔ Y.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.IsDaggerCohesive
targets.statement: Call a map A → B of Gelfand rings a †-thickening if it is surjective and induces an isomorphism on †-reductions. Call a map f: Y → X of Gelfand stacks †-cohesive if for every †-thickening B → A and every surjection C → A of Gelfand rings the square with corners Y(B ×_A C), Y(B) ×_{Y(A)} Y(C), X(B ×_A C), X(B) ×_{X(A)} X(C) is cartesian (ALRS Definition 2.7.7, p. 29, ALRS line 1538). Prove that maps of Berkovich spaces are †-cohesive, that Perf(−) is †-cohesive, that X^an → GSpec(R) is †-cohesive for a perfect strongly Tannakian X (ALRS Example 2.7.8, p. 29, ALRS line 1546), and that †-cohesive maps satisfy two-out-of-three over a †-cohesive base, are stable under base change, and include all †-formally étale maps (ALRS Lemma 2.7.9, p. 29, ALRS line 1555).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of Gelfand stacks

locator.where: Definition 2.7.7, Example 2.7.8, Lemma 2.7.9, p. 29; ALRS line 1538

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.daggerCohesive_berkovich
api.statement: Every morphism of Berkovich spaces is †-cohesive (by 4.3(2)).

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.daggerCohesive_cancel
api.statement: If f: Y → X is †-cohesive then g: Z → Y is †-cohesive if and only if f ∘ g is; base changes of †-cohesive maps are †-cohesive.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.daggerCohesive_ofEtale
api.statement: †-formally étale maps are †-cohesive; in particular every de Rham stack Y^dR → GSpec(ℚ_p) is †-cohesive.

tests.name: thickening_dualNumbers
tests.statement: ℚ_p[ε]/ε² → ℚ_p is a †-thickening; ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p (T ↦ 0) is surjective but not a †-thickening, since the †-reductions differ.

tests.name: cohesive_perf
tests.statement: For B = ℚ_p[ε]/ε² → A = ℚ_p and C = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p, Perf(B ×_A C) ≅ Perf(B) ×_{Perf(A)} Perf(C) by 4.3(3).

tests.name: cohesive_point
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p) → GSpec(ℚ_p) is †-cohesive.

targets.name: TauCeti.Gelfand.cotangentComplex
targets.statement: With the solid cotangent complex of the contract `solid-cotangent-complex` (AnalyticStacks §§5.1–5.2): for a map A → B of solid animated ℤ-algebras, L_{B/A} ∈ D_{≥0}(B) corepresents A-linear derivations into connective modules, with base change, colimit, transitivity and idempotent-vanishing properties (ALRS Lemma A.1.1, p. 175, ALRS line 9427), and for discrete A, L_{A/ℤ} is discrete with L_{A/ℤ}(*) = L_{A(*)/ℤ} (ALRS Lemma A.1.3(1), p. 175, ALRS line 9463). AnalyticStacks §5.3 gives, for a descendable map A → A_0 of solid animated R-algebras with Čech conerve A^•, the equivalence ∧^m_A L_{A/R} → Tot(∧^m_{A^•} L_{A^•/R}) for all m (ALRS Lemma A.1.2, p. 175, ALRS line 9435). Prove that for a p-complete solid animated ℤ-algebra A, L_{A/ℤ_p} is p-complete and L_{A[1/p]/ℚ_p} = (lim_n L_{(A/p^n)/(ℤ/p^n)})[1/p] (ALRS Lemma A.1.3(2), p. 175, ALRS line 9464).
hypotheses: A → B is a map of solid animated ℤ-algebras; in the proved clause A is a p-complete solid animated ℤ-algebra

locator.where: Lemma A.1.3, p. 175; ALRS line 9462

tests.name: cotangent_Tate
tests.statement: L_{ℚ_p⟨T⟩/ℚ_p} = ℚ_p⟨T⟩·dT in degree 0 (ALRS Remark 2.6.6).

tests.name: cotangent_idempotent
tests.statement: For a †-rational localization A → A⟨f/g⟩_{≤1}, an idempotent map, the cotangent complex vanishes.

tests.name: cotangent_Cp
tests.statement: L_{C_p/ℚ_p} ≅ gr¹B⁺_dR(C_p)[1] = C_p(1)[1] (ALRS line 3889), nonzero although C_p is perfectoid: perfectoid vanishing applies only between perfectoid rings.

tests.name: cotangent_not_p_complete
tests.statement: For the solid ℤ_p-algebra ℤ_p[T] = ⊕_{n ≥ 0} ℤ_p·T^n, which is not p-complete, base change gives L_{ℤ_p[T]/ℤ_p} = ℤ_p[T]·dT, a countable direct sum of copies of ℤ_p and not p-complete (its p-completion is ℤ_p⟨T⟩·dT): the p-completeness hypothesis on A cannot be dropped.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.DeformationTheory
targets.statement: For a map f: Y → X of presheaves on affinoid Gelfand stacks define: f is nilcomplete if Y(A) = lim_n Y(τ_{≤n}A) relative to X for strictly totally disconnected A; infinitesimally cohesive if for every square-zero extension Ã_d → A with derivation d: A → M[1], M connective, Y(Ã_d) ≅ Y(A) ×_{Y(A ⊕ M[1])} Y(A) relative to X; f admits a cotangent complex if there is a locally eventually connective L_{Y/X} ∈ D^+(Y) with fib(Y(R ⊕ M) → Y(R) ×_{X(R)} X(R ⊕ M)) ≅ τ_{≥0}Hom_R(η^*L_{Y/X}, M) naturally; f is formally étale if L_{Y/X} = 0 and formally smooth if L_{Y/X} is the dual of a connective perfect complex; f admits a deformation theory if it has all three properties (ALRS Definition A.2.2, p. 177, ALRS line 9552). Prove that maps of affinoid Gelfand stacks admit a deformation theory (ALRS Example A.2.3, p. 178, ALRS line 9591), that de Rham stacks are nilcomplete, infinitesimally cohesive and have zero cotangent complex (ALRS Lemma A.2.4, p. 178, ALRS line 9595), and the stability properties with the transitivity fibre sequence f^*L_{Y/X} → L_{Z/X} → L_{Z/Y} (ALRS Lemma A.2.5, p. 178, ALRS line 9601).
hypotheses: f is a map of presheaves of anima on affinoid Gelfand stacks

locator.where: Definition A.2.2, Lemmas A.2.4–A.2.5, p. 177; ALRS line 9552

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.DeformationTheory.transitivity
api.statement: For Z → Y → X with Y → X admitting a cotangent complex, Z → Y admits one if and only if Z → X does, with the fibre sequence f^*L_{Y/X} → L_{Z/X} → L_{Z/Y}.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.DeformationTheory.affinoid
api.statement: For GSpec(B) → GSpec(A), L is the solid cotangent complex L_{B/A} of 4.5.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.DeformationTheory.deRham
api.statement: X^dR → GSpec(ℚ_p) admits a deformation theory with L = 0.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.DeformationTheory.sqz
api.statement: If f is infinitesimally cohesive with cotangent complex, square-zero extensions of Y over X with ideal M are τ_{≥0}Hom(L_{Y/X}, M[1]).

tests.name: deformation_line
tests.statement: L_{A¹} = O·dT, so A¹ is formally smooth.

tests.name: deformation_point
tests.statement: For the zero section 0 → A¹, L = (T)/(T²)[1] = ℚ_p[1], whose dual ℚ_p[−1] is not connective; the map is not formally smooth, but it has perfect amplitude [−1, 0] (quasi-syntomic).

tests.name: deformation_deRham
tests.statement: L_{(A¹)^dR} = 0, consistent with (A¹)^dR = A¹/G_a^†: in the transitivity sequence of the G_a^†-torsor A¹ → (A¹)^dR, the term L_{A¹} = O·dT maps isomorphically onto the relative cotangent complex O, the dual of Lie(G_a^†) = ℚ_p.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.quasiProEtale_descent
targets.statement: Call A → B a †-quasi-pro-étale map of Gelfand rings if Marc(B) → Marc(A) is quasi-pro-étale and GSpec(B) → GSpec(A) is †-formally étale, with covers the finite jointly surjective families (ALRS Definition A.2.17, p. 184, ALRS line 9917). Prove that †-rational localizations and Berkovich-étale maps are †-quasi-pro-étale (ALRS Remark A.2.18, p. 184, ALRS line 9921), the stability properties of ALRS Lemma A.2.19, p. 184, ALRS line 9939, and that over a strictly totally disconnected A every †-quasi-pro-étale A → B is a filtered colimit of finite étale A-algebras, hence flat (ALRS Lemma A.2.20, p. 186, ALRS line 10024). For a topology τ of !-covers satisfying the flatness and formal smoothness conditions of ALRS §A.2, prove that nilcompleteness, infinitesimal cohesiveness and existence of cotangent complexes descend along epimorphisms that are infinitesimally cohesive and formally smooth, and along τ-covers of the target (ALRS Proposition A.2.15, p. 182, ALRS line 9833; ALRS Lemma A.2.11, p. 180, ALRS line 9732).
hypotheses: Gelfand rings are qfd; τ is a topology of !-covers with the (flat) and (formsm) properties of ALRS §A.2

locator.where: Definition A.2.17, Lemmas A.2.19–A.2.20, Proposition A.2.15, p. 184; ALRS line 9917

tests.name: qpe_localization
tests.statement: A †-rational localization is †-quasi-pro-étale but not finite étale.

tests.name: qpe_flat
tests.statement: For A = C(S, C_p) with S light profinite and a clopen decomposition S = S_1 ⊔ S_2, A → C(S_1, C_p) is †-quasi-pro-étale and flat.

tests.name: qpe_identity
tests.statement: Identities are †-quasi-pro-étale covers.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.tangentComplex
targets.statement: For an infinitesimally cohesive map f: Y → X with cotangent complex define its tangent complex T_f (and shifts T_f[1]) as the spectrum-valued functor (R, η, M) ↦ fib(Y(R ⊕ M) → Y(R) ×_{X(R)} X(R ⊕ M)) (ALRS Construction A.3.1, p. 186, ALRS line 10041), and the overconvergent shifted twisted tangent complex (T_X[1]{1})^† as the fibre of T_X[1]{1} → its de Rham stack (ALRS Remark 3.1.4, p. 43, ALRS line 2230). Prove that for a map Y → X of arc-stacks weakly representable in arc-diamonds, Ŷ → X̂ is infinitesimally cohesive with zero cotangent complex (ALRS Lemma A.3.4, p. 187, ALRS line 10104); that for a group G → S admitting a deformation theory and formally smooth, with BG → S admitting a deformation theory, L_{BG/S} ≅ e^*L_f[−1] is the shifted adjoint representation on the cotangent complex at the unit (ALRS Proposition A.3.5, p. 188, ALRS line 10123); and that for a partially proper rigid analytic group G over a Banach field K, BG and BG^† (G^† the overconvergent neighbourhood of 1) admit a deformation theory over GSpec(K), with GSpec(K) → BG^{dR/K} and BG^† → BG epimorphisms for the †-quasi-pro-étale topology (ALRS Lemma A.3.6, p. 190, ALRS line 10234).
hypotheses: f is infinitesimally cohesive and admits a cotangent complex; G is formally smooth with a deformation theory

locator.where: Construction A.3.1, Lemma A.3.4, Proposition A.3.5, Lemma A.3.6, p. 186; ALRS line 10041

tests.name: tangent_BGm
tests.statement: L_{BG_m} = O[−1], the dual of the one-dimensional adjoint representation shifted by −1.

tests.name: tangent_BGaDagger
tests.statement: L_{BG_a^†} = O[−1], although G_a^† has trivial underlying arc-stack.

tests.name: tangent_trivialGroup
tests.statement: For the trivial group, BG = S and L_{BG/S} = 0.

tests.name: tangent_perfectoid
tests.statement: For a perfectoid space Y over a perfectoid X, L_{Ŷ/X̂} = 0, whereas L_{C_p/ℚ_p} ≠ 0 since ℚ_p is not perfectoid (compare 4.5).

layers.title: The cone construction and the filtered de Rham stack

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone
targets.statement: For a Gelfand stack Y define its cone Y^cone → A¹/G_m as the functor sending a Gelfand stack Z with a Cartier divisor D ⊆ Z to Y(D), its overconvergent cone Y^{†-cone} = Y^cone ×_{A¹/G_m} A^{1,†}/G_m, its formal cone Y^{cone^} = Y^cone ×_{A¹/G_m} Â¹/G_m and its special fibre Y^cone_s = Y^cone ×_{A¹/G_m} BG_m; for f: Y → X define the relative cone Y^{cone/X} = Y^cone ×_{X^cone} (X × A¹/G_m) (ALRS Definition 2.8.1, p. 30, ALRS line 1598). Prove that Y^cone is a Gelfand stack (ALRS Lemma 2.8.2, p. 30, ALRS line 1609), that it is g_* f^* for f: BG_m → GSpec(ℚ_p) and g: BG_m → A¹/G_m and so commutes with limits (ALRS Remark 2.8.4, p. 30, ALRS line 1621), that there is a natural map Y^cone_s → Y × BG_m induced by R ⊕ I[1] → R (ALRS Remark 2.8.3, p. 30, ALRS line 1618), that Y^{cone/X} ×_{A¹/G_m} G_m/G_m ≅ X and, when f admits a cotangent complex, Y^{cone/X}_s ≅ T_{Y/X}[1](−1) over Y × BG_m, with G_m acting through t ↦ t^{-1} (ALRS Lemma 2.8.6, p. 31, ALRS line 1653), and that for †-formally étale Y → X the squares relating Y^{†-cone}, X^{†-cone}, their de Rham stacks and Y^dR, X^dR are cartesian, likewise for formal cones (ALRS Lemma 2.8.7, p. 31, ALRS line 1677). For a Cartier divisor D → W and Y → D define the relative cone Y^{cone/(D,W)} = Y^cone ×_{D^cone} W along the natural map W → D^cone (ALRS Definition 2.8.9, p. 32, ALRS line 1700). For an analytic stack X (in particular X^An for a Gelfand stack X, 2.1) define the algebraic cone X^{cone-alg} → A^{1,alg}/G_m^alg as the sheafification of the functor sending an affinoid analytic stack AnSpec(A) with a Cartier divisor I → A to X(A/I), its algebraic formal cone X^{cone-alg^} over Â¹/G_m^alg and their relative versions (ALRS Remark 2.9.7(1), p. 39, ALRS line 2062). Prove that for a !-Zariski closed map f: Z → X of Gelfand stacks (f Toën-affine and O_X → f_*O_Z !-locally a surjection of connective rings) the algebraic formal cone Z^{cone-alg^/X} → X × Â¹/G_m^alg is the relative spectrum of the adic filtration of O_X → f_*O_Z, defined by descent from the affinoid case of the contract `formal-cone-adic-filtration` (ALRS Remark 2.9.7(2), p. 39, ALRS line 2086).
hypotheses: Y → X is a map of Gelfand stacks; for the special-fibre identification it admits a cotangent complex

locator.where: Definition 2.8.1, Lemmas 2.8.2, 2.8.6, 2.8.7, Definition 2.8.9, p. 30; ALRS line 1598

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_limits
api.statement: Y ↦ Y^cone commutes with all limits of Gelfand stacks.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_generic
api.statement: The restriction of Y^{cone/X} to G_m/G_m is X.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_special
api.statement: If f admits a cotangent complex, Y^{cone/X}_s ≅ T_{Y/X}[1] ⊗_{G_a} G_a(−1) over Y × BG_m.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_relative_divisor
api.statement: The natural map W → D^cone over A¹/G_m sends Z → W to Z ×_W D → D; relative cones over (D, W) are functorial in Y → D.

api.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_zariski
api.statement: For a Zariski closed immersion Z → X of Berkovich spaces, Z^{cone/X} is the analytification of the deformation to the normal bundle (SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5, adic filtration of O_X → O_Z).

tests.name: cone_point
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p)^cone = A¹/G_m and ∅^cone = G_m/G_m, since Y(R/I) = Y(0) is a point when I = R and empty otherwise for Y = ∅.

tests.name: cone_Ga
tests.statement: G_a^cone = G_{a,A¹/G_m}/G_a(−1), where G_a(−1) is the geometric vector bundle of the ideal I → R (ALRS Example 2.8.5(1)).

tests.name: cone_special_line
tests.statement: For Y = A¹ over GSpec(ℚ_p), the special fibre is T_{A¹}[1](−1) = BG_a(−1) over A¹ × BG_m.

tests.name: cone_weight
tests.statement: The weight convention is t ↦ t^{-1} on the tangent direction: with weight +1 the special fibre of A¹ would be BG_a(1), which is not the classifying stack of the ideal sheaf I of the universal divisor (3.6).

tests.name: cone_adicFiltration_zeroSection
tests.statement: For the zero section Z = GSpec(ℚ_p) → X = GSpec(ℚ_p⟨x⟩) the adic filtration is (x^n)_n with associated graded Sym(I/I²) = ℚ_p[x̄], so the special fibre of the algebraic formal cone is the line Spec ℚ_p[x̄], the normal bundle T_{Z/X}[1] of the special-fibre law of this section; for the identity of X the adic filtration is constant with associated graded O_X in degree 0 and the cone is X × Â¹/G_m^alg, so a construction that always returned the normal line of a point is excluded.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.cone_obstruction
targets.statement: For Y → X with cotangent complex and locally eventually connective M define the anima of square-zero extensions Sqz(Y/X; M) = τ_{≥0}Hom_Y(L_{Y/X}, M[1]) and, for Y → X → S and η ∈ Sqz(X/S; M), the anima of square-zero lifts Sqz(Y/S; η) (ALRS Definition 2.8.11, p. 32, ALRS line 1712); the divisor BG_m → A¹/G_m carries the square-zero extension ℚ_p[t]/t², so every Cartier divisor D → W has its first infinitesimal neighbourhood D(1) (ALRS Example 2.8.12, p. 32, ALRS line 1724). For Berkovich spaces construct the underlying square-zero thickening of η, compatible with base change and †-formally étale maps (ALRS Lemma 2.8.13, p. 33, ALRS line 1762; ALRS Lemma 2.8.14, p. 33, ALRS line 1777). Prove: for a Cartier divisor D → W over S and Y → D, Y^{cone/(D,W)} → W is an isomorphism off D; if Y → D → W → S are infinitesimally cohesive with cotangent complexes, Y^{cone/(D,W)}_s = D ×_{T_{D/S}[1](−1)} T_{Y/S}[1](−1) along the map classifying L_{D/S} → L_{D/W}; Y^{cone/(D,W)}_s → Y is a principal homogeneous space for T_{Y/D}[1] ⊗ N*_{D/W}, whose sections over †-formally étale U → Y are the square-zero lifts of U from D to D(1) (ALRS Proposition 2.8.15, p. 34, ALRS line 1805).
hypotheses: D → W is a Cartier divisor of Gelfand stacks over S; Y → D → W → S are infinitesimally cohesive and admit cotangent complexes

locator.where: Definition 2.8.11, Example 2.8.12, Lemmas 2.8.13–2.8.14, Proposition 2.8.15, p. 32; ALRS line 1712

tests.name: sqz_dualNumbers
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), M = ℚ_p, Sqz(X/X; ℚ_p) is a point (L = 0) and the unique extension is ℚ_p[ε]/ε².

tests.name: sqz_trivialDivisor
tests.statement: For the trivial divisor D × 0 → D × A¹, sections of the special fibre of X^{cone/D} always exist (the trivial deformation to D × GSpec(ℚ_p[t]/t²)), whereas for the divisor GSpec(C_p) → Spf B⁺_dR sections correspond to lifts to B⁺_dR/ξ², which need not exist (ALRS Remark 2.8.16).

tests.name: sqz_identity
tests.statement: For Y = D the principal homogeneous space is trivial since T_{D/D} = 0, and its canonical section corresponds to D(1) itself.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.formalCone_deRham
targets.statement: Use the realization of algebraic stacks as analytic stacks, under which sheaves on BG_m^alg, A^{1,alg}/G_m^alg and Â¹/G_m^alg over an analytic stack are graded, filtered and complete filtered modules, and Â¹/G_m^alg = BG_a[−1]/G_m^alg with the Beilinson t-structure (ALRS Remark 2.9.1, p. 35, ALRS line 1866; ALRS Remark 2.9.2, p. 36, ALRS line 1900). Prove that for a formally smooth map f: Y → X of Berkovich spaces with Ω¹_{Y/X} = L_{Y/X} a vector bundle, the map h: Y^{cone^/X} → |Y|^Betti × Â¹/G_m^alg is prim, so Mod_{h_*1}(D(|Y|^Betti × Â¹/G_m^alg)) → D(Y^{cone^/X}) is fully faithful; that the underlying graded algebra of h_*1 is ⊕_i Ω^i_{Y/X}[−i](i) with Ω^i_{Y/X} = ∧^i Ω¹_{Y/X}; and that if f factors through a formally étale Y → A^n_X then, after shearing, h_*1 ≅ (Ω^•_{A^n/ℚ_p}, d) ⊗ O_Y (ALRS Proposition 2.9.3, p. 36, ALRS line 1914). Prove that for a smooth rigid space X over a Banach field K which is a Berkovich space, h_*1 lies in the heart of the Beilinson t-structure and is, after shearing, the de Rham complex (Ω^•_{X/K}, d) with its structure of commutative differential graded algebra, so that filtered flat connections with Griffiths transversality embed fully faithfully into D(X^{cone^/K}) (ALRS Corollary 2.9.4, p. 38, ALRS line 2010; ALRS Example 2.9.5, p. 38, ALRS line 2021). Prove the relative version over a Cartier divisor D ⊆ W with W complete along D and a lift X̃ → W of a formally smooth X → D: X^{cone^/(D,W)} → |X|^Betti × W is prim, and for X̃ formally étale over A^n_W and D static, h_*1 is the D-de Rham complex O → Ω¹(D) → Ω²(2D) → ⋯ (ALRS Proposition 2.9.9, p. 40, ALRS line 2119).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a formally smooth morphism of Berkovich spaces with Ω¹_{Y/X} a vector bundle; in Corollary 2.9.4 X is smooth rigid over a Banach field K and a Berkovich space

locator.where: Proposition 2.9.3, Corollary 2.9.4, Proposition 2.9.9, p. 36; ALRS line 1914

tests.name: formalCone_point
tests.statement: For X = Y = GSpec(K), h_*1 = K in degree 0 and weight 0.

tests.name: formalCone_line
tests.statement: For the open disc over ℚ_p, h_*1 is O → Ω¹ with Fil¹ = Ω¹[−1] and gr¹ = Ω¹[−1](1).

tests.name: formalCone_hodge
tests.statement: Before shearing, h_*1 is the Hodge complex ⊕ Ω^i[−i](i) with zero differential as a graded algebra; the de Rham differential is extra structure visible only through the cdga structure, so identifying h_*1 with the graded algebra alone loses the connection.

targets.name: TauCeti.GelfandStack.filteredDeRham
targets.statement: For a Gelfand stack X define the filtered de Rham stack X^{dR,+} → A¹/G_m as the sheafification of (I → R) ↦ X(R/(I ⊗_R Nil†(R))), with relative versions Y^{dR,+/X} and X^{dR,+/(D,W)} (ALRS Definition 3.1.1, p. 42, ALRS line 2195).
