Prove that for a †-cohesive map Y → X the square relating Y^{dR,+/X}, Y^{cone/X}, (Y × A¹/G_m)^dR and (Y^{cone/X})^dR is cartesian (ALRS Proposition 3.1.3, p. 42, ALRS line 2221), that over G_m/G_m the filtered de Rham stack is X^dR and, for X with a cotangent complex, over BG_m it is the Hodge stack, the classifying stack of the shifted tangent bundle T_X[1](−1) restricted to its overconvergent neighbourhood of zero, T^†_X[1](−1) (ALRS Remark 3.1.4, p. 43, ALRS line 2230). For a nilperfectoid A let Ã¹_A = A¹_{A^u} ⊔_{GSpec A^u} GSpec(A), a degree-one divisor on Ã¹_A being a Cartier divisor whose pullback to A¹_{A^u} is a section; define Div¹_{A¹} and X^{Div¹_{A¹}} (ALRS Definition 3.1.5, p. 43, ALRS line 2240). Prove the cartesian square (3.1.1) and Div¹_{A¹} ≅ A¹/G_m^†, and, for †-cohesive X, X^{Div¹_{A¹}} = X^{dR,+} ×_{A¹/G_m} A¹/G_m^† (ALRS §3.1, p. 43, ALRS line 2255).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; the cartesian descriptions need †-cohesiveness

locator.where: Definition 3.1.1, Proposition 3.1.3, Definition 3.1.5, p. 42; ALRS line 2195

tests.name: filtered_point
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p)^{dR,+} = A¹/G_m, since the point takes value a point on every ring.

tests.name: filtered_generic
tests.statement: Over G_m/G_m, (A¹)^{dR,+} restricts to (A¹)^dR = A¹/G_a^†.

tests.name: filtered_logConnection
tests.statement: Vector bundles on A¹/G_m^† are vector bundles on A¹ with a T-connection whose operator T∂_T integrates (ALRS Remark 3.1.6, ALRS line 2263); vector bundles on A¹/Ĝ_m are all T-connections, so A¹/Ĝ_m and A¹/G_m^† differ.

tests.name: filtered_nonCohesive
tests.statement: Without †-cohesiveness the square of ALRS Proposition 3.1.3 need not be cartesian; the proof uses exactly the cohesive square for the †-thickening R/I → R^{†-red}/(R^{†-red} ⊗ I).

layers.title: Fargues–Fontaine discs and curves, Hyodo–Kato stacks

targets.name: TauCeti.FF.disc
targets.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid space S = Spa(A) of characteristic p, qfd and separable, with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, define the relative Fargues–Fontaine disc D_{FF,S} = Spa(A_inf(A)) ∖ V([ϖ]) as the Berkovich space ⋃_s GSpec(B^†_{[0,s]}(S)), where A_inf(A) = W(A°) and B^†_{[0,s]} is the overconvergent rational localization of {|p|^s ≤ |[ϖ]| ≠ 0}, and the punctured disc D^×_{FF,S} = D_{FF,S} ∖ V(p) (ALRS §3.2, p. 44, ALRS line 2295). Construct its Frobenius φ_S and the radius map κ_ϖ: D_{FF,S} → [0, ∞)^Betti with κ_ϖ(x) = log|[ϖ]|_x / log|p|_x, so that κ_ϖ ∘ φ = p·κ_ϖ, κ_ϖ^{-1}(0) is the overconvergent neighbourhood of {p = 0} and κ_ϖ^{-1}((0,∞)) = D^×_{FF,S}; for S = T♭ with T perfectoid over ℚ_p fix the canonical radius κ by taking ϖ = p♭, which does not depend on the choice (ALRS Remark 3.2.1, p. 44, ALRS line 2322). Prove D^⋄_{FF,S} = S × Marc(ℤ_p) and D^{×,⋄}_{FF,S} = S × Marc(ℚ_p), that the constructions globalize to perfectoid spaces over 𝔽_p preserving Tate-analytic covers, and that every map of Gelfand stacks X → D^×_{FF,Y} from a perfectoid space X over ℚ_p extends uniquely to a φ-equivariant map D^×_{FF,X♭} → D^×_{FF,Y} through the untilt (ALRS Lemma 3.2.2, p. 45, ALRS line 2336).
hypotheses: S is a separable qfd affinoid perfectoid space over 𝔽_p with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ

locator.where: §3.2, Remark 3.2.1, Lemma 3.2.2, p. 44; ALRS line 2295

api.name: TauCeti.FF.radius_frobenius
api.statement: κ_ϖ(φ(x)) = p·κ_ϖ(x), and replacing ϖ by ϖ^m multiplies κ_ϖ by m.

api.name: TauCeti.FF.disc_diamond
api.statement: D^{×,⋄}_{FF,S} = S ×_{Marc(𝔽_p)} Marc(ℚ_p), compatibly with φ = φ_S × id.

api.name: TauCeti.FF.disc_compare
api.statement: On analytic adic spaces, D^×_{FF,S} agrees with the period domain Y_S of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals §VB−1 (relative-annuli) and RelativeFarguesFontaine §1.2, and κ_ϖ with periodRadius of radiusFunctionAndRationalAnnuli; for S = Spa(A) and R = A°, the points of the classical adic space underlying D^×_{FF,S} form Tau Ceti's 𝒴 ⊂ Spa(W(R), W(R)) with its Frobenius homeomorphism, and Tau Ceti's radius bounds and their Frobenius law are the conditions q ≤ κ_ϖ, κ_ϖ ≤ q and the identity κ_ϖ ∘ φ = p·κ_ϖ (supplier contracts, From Tau Ceti).

api.name: TauCeti.FF.disc_witt
api.statement: Maps X → D^×_{FF,Y} from a perfectoid X over ℚ_p factor uniquely as X → D^×_{FF,X♭} → D^×_{FF,Y} with the second map φ-equivariant (the analytic analogue of W(R) → A factoring through W(A)).

tests.name: radius_untilt
tests.statement: At the point of D^×_{FF,C♭} given by the untilt C, |[p♭]| = |p| = p^{-1}, so κ = 1 for the canonical radius; its Frobenius translates have radius p^n for n ∈ ℤ.

tests.name: radius_reciprocal
tests.statement: The reciprocal convention log|p|/log|[ϖ]| would send Frobenius to multiplication by p^{-1} and κ^{-1}(0) to {[ϖ] = 0}, contradicting κ ∘ φ = p·κ and κ^{-1}(0) = {|p| = 0}.

tests.name: disc_field
tests.statement: For S = Spa(C♭), D^×_{FF,S} is the punctured open disc Y_{(0,∞)} of C♭.

tests.name: disc_empty
tests.statement: For S = ∅ both discs are empty.

targets.name: TauCeti.FF.curve
targets.statement: Prove that Marc(A) ↦ D^×_{FF,A} takes the geometric realization of an arc-hypercover of separable totally disconnected perfectoid rings over 𝔽_p to a !-equivalence (ABLB Corollary 4.4.10, p. 50, ABLB line 2641), and deduce the left exact colimit-preserving relative punctured Fargues–Fontaine disc D^×_{FF,−}: ArcStk → GelfStk (ALRS (3.2.1), p. 45, ALRS line 2352). For an arc-stack X over 𝔽_p define the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_X = D^×_{FF,X}/φ^ℤ, a Gelfand stack (ALRS Definition 3.2.6, p. 45, ALRS line 2390). Prove that the natural map \hat{FF^⋄_X} → FF_X is not an isomorphism unless X = ∅: for a perfectoid X it is the map from the quotient of the uniformly completed cyclotomic base change by ℤ_p^{×,cont} to the quotient of the uncompleted one by ℤ_p^{×,sm} (ALRS Remark 3.2.4, p. 45, ALRS line 2357), and that FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)} ≅ FF_{ℚ_p^cyc}/Γ^cont with Γ = Gal(ℚ_p^cyc/ℚ_p) (ALRS Example 3.2.7, p. 46, ALRS line 2394). The quasi-coherent theory of (3.2.1) is a light variant of the solid formalism D_{(0,∞)} of ALBM (ALRS Remark 3.2.5, p. 45, ALRS line 2385).
hypotheses: X is an arc-stack over 𝔽_p

locator.where: (3.2.1), Definition 3.2.6, Remark 3.2.4, Example 3.2.7, p. 45; ALRS line 2352

api.name: TauCeti.FF.disc_colim
api.statement: D^×_{FF,−} preserves colimits and finite limits; FF_− preserves colimits.

api.name: TauCeti.FF.curve_compare
api.statement: For a perfectoid S over 𝔽_p, FF_S is the Gelfand stack of the relative curve X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals §VB−1 and RelativeFarguesFontaine §2.1.

api.name: TauCeti.FF.curve_cyclotomic
api.statement: FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)} ≅ FF_{ℚ_p^cyc}/Γ^cont, with Γ^cont = GSpec(C(Γ, ℚ_p)).

tests.name: curve_field
tests.statement: For X = Marc(C♭), FF_X is the Fargues–Fontaine curve of C♭.

tests.name: curve_notHat
tests.statement: For X = Marc(ℚ_p^cyc,♭) the map \hat{FF^⋄_X} → FF_X is the map from a quotient by ℤ_p^{×,cont} to a quotient by ℤ_p^{×,sm}, not an isomorphism.

tests.name: curve_empty
tests.statement: For X = ∅ both sides are empty and the map is an isomorphism.

targets.name: TauCeti.FF.hyodoKato
targets.statement: For an arc-stack X over 𝔽_p define the open punctured curve Y^⋄_X = X ×_{Marc(𝔽_p)} Marc(ℚ_p), its de Rham stack Y^dR_X = (Y^⋄_X)^dR, the curve FF^⋄_X = Y^⋄_X/φ^ℤ and the Hyodo–Kato stack X^HK = (FF^⋄_X)^dR; for a Gelfand stack X put X^HK = (X^⋄)^HK (ABLB Definition 6.1.1, p. 94, ABLB line 4983; ABLB Definition 6.1.2, p. 94, ABLB line 4989). Let O(n) on Marc(𝔽_p)^HK ≅ GSpec(ℚ_p)/φ^ℤ be the line bundle of the isocrystal (ℚ_p, p^{-n}φ) (ABLB Definition 6.2.4, p. 99, ABLB line 5247). Prove: for a map f: Y → X of qfd arc-stacks over ℤ_p which is arc-locally lqfd, f^HK is !-able and cohomologically proper when f is proper; if f is smooth of pure relative dimension d, f^HK is cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex (O(1)[2])^{⊗d}, the d-th power of the Tate twist, and cohomologically étale when f is étale; similarly for f^{Y^dR} (ABLB Theorem 6.3.1, p. 102, ABLB line 5415); for proper smooth f between Berkovich spaces over ℚ_p, f^HK_* preserves perfect modules (ABLB Corollary 6.3.2, p. 103, ABLB line 5470). Prove that f^HK_*O = O ⊕ O(−1)[−1] for G_m → Marc(𝔽_p) (ABLB Lemma 6.2.5, p. 99, ABLB line 5250) and that Hyodo–Kato stacks carry a strong theory of first Chern classes in the sense of Zav Definition 5.2.8 (ABLB Lemma 6.2.9, p. 100, ABLB line 5303).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of qfd arc-stacks over ℤ_p; smoothness of pure relative dimension d for the dualizing statement

locator.where: Definitions 6.1.1–6.1.2, Theorem 6.3.1, Corollary 6.3.2, p. 102; ABLB line 5415

tests.name: hk_point
tests.statement: Marc(𝔽_p)^HK = GSpec(ℚ_p)/φ^ℤ and its vector bundles are isocrystals over ℚ_p; O(1) is (ℚ_p, p^{-1}φ), of slope −1.

tests.name: hk_Gm
tests.statement: For G_m, H¹ = O(−1), the isocrystal (ℚ_p, pφ): Frobenius acts on dlog T by p, matching the convention φ(dlog t) = p·dlog t.

tests.name: hk_duality_P1
tests.statement: For P¹ → Marc(𝔽_p), f^HK_*O = O ⊕ O(−1)[−2] and ω = O(1)[2], so the trace pairs H²(P¹) = O(−1) with O(1) to give O.

tests.name: hk_sign
tests.statement: With ω = O(−1)[2] the trace H²(P¹) ⊗ ω would land in O(−2) ≠ O, so the dualizing twist has slope −1 isocrystal O(1), not O(−1).

targets.name: TauCeti.FF.smooth_light
targets.statement: Transport to the light Gelfand formalism, through the comparison of !-functors of ABLB §4.4 (ALRS footnote 57, p. 164, ALRS line 8910), the following statements. (1) For a smooth morphism g: Y → X of analytic adic spaces over ℚ_p, FF_{Y^⋄} → FF_{X^⋄} is cohomologically smooth (ALBM Theorem 4.4.4, p. 36, ALBM line 1580); if g is equidimensional of dimension d, its dualizing complex is the Tate twist O ⊗ ℚ_p(d) placed in cohomological degree −2d (ALBM Theorem 4.4.6, p. 38, ALBM line 1654). (2) FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)} → GSpec(ℚ_p) is cohomologically smooth and proper, with dualizing complex the (φ, Γ)-module of the cyclotomic character in degree −2 (ALBM Theorem 4.5.1, p. 40, ALBM line 1753; ALBM Corollary 4.5.2, p. 44, ALBM line 1930). Here the Tate twist ℚ_p(1) is the slope-zero line bundle given by the cyclotomic character, not the degree-one bundle O(1) of 7.6.
hypotheses: g: Y → X is a smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over ℚ_p, equidimensional of dimension d for the dualizing statement

locator.where: Theorems 4.4.4, 4.4.6, 4.5.1, Corollary 4.5.2, p. 36; ALBM line 1580

tests.name: ffsmooth_dim0
tests.statement: For g an étale map, d = 0 and the dualizing complex is O.

tests.name: ffsmooth_tate_vs_slope
tests.statement: On FF_{C♭} the Tate twist O ⊗ ℚ_p(1) has H⁰ = ℚ_p(1), one-dimensional, whereas O(1) has H⁰ = BC(O(1))(C) = B^{φ=p}_cris, infinite-dimensional; reading (d) as O(d) gives the wrong dualizing complex.

tests.name: ffsmooth_point
tests.statement: For (2), Γ(FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)}, O) = RΓ(G_{ℚ_p}, ℚ_p) has dimensions 1, 2, 0 in degrees 0, 1, 2, and duality with ℚ_p(1)[2] pairs H⁰ with H²(ℚ_p(1)) = ℚ_p and H¹ with H¹(ℚ_p(1)), local Tate duality.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.DeltaSpace
targets.statement: A rational δ-space is a tuple (S, 𝒳, ι, φ_𝒳) with S a qfd perfectoid space of characteristic p, 𝒳 a Berkovich space with an endomorphism φ_𝒳, and ι: D^×_{FF,S} → 𝒳 a map of Berkovich spaces inducing an isomorphism of arc-stacks D^{×,⋄}_{FF,S} ≅ 𝒳^⋄ with φ_𝒳 ∘ ι ≅ ι ∘ φ (a property, since D^×_{FF,S} is locally the spectrum of a static Banach algebra). A morphism (S, 𝒳) → (S′, 𝒳′) is a map α: S → S′, a φ-equivariant map 𝒳 → 𝒳′ (a datum) and the commutative square with the map of discs induced by α (a property). A δ-space is perfect if φ_𝒳 is an automorphism; Spc^δ and PerfSpc^δ denote the categories (ALRS Definition 3.3.1, p. 46, ALRS line 2398). For a perfect δ-space the Frobenius acts totally discontinuously on |𝒳| and the thickened Fargues–Fontaine curve 𝒳/φ^ℤ is defined (ALRS Remark 3.3.2, p. 46, ALRS line 2417). Prove that S ↦ (S, D^×_{FF,S}) is an equivalence from perfectoid spaces of characteristic p onto the full subcategory Spc^{δ,cl} of classical δ-spaces, and that the inclusion has right adjoint (S, 𝒳) ↦ S (ALRS Example 3.3.4, p. 46, ALRS line 2429; ALRS Lemma 3.5.2, p. 51, ALRS line 2670).
hypotheses: S is a separable qfd perfectoid space over 𝔽_p; 𝒳 is a qfd Berkovich space

locator.where: Definition 3.3.1, Remark 3.3.2, Lemma 3.5.2, p. 46; ALRS line 2398

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.DeltaSpace.frobenius
api.statement: The Frobenius φ_𝒳 together with φ_S is an endomorphism of δ-spaces, natural in morphisms.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.DeltaSpace.classical_equiv
api.statement: Perf ≅ Spc^{δ,cl}, and Hom((S, D^×_{FF,S}), (S′, 𝒳′)) = Hom(S, S′).

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.DeltaSpace.curve
api.statement: For a perfect δ-space, 𝒳/φ^ℤ is a Berkovich space with |𝒳/φ^ℤ| = |𝒳|/φ^ℤ.

tests.name: delta_classical
tests.statement: For S = Spa(C♭), (S, D^×_{FF,S}) is a perfect δ-space whose thickened curve is FF_{C♭}.

tests.name: delta_cyclotomic
tests.statement: For S = Marc(𝔽_p((π^{1/p^∞}))), the decompleted perfected punctured open disc D^{×,<1,perf}_{ℚ_p} with φ(x) = x^p is a perfect δ-space which is not a †-thickening of D^×_{FF,S} (ALRS Example 3.3.5).

tests.name: delta_doubled
tests.statement: For 𝒳 = D^×_{FF,S} ⊔ D^×_{FF,S} with ι the first inclusion, ι^⋄ is not an isomorphism, so this is not a δ-space.

tests.name: delta_empty
tests.statement: For S = ∅ the only δ-space is (∅, ∅), since a Berkovich space with empty perfectoidization is empty.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.DeltaSpace.ofUniformlyPerfectoid
targets.statement: Let A be a uniformly perfectoid Gelfand ring, T = GSpec(A), T^u = GSpec(A^u), T♭ the tilt of T^u, f: T^u → D^×_{FF,T♭} the untilt and f_φ: ℕ × T^u → D^×_{FF,T♭} the map equal to φ^n ∘ f on {n} × T^u. Prove that the category of δ-spaces (S, 𝒳) with a map T → 𝒳 of Berkovich spaces has an initial object (T♭, 𝒳_T), where 𝒳_T is the pushout in Berkovich spaces of f_φ and ℕ × T^u → ℕ × T (ALRS Proposition 3.4.7, p. 48, ALRS line 2501; ALRS Definition 3.4.8, p. 48, ALRS line 2524). Prove the perfect analogue, with initial perfect δ-space D^×_{FF,A} = (ℤ × T) ⊔_{ℤ × T^u} D^×_{FF,T♭} and Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_A = D^×_{FF,A}/φ^ℤ (ALRS Remark 3.4.10, p. 48, ALRS line 2535); the radius map κ: 𝒳_T → (0, ∞) sends the n-th copy of T to p^n and κ^{-1}(p^n) = GSpec(A ×_{A^u} B^†_{[p^n,p^n],A^u}) (ALRS Remark 3.4.9, p. 48, ALRS line 2526). Prove that D^×_{FF,Marc(A^u)} → D^×_{FF,A} is an isomorphism if and only if A is perfectoid (ALRS Remark 3.4.17, p. 50, ALRS line 2634), and that 𝒳_T represents the maps W′(A_{≤1}) → B_{≤1} whose composite to every perfectoid B-algebra factors through D^×_{FF,A^u}, where W′(A_{≤1}) = W(A_{≤1}) ×_{W(A^{u,°})} W(A^{u,°,♭}) (ALRS Remark 1.5, p. 4, ALRS line 197).
hypotheses: A is a uniformly perfectoid Gelfand ring (A^u perfectoid)

locator.where: Proposition 3.4.7, Remarks 3.4.9–3.4.10, p. 48; ALRS line 2501

tests.name: deltaT_perfectoid
tests.statement: For A perfectoid, 𝒳_T = D^×_{FF,T♭}, since the pushout is along the identity of ℕ × T.

tests.name: deltaT_thickened
tests.statement: For A = C_p[ε]/ε², 𝒳_T agrees with D^×_{FF,C♭} away from the radii p^n, n ≥ 0, and at radius p^n contains the thickened point GSpec(C_p[ε]/ε²).

tests.name: deltaT_notIso
tests.statement: For A = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) uncompleted, the map D^×_{FF,Marc(A^u)} → D^×_{FF,A} is not an isomorphism, since A is not perfectoid.

tests.name: deltaT_zero
tests.statement: For A = 0, 𝒳_T = ∅.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack
targets.statement: Let (−)^preal: P(Spc^δ) → GelfStk be the colimit-preserving functor sending (S, 𝒳) to 𝒳; call a map of presheaves a !-equivalence if its realization is an isomorphism, and define the ∞-category AnStk^δ of rational analytic δ-stacks as the localization at !-equivalences, with induced colimit-preserving realization (−)^real: AnStk^δ → GelfStk; define PerfAnStk^δ likewise from perfect δ-spaces (ALRS Definition 3.4.2, p. 47, ALRS line 2470; ALRS Remark 3.4.4, p. 47, ALRS line 2482). Every analytic δ-stack has a Frobenius endomorphism, an automorphism in the perfect case, and realization is conservative (ALRS Remark 3.4.3, p. 47, ALRS line 2479; ALRS Remark 3.4.5, p. 47, ALRS line 2488). Prove that realization commutes with finite limits, hence is the inverse image of a geometric morphism, and that it sends 𝒴 to the !-sheafification of T = GSpec(A) ↦ 𝒴(T♭, 𝒳_T) on uniformly perfectoid A; in the perfect case to the sheafification of A ↦ 𝒴(Marc(A)♭, D^×_{FF,A}) (ALRS Proposition 3.4.12, p. 49, ALRS line 2569; ALRS Remark 3.4.13, p. 49, ALRS line 2586). Define admissible δ-stacks (realization needs no sheafification on nilperfectoids), prove that they are closed under limits and that for admissible 𝒴, (𝒴^perf)^real ≅ lim_φ 𝒴^real (ALRS Definition 3.4.15, p. 50, ALRS line 2614; ALRS Lemma 3.4.16, p. 50, ALRS line 2617); construct the perfection adjunction (ALRS Remark 3.4.14, p. 50, ALRS line 2599) and the δ-stacks T_{Spc^δ}: (S, 𝒳) ↦ T(𝒳) and T_{FF}: (S, 𝒳) ↦ T(𝒳/φ^ℤ) for a Gelfand stack T (ALRS Definition 3.4.18, p. 51, ALRS line 2651).
hypotheses: δ-spaces as in 7.1

locator.where: Definition 3.4.2, Proposition 3.4.12, Lemma 3.4.16, p. 47; ALRS line 2470

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack.real_finiteLimits
api.statement: (−)^real preserves colimits and finite limits and is conservative.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack.real_formula
api.statement: 𝒴^real is the !-sheafification of A ↦ 𝒴(T♭, 𝒳_T) on uniformly perfectoid A.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack.admissible_limits
api.statement: Admissible (perfect) analytic δ-stacks are closed under limits, and for admissible 𝒴 the perfection is computed by lim_φ on realizations.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack.frobenius
api.statement: The Frobenius of an analytic δ-stack is a natural endomorphism, inducing a Frobenius on its realization; T_{FF} has trivialized Frobenius.

tests.name: real_terminal
tests.statement: The final analytic δ-stack realizes to GSpec(ℚ_p), since realization preserves finite limits.

tests.name: real_representable
tests.statement: The δ-stack represented by (S, 𝒳) realizes to 𝒳.

tests.name: real_notSheaf
tests.statement: The presheaf T ↦ 𝒴(T♭, 𝒳_T) need not be a !-sheaf, because T ↦ 𝒳_T does not preserve fibre products even over a perfectoid base (ALRS footnote 24); sheafification is part of the definition.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.AnalyticDeltaStack.hyodoKato
targets.statement: Prove that (−)^⋄_FF: PerfAnStk^δ → ArcStk, 𝒴 ↦ (S ↦ 𝒴(S, D^×_{FF,S})), is well defined with a fully faithful left adjoint D^×_{FF,(−)}, the colimit-preserving extension of S ↦ D^×_{FF,S} which preserves finite limits, and a fully faithful right adjoint D^{×,dR}_{FF,(−)}: Y ↦ ((S, 𝒳) ↦ Y(S)) with admissible values (ALRS Proposition 3.5.3, p. 51, ALRS line 2685). Define the de Rham Fargues–Fontaine stack D^{×,dR}_{FF,Y} and 𝒴^dR = D^{×,dR}_{FF,𝒴^⋄_FF} (ALRS Definition 3.5.4, p. 52, ALRS line 2735). Prove that (D^{×,dR}_{FF,Y})^real = (Y × Marc(ℚ_p))^dR, so that Y^HK = D^{×,dR}_{FF,Y}/φ^ℤ realizes the Hyodo–Kato stack of 6.3 (ALRS Remark 3.5.6, p. 52, ALRS line 2743), that D^{×,dR}_{FF,(−)} commutes with colimits (ALRS Lemma 3.5.7, p. 53, ALRS line 2754), and that realization commutes with de Rham stacks, with D^×_{FF,𝒴^⋄} → 𝒴^real → (𝒴^dR)^real inducing equivalences on de Rham stacks, also for non-perfect analytic δ-stacks (ALRS Remark 3.5.8, p. 53, ALRS line 2764).
hypotheses: analytic δ-stacks as in 7.3; Y is an arc-stack over 𝔽_p

locator.where: Proposition 3.5.3, Definition 3.5.4, Remark 3.5.6, Lemma 3.5.7, p. 51; ALRS line 2685

tests.name: hk_point_delta
tests.statement: For Y = Marc(𝔽_p), (D^{×,dR}_{FF,Y})^real = Marc(ℚ_p)^dR = GSpec(ℚ_p), so Y^HK = GSpec(ℚ_p)/φ^ℤ as in 6.3.

tests.name: dR_product
tests.statement: D^×_{FF,Marc(K)×Marc(K)} = D^×_{FF,K} ×_{GSpec(ℚ_p)} D^×_{FF,K} for K = 𝔽_p((π^{1/p^∞})), from the finite-limit compatibility of D^×_{FF,(−)}, of realization (7.3) and the realization GSpec(ℚ_p) of the final object; the unpunctured product D_{FF,K} ×_{GSpec(ℚ_p)} D_{FF,K} is strictly larger, containing the points of radius (0, r) and (r, 0) coming from the radius-0 loci κ_ϖ⁻¹(0) of both factors.

tests.name: dR_final
tests.statement: D^{×,dR}_{FF,(−)} is a right adjoint and preserves the final object: D^{×,dR}_{FF,Marc(𝔽_p)} is the final perfect analytic δ-stack, consistent with its realization GSpec(ℚ_p).

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.perfFF_pullback
targets.statement: With Perf^{[n,m]} on Gelfand stacks as in 2.3 (AnalyticStacks §4.5), define the sheaf of categories Perf^{[n,m],FF} on perfect δ-spaces, (S, 𝒳) ↦ Perf^{[n,m]}(𝒳/φ^ℤ) (ALRS Definition 3.6.1, p. 53, ALRS line 2797). Prove that for a nilperfectoid (or uniformly perfectoid) A the square Perf(FF_A) → Perf(FF_{A^u}), Perf(GSpec A) → Perf(GSpec A^u) is cartesian; consequently A ↦ Perf(FF_A) is a sheaf of categories on Gelfand stacks and (Perf^≃_FF)^real = Perf^≃ ×_{Perf^{≃,dR}} (Perf^≃_FF)^{dR,real} (ALRS Proposition 3.6.3, p. 54, ALRS line 2822); the same holds for D^+ and fixed amplitudes (ALRS Remark 3.6.4, p. 54, ALRS line 2838), for Perf on perfect δ-spaces and on δ-spaces (ALRS Remark 3.6.7, p. 55, ALRS line 2857), and for global sections: Γ(FF_A, E) = Γ(FF_{A^u}, E) ×_{Γ(A^u, E)} Γ(A, E) (ALRS Corollary 3.6.5, p. 54, ALRS line 2841). For a strictly totally disconnected nilperfectoid A deduce Γ(GSpec A, O_{FF_A}) ≅ A ×_{A^u} ℚ_p^dR(A) = ℚ_p^la(A) (ALRS Example 3.6.6, p. 54, ALRS line 2847).
hypotheses: A is a nilperfectoid ℚ_p-algebra (or uniformly perfectoid)

locator.where: Proposition 3.6.3, Corollary 3.6.5, Example 3.6.6, p. 54; ALRS line 2822

tests.name: perfFF_perfectoid
tests.statement: For A perfectoid both horizontal maps are identities and the square is trivially cartesian.

tests.name: perfFF_thickenedCp
tests.statement: For A = C_p[ε]/ε², Γ(FF_A, O) = ℚ_p ×_{C_p} (C_p[ε]/ε²) = ℚ_p ⊕ C_p·ε, using Γ(FF_{C♭}, O) = ℚ_p.

tests.name: perfFF_laPoints
tests.statement: The value of ALRS Example 3.6.6 at A = C_p[ε]/ε² agrees with the computation ℚ_p^la(C_p[ε]/ε²) = ℚ_p ⊕ C_p·ε of 3.4.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.banachColmez
targets.statement: For λ ∈ ℚ let (D_λ, φ_{D_λ}) be the standard isocrystal of slope λ and, for a nilperfectoid A, O_{FF_A}(λ) the descent along D^×_{FF,A} → FF_A of O ⊗_{ℚ_p} D_{−λ}; define the absolute Banach–Colmez spaces BC(O(λ)): A ↦ Γ(FF_A, O(λ)) for λ ≥ 0 and BC(O(λ)[1]): A ↦ Γ(FF_A, O(λ)[1]) for λ < 0, and their incarnations BC_FF in PerfAnStk^δ with BC_FF(O(λ))^real = BC(O(λ)) (ALRS Definition 3.7.1, p. 55, ALRS line 2869; ALRS Remark 3.7.2, p. 55, ALRS line 2878). Prove 1 + D̃^{<1}_{ℚ_p} := lim_{x↦x^p}(1 + D^{<1}_{ℚ_p}) ≅ BC(O(1)) compatibly with the logarithm (ALRS Example 3.7.3, p. 55, ALRS line 2890), and: for λ ≥ 0, BC(O(λ)) = (G_a^an ⊗ D_{−λ}) ×_{G_a^{an,dR} ⊗ D_{−λ}} BC(O(λ))^dR, so BC(O) = ℚ_p^la and G_a^† ⊗ D_{−λ} → BC(O(λ)) → BC(O(λ))^dR is an extension of ℚ_p^la-modules; for λ < 0 the analogous square with B(G_a^dR ⊗ D_{−λ}) (ALRS Proposition 3.7.4, p. 56, ALRS line 2915); and BC_FF → BC_FF^dR is an epimorphism (ALRS Corollary 3.7.5, p. 56, ALRS line 2937). Prove that the de Rham stacks agree, after base change to Marc(ℚ_p), with the classical Banach–Colmez spaces BC of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals §VB3 (FS Proposition II.2.2, p. 60, FS line 2274).
hypotheses: λ ∈ ℚ; A ranges over nilperfectoid ℚ_p-algebras

locator.where: Definition 3.7.1, Example 3.7.3, Proposition 3.7.4, p. 55; ALRS line 2869

tests.name: bc_zero
tests.statement: BC(O) = ℚ_p^la and BC(O)^dR = ℚ_p^sm; the kernel of BC(O)(A) → BC(O)^dR(A) is Nil†(A), which is ℚ_p·ε for A = ℚ_p[ε]/ε².

tests.name: bc_one
tests.statement: BC(O(1))(C_p) = 1 + 𝔪_{C_p♭} as a group under multiplication, and its image under the logarithm of the first coordinate lands in C_p.

tests.name: bc_negative
tests.statement: For λ = −1, BC(O(−1)[1])^dR(C_p) = H¹(FF_{C♭}, O(−1)) = C_p/ℚ_p (FS Proposition II.2.5).

tests.name: bc_sign
tests.statement: Using D_λ instead of D_{−λ} would give O(1) the slope −1, with H⁰(FF_{C♭}, O(1)) = 0, contradicting BC(O(1)) = 1 + D̃^{<1}.

layers.title: The rational analytic prismatization and the p-adic twistor stack

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.RationalPrism
targets.statement: For a δ-space (S, 𝒳) call a Cartier divisor (s: L → O_𝒳) of degree one if its pullback to D^×_{FF,S} represents the closed Cartier divisor S^♯ → D^×_{FF,S} of an untilt S^♯ of S (FS Proposition II.1.18, p. 55, FS line 2105). A rational analytic prism (S, 𝒳, D) is a δ-space with a degree-one divisor D ⊆ 𝒳 (the map D → 𝒳 need not be a monomorphism). For a Gelfand stack X the rational analytic prismatic site X_{Δ-site} consists of tuples (S, 𝒳, D, α: D → X), with coverings induced by !-covers of (S, 𝒳); Q_{p,Δ} is the analytic δ-stack of degree-one divisors and X_Δ → Q_{p,Δ} the analytic δ-stack (S, 𝒳, D) ↦ Map(D, X) (ALRS Definition 4.1.1(1)–(4), p. 57, ALRS line 2953). Prove rigidity: for a morphism of prisms (S′, 𝒳′, D′) → (S, 𝒳, D), D′ → D ×_𝒳 𝒳′ is an isomorphism (ALRS Remark 4.1.2(3), p. 57, ALRS line 2988).
hypotheses: (S, 𝒳) is a rational δ-space; X is a Gelfand stack

locator.where: Definition 4.1.1(1)–(4), Remark 4.1.2(3), p. 57; ALRS line 2953

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.RationalPrism.pullback
api.statement: The pullback of a degree-one divisor along a morphism of δ-spaces is of degree one, giving the δ-stack Q_{p,Δ}.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.RationalPrism.rigid
api.statement: For a morphism of prisms, D′ ≅ D ×_𝒳 𝒳′.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.RationalPrism.untilt
api.statement: On the classical δ-space (S, D^×_{FF,S}), degree-one divisors are the untilt divisors of RelativeFarguesFontaine §3.2 and FarguesFontaineDiamonds §F4.

tests.name: prism_cyclotomic
tests.statement: On X_cyc = (lim_{x↦x^p} 1 + D^{<1}_{ℚ_p}) ∖ {1}, the divisor of [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) has degree one, with D = GSpec(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})) uncompleted (ALRS Example 4.1.7(1)).

tests.name: prism_unit
tests.statement: On X_cyc the divisor of q − 1 is empty, since q = 1 is excluded from X_cyc, so it is not of degree one.

tests.name: prism_square
tests.statement: The divisor of [p]_q² pulls back to twice an untilt divisor and is not of degree one.

tests.name: prism_breuilKisin
tests.statement: On lim_{x↦x^p} D^{<1}_{ℚ_p} ∖ {0} with φ(X) = X^p, the divisor of X − p has degree one, with D = GSpec(ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})) (ALRS Example 4.1.7(2)).

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.prismatization
targets.statement: For a Gelfand stack X define the rational analytic prismatization X^Δ as the realization of X_Δ, equivalently the sheafification of the functor sending a nilperfectoid A over Q_p^Δ = GSpec(ℚ_p)^Δ to Map(D, X), D ⊆ 𝒳_{GSpec A} the classified degree-one divisor; the rational perfect analytic prismatization X^{Div¹~} = lim_φ X^Δ; and the p-adic twistor stack X^{Div¹} = X^{Div¹~}/φ^ℤ, with Div¹~ = (Q_p^Δ)^{Div¹~} and Div¹ = Div¹~/φ (ALRS Definition 4.1.1(5)–(7), p. 57, ALRS line 2965). Construct the natural map X^Δ → A¹/G_m from the divisor {0} × T ⊂ ℕ × T → 𝒳_T and the analytic Hodge–Tate stack X^HT = X^Δ ×_{A¹/G_m} BG_m (ALRS Definition 4.1.4, p. 58, ALRS line 3010). Prove that X ↦ X_Δ is right adjoint to the colimit-preserving functor (S, 𝒳, D) ↦ D and commutes with fibre products (ALRS Remark 4.1.2(2), p. 57, ALRS line 2980), that the perfect prismatic site gives a perfect δ-stack with (X^{Div¹~})^real → X^{Div¹~} an equivalence for †-cohesive X (ALRS Remark 4.1.2(4), p. 57, ALRS line 2993), and construct the maps 𝒳 → D^Δ → Q_p^Δ attached to a prism (ALRS Remark 4.1.6, p. 58, ALRS line 3017) and the relative prismatization Y^{Δ/𝒳} = Y^Δ ×_{D^Δ} 𝒳 and relative Hodge–Tate stack Y^{HT/D} = Y^{Δ/𝒳} ×_𝒳 D over a prism (ALRS Definition 4.1.8, p. 59, ALRS line 3048).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; Y is a Gelfand stack over D for the relative version

locator.where: Definition 4.1.1(5)–(7), Definition 4.1.4, Definition 4.1.8, p. 57; ALRS line 2965

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.prismatization_fiberProduct
api.statement: (X ×_Z Y)^Δ = X^Δ ×_{Z^Δ} Y^Δ, and likewise for X^{Div¹~}, X^{Div¹} and X^HT.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.prismatization_frobenius
api.statement: X^Δ carries a Frobenius φ over the Frobenius of Q_p^Δ; X^{Div¹~} is its perfection and X^{Div¹} the quotient by φ^ℤ.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.toA1Gm
api.statement: The map X^Δ → A¹/G_m is the pullback of the classified divisor along {0} × T → 𝒳_T; the resulting divisor X^HT ⊆ X^Δ is the Hodge–Tate divisor.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.prism_toPrismatization
api.statement: A prism (S, 𝒳, D) gives maps 𝒳 → D^Δ → Q_p^Δ sending D to D^HT → Q_p^HT.

tests.name: prismatization_empty
tests.statement: ∅^Δ = ∅ and GSpec(ℚ_p)^Δ = Q_p^Δ.

tests.name: prismatization_cyclotomicSquare
tests.statement: The cyclotomic prism gives a cartesian square GSpec(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})) = X_cyc ×_{Q_p^Δ} Q_p^HT (ALRS Example 4.1.7(1)).

tests.name: prismatization_HTnotCartier
tests.statement: The map {0} × T → 𝒳_T is not itself a Cartier divisor; for D ∈ Q_p^HT(A) the map T → D is a derived thickening with fibre sequence Nil†(A)[1] → O_D → A (ALRS Remark 4.1.5), so X^HT must be defined through A¹/G_m.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.prismatization_deRham
targets.statement: Prove that (X_Δ)^⋄_FF = X^⋄, so that X^dR_Δ = D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄} over Q^dR_{p,Δ} (ALRS Lemma 4.2.1, p. 59, ALRS line 3062), giving maps D^×_{FF,X^⋄} → X^Δ → D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄} inducing equivalences on de Rham stacks (ALRS Remark 4.2.2, p. 59, ALRS line 3069); that X^{Div¹~,dR} → X^{Δ,dR} and colim_φ X^Δ → X^{Δ,dR} are isomorphisms and X^{Div¹~,dR} ≅ D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄} (ALRS Proposition 4.2.3, p. 59, ALRS line 3080); that for a perfectoid space Y over ℚ_p the map π_Y: Y^HT → Y, sending a point (D, T → D → FF_A, D → Y) to the composite T → D → Y, is an isomorphism (ALRS Proposition 4.2.4, p. 59, ALRS line 3094); and that for a †-formally étale X′ → X, X′^Δ = X^Δ ×_{D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄}} D^{×,dR}_{FF,X′^⋄}, so X ↦ X^Δ satisfies descent for †-formally étale hypercovers (ALRS Lemma 4.2.5, p. 60, ALRS line 3118).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; Y is a perfectoid space over ℚ_p; X′ → X is †-formally étale

locator.where: Lemma 4.2.1, Propositions 4.2.3–4.2.4, Lemma 4.2.5, p. 59; ALRS line 3062

tests.name: HT_perfectoid
tests.statement: For Y = GSpec(C_p), Y^HT = GSpec(C_p).

tests.name: twistor_notFF
tests.statement: For a perfectoid Y over ℚ_p, Y^{Div¹} and FF_Y are not isomorphic (ALRS line 3114), in contrast with the p-complete prismatization of perfectoids.

tests.name: deRham_thickening_prism
tests.statement: GSpec(ℚ_p[ε]/ε²) and GSpec(ℚ_p) have the same de Rham stack of the prismatization, D^{×,dR}_{FF,Marc(ℚ_p)}, although their prismatizations differ.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisin_cone
targets.statement: Let I_Δ be the ideal sheaf of the Hodge–Tate locus and define the Breuil–Kisin ideal I_BK = ⊗_{n∈ℕ} (φ^n)^* I_Δ, a line bundle on Q_p^Δ (the product is locally finite, since locally all but finitely many factors are trivial), with Breuil–Kisin divisor μ_BK: Q_p^Δ → A¹/G_m (ALRS Definition 4.2.7, p. 61, ALRS line 3166; ALRS Remark 4.2.8, p. 61, ALRS line 3175). Prove that the pullback of μ_BK along 𝒳_T → Q_p^Δ is D_BK = ⊔_{n∈ℕ} φ^{n,*}D, the Frobenius translates being disjoint (ALRS Lemma 4.2.10, p. 62, ALRS line 3217). Prove that for †-cohesive X, X^Δ is admissible and the diagram (4.2.2) is cartesian (ALRS Lemma 4.2.6, p. 61, ALRS line 3154), and that the square with corners X^Δ, D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄}, X^cone, (X^cone)^dR, through μ_BK: X^Δ → X^cone ×_{A¹/G_m, μ_BK} Q_p^Δ, is cartesian, so that μ_BK is †-formally étale (ALRS Proposition 4.2.11, p. 62, ALRS line 3250).
hypotheses: X is a †-cohesive Gelfand stack for the cartesian statements

locator.where: Definition 4.2.7, Lemmas 4.2.6, 4.2.10, Proposition 4.2.11, p. 61; ALRS line 3166

tests.name: BK_cyclotomic
tests.statement: On X_cyc, μ_BK pulls back to the ideal generated by log(q)/(q − 1): log(q) has simple zeros at all p-power roots of unity, and dividing by q − 1 removes q = 1, leaving the zeros of [p]_{q^{p^n}}, n ≥ 0 (ALRS Proposition 4.8.1(3)).

tests.name: BK_disjoint
tests.statement: The translates φ^{n,*}D and φ^{m,*}D for n ≠ m have disjoint supports because the radius map multiplies by p under Frobenius (6.1).

tests.name: BK_ZnotN
tests.statement: On Q_p^Δ only the pullbacks φ^{n,*} with n ≥ 0 exist, because φ is not invertible on the δ-spaces 𝒳_T; the ℤ-indexed product ⊗_{n∈ℤ} φ^n(I_Δ) exists only on the perfection Div¹~, where it is the perfected twist of 9.8.

tests.name: BK_trivialDivisor
tests.statement: Over the open complement Q_p^Δ ∖ ⋃_n φ^{-n}(Q_p^HT) the Breuil–Kisin ideal is trivial.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.radius_decomposition
targets.statement: Construct the radius map κ: X^Δ → (0, ∞) through X^Δ → (D^×_{FF,X^⋄})^dR (ALRS Remark 4.2.12, p. 63, ALRS line 3287). Prove that for †-cohesive X: (1) X^Δ → (D^×_{FF,X^⋄})^dR is an isomorphism over (1, ∞), so φ induces X^Δ_{(1,∞)} ≅ X^Δ_{(p,∞)} with coequalizer X^HK; (2) X^{Div¹~} → X^Δ is an isomorphism over (0, p), so φ induces X^Δ_{(0,1)} ≅ X^Δ_{(0,p)} with coequalizer X^{Div¹} (ALRS Proposition 4.2.13, p. 63, ALRS line 3309); and X^Δ ≅ X^{Div¹~}_{(0,p)} ⊔_{X^{Div¹~}_{(1,p)}} (D^{×,dR}_{FF,X^⋄})_{(1,∞)} (ALRS Corollary 4.2.14, p. 64, ALRS line 3362). The two radius functions are reciprocal: a divisor D ⊆ 𝒳_T lands in 𝒳_{T,(r,s)} if and only if the corresponding point of X^Δ lands in X^Δ_{(1/s,1/r)} (ALRS Proposition 4.2.13, proof, p. 64, ALRS line 3327).
hypotheses: X is a †-cohesive Gelfand stack

locator.where: Remark 4.2.12, Proposition 4.2.13, Corollary 4.2.14, p. 63; ALRS line 3309

tests.name: radius_HT
tests.statement: The Hodge–Tate locus of X^Δ lies at κ = 1 and its n-th inverse Frobenius translate at κ = p^{-n}, whereas the n-th copy of T in 𝒳_T lies at radius p^n.

tests.name: radius_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), Q^Δ_{p,(1,∞)} = (D^×_{FF,Marc(ℚ_p)})^dR_{(1,∞)} and the coequalizer over (1, ∞) is Q_p^HK = GSpec(ℚ_p)^HK.

tests.name: radius_reversed
tests.statement: Using the radius of 𝒳_T instead of that of X^Δ would place the Hodge–Tate locus at p^n for n ≥ 0 and exchange the roles of (0, p) and (1, ∞) in ALRS Proposition 4.2.13.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.twistor_square
targets.statement: Construct the factorization FF_{X^⋄} → X^{Div¹} → FF^dR_{X^⋄} = X^HK of the natural map from the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve to its de Rham stack (ALRS (4.3.1), p. 65, ALRS line 3392). Prove that restriction of degree-one divisors on FF_A to GSpec(A) and FF_{A^u} gives a commutative square X^{Div¹} → X^HK over X^cone → (X^cone)^dR, cartesian when X is †-cohesive (ALRS Proposition 4.3.1, p. 65, ALRS line 3396), and that X^{Div¹} → X^HK is an isomorphism after base change to Div¹ ∖ Q_p^HT ≅ Div^{1,dR} ∖ GSpec(ℚ_p) (ALRS Proposition 4.3.2, p. 65, ALRS line 3406).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; †-cohesive for the cartesian square

locator.where: (4.3.1), Propositions 4.3.1–4.3.2, p. 65; ALRS line 3396

tests.name: twistor_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p) the square reads Div¹ = A¹/G_m ×_{A^{1,dR}/G_m^dR} Q_p^HK (ALRS Proposition 4.8.1(1)).

tests.name: twistor_generic
tests.statement: Over the complement of the Hodge–Tate locus, vector bundles on X^{Div¹} are vector bundles on X^HK, i.e. analytic D-modules on FF_{X^⋄} ∖ X^⋄.

tests.name: twistor_empty
tests.statement: For X = ∅ all four corners are empty.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.descent
targets.statement: Prove: (1) if f: Y → X is †-formally étale locally †-formally smooth, then f^Δ, f^{Div¹~} and f^{Div¹} are weakly †-formally smooth; (2) if moreover f is an arc-cover they are epimorphisms; (3) if f is †-formally smooth and Y, X are †-cohesive they are †-formally smooth (ALRS Theorem 4.7.1, p. 78, ALRS line 4040). In particular the prismatization, its perfection and the twistor stack satisfy descent along rigid étale covers and Tate-rational covers of smooth rigid spaces.
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of Gelfand stacks, †-formally étale locally †-formally smooth

locator.where: Theorem 4.7.1, p. 78; ALRS line 4040

tests.name: descent_rigidEtale
tests.statement: A rigid étale cover of a smooth rigid space by charts étale over G_m^d is †-formally étale (4.2) and an arc-cover, so the twistor stacks of the charts cover X^{Div¹}.

tests.name: descent_notCover
tests.statement: An open immersion that is not surjective is †-formally étale but not an arc-cover, and the induced map of prismatizations is not an epimorphism.

tests.name: descent_identity
tests.statement: The identity satisfies all hypotheses and its induced maps are isomorphisms.

layers.title: Hodge–Tate geometry, Faltings' extension and explicit computations

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.hodgeTate_gerbe
targets.statement: Let I_{Div¹} be the ideal of the Hodge–Tate divisor Q_p^HT → Div¹ and I its restriction to Q_p^HT (ALRS Definition 4.4.1, p. 65, ALRS line 3413). Prove that for a nilperfectoid A, a degree-one divisor D → FF_T and a factorization T → D → FF_T through the Hodge–Tate locus, O(D) → A is a square-zero extension with ideal Nil†(A) ⊗_A I_A[1], classified by the derivation d̃: A → A ⊕ Nil†(A) ⊗ I_A[2] obtained from the derivation of A^u attached to B⁺_dR(A^u)/ξ² → A^u through the connecting map of I_A[1] → I_{A^u}[1] → Nil†(A) ⊗ I_A[2] (ALRS Lemma 4.4.2, p. 65, ALRS line 3417); thus G_a^HT is a square-zero extension of G_a × Q_p^HT by G_a^†{1}[1]. Prove that for a Gelfand stack X there is a natural map π_X: X^HT → X × Q_p^HT through X^cone_s; that for †-cohesive X with a cotangent complex the square X^HT → X^dR over X^cone_s → (X^cone_s)^dR is cartesian and π_X is a principal homogeneous space for the overconvergent shifted twisted tangent complex (T_X[1]{1})^†; and that π_X is the fibre of a derivation d̃_X: X × Q_p^HT → (T_X{1}[2])^†, so that for formally smooth X with tangent bundle T_X, π_X is an epimorphism and a gerbe banded by T_X^†{1}, where {1} is the twist by I (ALRS Proposition 4.4.3, p. 66, ALRS line 3481).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack; †-cohesive with a cotangent complex for (2); formally smooth for the gerbe statement

locator.where: Definition 4.4.1, Lemma 4.4.2, Proposition 4.4.3, p. 66; ALRS line 3481

tests.name: HT_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), T_X = 0 and π_X is the identity of Q_p^HT.

tests.name: HT_line
tests.statement: For X = A¹, X^HT → A¹ × Q_p^HT is a gerbe banded by G_a^†{1}.

tests.name: HT_perfectoid
tests.statement: For Y = GSpec(C_p), L_{C_p/ℚ_p} = C_p(1)[1] (4.5) gives T_Y[1]{1} = O, the twists cancelling; Y × Q_p^HT is a G_m^† ≅ G_a^†-gerbe over Y, and π_Y makes Y^HT a torsor over it under (T_Y[1]{1})^† = G_a^†, which trivializes the gerbe, so Y^HT ≅ Y as in 8.3.

tests.name: HT_twist
tests.statement: For X = A¹ the band restricted over the origin is G_a^†{1} = G_a^† ⊗ I on Q_p^HT, whose arithmetic Sen weight is 1 because I ≅ Ô(1) (9.7, 11.2); the untwisted band G_a^† has Sen weight 0, so the twist {1} is detected by the Sen operator.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.hodgeTate_relative
targets.statement: Let (S, 𝒳, D) be a perfect analytic prism and X → D a †-cohesive map of Gelfand stacks. Prove that the squares relating X^{Div¹/𝒳}, X^{HK/𝒳}, X^HK, X^{cone/(D,𝒳/φ^ℤ)} and its relative and absolute de Rham stacks are cartesian, and that if X admits a cotangent complex then X^{HT/D} = X ×_{(T_{X/D}{1}[2])^†} X along 0 and the derivation d̃_X, so that for X → D formally smooth X^{HT/D} → X is a gerbe banded by T^†_{X/D}{1}, {1} being the twist by the ideal of D ⊆ 𝒳 (ALRS Proposition 4.4.4, p. 68, ALRS line 3535). For formally smooth X → D prove that the pushout of X^{HT/D} along BT^†_{X/D}{1} → BT_{X/D}{1} is the stack of square-zero lifts of X to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood D(1) (ALRS Remark 4.4.5, p. 68, ALRS line 3552).
hypotheses: (S, 𝒳, D) is a perfect analytic prism; X → D is †-cohesive with a cotangent complex

locator.where: Proposition 4.4.4, Remark 4.4.5, p. 68; ALRS line 3535

tests.name: relHT_identity
tests.statement: For X = D, T_{X/D} = 0 and X^{HT/D} = D.

tests.name: relHT_curve
tests.statement: For a smooth curve X over a perfectoid field C with prism given by FF_{C♭} and the untilt C, X^{HT/C} is a gerbe banded by T^†_X{1}, and its pushout to T_X{1} is the gerbe of lifts of X to B⁺_dR(C)/ξ².

tests.name: relHT_nonsplit
tests.statement: The relative Hodge–Tate gerbe need not split, in contrast with the archimedean Hodge stack (ALRS Remark 1.14); the two are distinguished by the twist {1}.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.hodgeTate_descent
targets.statement: Prove that if f: Y → X is an infinitesimally cohesive epimorphism of Gelfand stacks with a cotangent complex L_{Y/X} perfect of amplitude [−1, 0], then f^HT: Y^HT → X^HT is an epimorphism (ALRS Theorem 4.7.2, p. 78, ALRS line 4062). In particular Hodge–Tate stacks satisfy descent along formally étale !-covers such as Tate-rational covers, which propagates 9.1 from smooth affinoids to smooth rigid spaces (ALRS footnote 27, p. 69, ALRS line 3631).
hypotheses: f is an epimorphism, infinitesimally cohesive, with L_{Y/X} perfect of amplitude [−1, 0]

locator.where: Theorem 4.7.2, p. 78; ALRS line 4062

tests.name: HTdescent_tate
tests.statement: A Tate-rational cover of a smooth affinoid has L = 0 and is an epimorphism, so the Hodge–Tate stacks of its pieces cover X^HT.

tests.name: HTdescent_closedPoint
tests.statement: The zero section 0 → A¹ has L = ℚ_p[1] of amplitude [−1, 0] but is not an epimorphism; its Hodge–Tate map misses the points of A¹^HT over A¹ ∖ {0}.

tests.name: HTdescent_identity
tests.statement: The identity has L = 0 and induces an isomorphism.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.hodgeTate_formal
targets.statement: Define the overconvergent and formal Hodge–Tate stacks X^{†-HT} = X^{Div¹} ×_{A¹/G_m} A^{1,†}/G_m and X^{HT^} = X^{Div¹} ×_{A¹/G_m} Â¹/G_m, and their relative versions over a perfect prism (ALRS Definition 4.5.1, p. 69, ALRS line 3602). Prove that for †-cohesive X the squares relating X^{HT^}, X^{†-HT}, X^dR, X^{cone^}, X^{†-cone} and (X^cone_s)^dR are cartesian, and that for formally smooth X with a cotangent complex X^dR → (X^cone_s)^dR = (X/T_X(−1) ⋊ G_m)^dR is a (T_X(−1) ⋊ G_m)^dR-torsor, hence so are X^{HT^} → X^{cone^} and X^{†-HT} → X^{†-cone} (ALRS Proposition 4.5.2, p. 69, ALRS line 3614); prove the relative version over a perfect prism, with a T_{X/D}{1}^dR-torsor (ALRS Proposition 4.5.3, p. 69, ALRS line 3630).
hypotheses: X is †-cohesive; formally smooth with a cotangent complex for the torsor statements

locator.where: Definition 4.5.1, Propositions 4.5.2–4.5.3, p. 69; ALRS line 3602

tests.name: formalHT_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), Q_p^{HT^} = Spf(K_∞[[t]])/ℤ_p^{×,la} with K_∞ = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}), because (B⁺_dR(ℚ_p^cyc)/t^n)^la = K_∞[t]/t^n (ALRS §6.7, line 9169).

tests.name: formalHT_dagger
tests.statement: The formal and overconvergent Hodge–Tate stacks differ: the formal one sees only nilpotent thickenings of the divisor, the overconvergent one its †-neighbourhood; for non-Berkovich X only the formal statement of 9.6 holds.

tests.name: formalHT_empty
tests.statement: For X = ∅ all stacks are empty.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.faltingsExtension
targets.statement: For a smooth rigid space X over ℚ_p define Faltings' extension FE_X as the extension 0 → O_{X̂^⋄}{1} → FE_X → Ω¹_X ⊗ O_{X̂^⋄} → 0 on X̂^⋄ whose T_X{1}-torsor is X̂^⋄ ×_{X^cone_s} (X × BG_m), for the map X × BG_m → X^cone_s of ALRS Lemma 2.8.6 and X̂^⋄ → X^HT → X^cone_s; for a smoothoid X over an affinoid perfectoid D with a lift X̃ to B⁺_dR(D)/ξ², define FE^{X̃}_X through X̂^⋄ ×_{X^{cone/(D,FF_D)}_s} X (ALRS Definition 4.6.1, p. 70, ALRS line 3674). Prove that X̂^⋄ → FF^∧_{X^⋄} ×_{X^dR} X is, locally on the pro-étale site X_proét^{ω₁}, a regular closed immersion with formal completion Spf(OB⁺_dR,X) (ALRS Lemma 4.6.4, p. 73, ALRS line 3819), so that L_{X̂^⋄/X} ≅ gr¹(OB⁺_dR,X)[1] (ALRS Remark 4.6.5, p. 74, ALRS line 3876); that, writing Spf^{≥0} for spectra of ℕ-filtrations (ALRS Construction 4.6.6, p. 75, ALRS line 3891), Spf^{≥0}(B⁺_dR,X) is the algebraic formal cone of X̂^⋄ and Spf^{≥0}(B⁺_dR,X) ×_{X^{cone-alg^}} (X × Â¹/G_m^alg) = Spf^{≥0}(OB⁺_dR,X) (ALRS Proposition 4.6.8, p. 75, ALRS line 3920); and that X̂^⋄ ×_{X^cone_s} (X × BG_m) ≅ (AnSpec(OC_X))^Gelf, so that FE_X is the classical Faltings' extension 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr¹OB⁺_dR,X → Ô_X ⊗ Ω¹_X → 0 of PadicHodgeTheory §2.3 (ALRS Corollary 4.6.10, p. 76, ALRS line 3966; Sch13 Corollary 6.14, p. 39, Sch13 line 1787).
hypotheses: X is a smooth rigid space over ℚ_p (absolute case); X is smoothoid over an affinoid perfectoid D with a lift X̃ to B⁺_dR(D)/ξ² (relative case)

locator.where: Definition 4.6.1, Lemma 4.6.4, Proposition 4.6.8, Corollary 4.6.10, p. 70; ALRS line 3674

tests.name: FE_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p) one has Ω¹ = 0 and FE_X = O_{X̂^⋄}{1}.

tests.name: FE_torus
tests.statement: For X = G_m with the toric cover T^{1/p^∞}, the class log([T♭]/T) in gr¹OB⁺_dR lifts dT/T and the generator γ of ℤ_p(1) moves it by t = log[ε]; the cocycle γ ↦ t is a nonzero class in H¹(ℤ_p(1), Ĉ(1)), so FE_X is a non-split Galois-equivariant extension.

tests.name: FE_twist
tests.statement: The subobject is O{1} = Ô(1), not Ô: the cocycle γ ↦ t takes values in the Tate twist, and an extension of Ô ⊗ Ω¹ by Ô would have an equivariant splitting on the toric cover.

tests.name: FE_cotangent
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), L_{X̂^⋄/X} = gr¹(B⁺_dR(C_p))[1] = C_p(1)[1], matching 4.5.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.formalHT_square
targets.statement: Prove that for a smooth rigid space X over ℚ_p there is a cartesian square X^{HT^} → X^dR over X^{cone^} → (X^cone_s)^dR = (X^cone)^dR ×_{(A¹/G_m)^dR} BG_m^dR, where the lower right term is the classifying stack B_{X^dR × BG_m^dR}T_X{1}^dR, the map X^dR → BG_m^dR is the Tate twist, and the T_X{1}^⋄-torsor on X^⋄ given by the right vertical map is Faltings' extension; if X is a Berkovich space the formal completion may be replaced by the overconvergent neighbourhood (ALRS Corollary 4.6.11, p. 77, ALRS line 3985). Prove the relative version for a smoothoid X over a perfectoid D with a smooth lift X̃ to B⁺_dR(D)/t², with FE^{X̃}_X and relative de Rham stacks over D^∧ (or D^†) (ALRS Corollary 4.6.12, p. 77, ALRS line 3999).
hypotheses: X is a smooth rigid space over ℚ_p; relative case: X smoothoid over a perfectoid D with a smooth lift to B⁺_dR(D)/t²

locator.where: Corollaries 4.6.11–4.6.12, p. 77; ALRS line 3985

tests.name: formalSquare_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), T_X = 0 and the square reads Q_p^{HT^} = Â¹/G_m ×_{BG_m^dR} GSpec(ℚ_p), the map GSpec(ℚ_p) → BG_m^dR being the Tate twist (9.7).

tests.name: formalSquare_torsor
tests.statement: For X = G_m the T_X{1}^⋄-torsor is the torsor of lifts of dT/T in gr¹OB⁺_dR, the class computed in 9.5.

tests.name: formalSquare_nonBerkovich
tests.statement: For a smooth rigid space which is not a Berkovich space (not partially proper and not affinoid) only the formal version is asserted.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.qp_prismatization
targets.statement: Let 1 + D̃^{<1}_{ℚ_p} = lim_{x↦x^p}(1 + D^{<1}_{ℚ_p}) with coordinate q and Frobenius q ↦ q^p, and let (S_cyc, X_cyc, I) be the cyclotomic prism with divisor ([p]_q). Prove: (1) the square Q_p^Δ → Q_p^{Δ,dR} over μ_BK: A¹/G_m → A^{1,dR}/G_m^dR is cartesian; (2) the square Q_p^HT → GSpec(ℚ_p) over ι: BG_m → BG_m^dR is cartesian, so π_{ℚ_p}: Q_p^HT → GSpec(ℚ_p) is a BG_m^†-torsor, a gerbe banded by G_m^†; (3) along X_cyc → Q_p^Δ, I_BK pulls back to (log(q)/(q − 1)) and I_Δ along X_cyc → Div¹~ → Div¹ to (log q); (4) X_cyc → Div¹~ induces Div¹~ ≅ X_cyc/ℤ_p^{×,la} with a·(q, q^{1/p}, …) = (q^a, q^{a/p}, …), hence Div¹ ≅ X_cyc/ℚ_p^{×,la} and Q_p^HT ≅ GSpec(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}))/ℤ_p^{×,la}, the action factoring through the Galois action of ℤ_p^{×,sm} via the cyclotomic character; and the cartesian square of 8.6 becomes ((1 + D̃^{<1}) ∖ {1})/ℚ_p^{×,la} over A¹/G_m via log (ALRS Proposition 4.8.1, p. 79, ALRS line 4112). Prove that ι^dR: GSpec(ℚ_p) → BG_m^dR is classified by the Tate twist Ô ⊗ ℚ_p(1) ≅ gr¹B⁺_dR on Spa(ℚ_p)_proét (ALRS §4.8, p. 81, ALRS line 4202), and that D^×_{FF,ℚ_p^cyc} → (1 + D̃^{<1}_{ℚ_p}) ∖ {1}, q ↦ [ε^{1/p}], is Γ-equivariant through χ and sends the prism ideal to the ideal of the untilt ℚ_p^cyc (ALRS Example 4.8.4, p. 81, ALRS line 4206).
hypotheses: p is any prime; ℤ_p^{×,la} and ℚ_p^{×,la} are the locally analytic groups of 3.4

locator.where: Proposition 4.8.1, Example 4.8.4, p. 79; ALRS line 4112

tests.name: qp_HT_gerbe
tests.statement: Q_p^HT → GSpec(ℚ_p) is a gerbe banded by G_m^† ≅ G_a^† (via exp and log on the overconvergent neighbourhood of 1); compare AHLB Theorem 1.2, where the integral Hodge–Tate stack of ℤ_p is BG_m^♯ (AHLB line 42), and PrismaticCohomologyPartII §4.12, where WCart^HT ≅ Spf ℤ_p × BG_m^♯: the rational analytic theory replaces G_m^♯ by G_m^†.

tests.name: qp_action
tests.statement: An element a ∈ ℤ_p^× acts on X_cyc by q^{1/p^n} ↦ q^{a/p^n}; the element p of ℚ_p^× acts by the Frobenius q ↦ q^p.

tests.name: qp_sen
tests.statement: The pullback of I to Q_p^HT is Ĉ(1); its arithmetic Sen operator (11.2) is multiplication by 1, matching the convention Θ_{O{n}} = n of PrismaticCohomologyPartII §4.13 and HT(χ_p) = +1 of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.P7.2.

tests.name: qp_notCompleted
tests.statement: The upper-left corner of the cyclotomic square is the uncompleted GSpec(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})), not GSpec(ℚ_p^cyc); the completed field gives the perfectoid Hodge–Tate stack of 8.3 instead.

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisinTwist
targets.statement: Let O_{Q_p^Δ}⟨1⟩ be the pullback along Q_p^Δ → D^{×,dR}_{FF,Marc(ℚ_p)} of the line bundle of the isocrystal (ℚ_p, p^{-1}φ), a φ-equivariant line bundle. Define the Breuil–Kisin twist O_{Q_p^Δ}{1} = I_BK ⊗ O⟨1⟩ with its Frobenius φ^*I_BK ≅ I_Δ^{-1} I_BK, and O{n} = O{1}^{⊗n} (ALRS Construction 4.9.1, p. 82, ALRS line 4233). Construct the perfected twist O_{Div¹~}{1} = ⊗_{n∈ℤ} φ^n(I_Δ) with Frobenius structure, descending to O_{Div¹}{1} = I_{Div¹}⟨1⟩ on Div¹; prove that its pullback along FF_{Q_p^⋄} → Div¹ is the Tate twist ℚ_p(1) as a pro-étale local system, whereas O_{Div¹}⟨1⟩ pulls back to the line bundle of Frobenius slope one (ALRS Remark 4.9.3, p. 82, ALRS line 4278). Compare with the integral Breuil–Kisin twist of PrismaticCohomologyPartII §3.9, built as a limit of I_k/I_k² along transition maps divided by p, which correspond rationally to the twist by O⟨1⟩ (ALRS Remark 4.9.2, p. 82, ALRS line 4239).
hypotheses: twists over Q_p^Δ, Div¹~ and Div¹ and their pullbacks to Gelfand stacks over them

locator.where: Construction 4.9.1, Remarks 4.9.2–4.9.3, p. 82; ALRS line 4233

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisinTwist_frobenius
api.statement: O{1} carries the φ-structure φ^*O{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O{1} obtained from φ^*I_BK ≅ I_Δ^{-1}I_BK and the slope twist of O⟨1⟩.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisinTwist_HT
api.statement: The restriction of O{1} to Q_p^HT is the conormal ideal I ≅ Ô(1) of the Hodge–Tate divisor.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisinTwist_FF
api.statement: The pullback of O_{Div¹}{1} to FF_{Q_p^⋄} is the Tate twist O ⊗ ℚ_p(1), a slope-zero line bundle; the pullback of O_{Div¹}⟨1⟩ has slope one.

api.name: TauCeti.Prism.breuilKisinTwist_tensor
api.statement: O{m} ⊗ O{n} ≅ O{m + n} and O{0} = O, compatibly with Frobenius structures.

tests.name: BK_qdeRham
tests.statement: On the cyclotomic prism, e = (log q/(q − 1)) ⊗ e⟨1⟩ generates O{1}, and φ(log q/(q − 1)) = p·log q/(q^p − 1) = p·[p]_q^{-1}·log q/(q − 1), while φ(e⟨1⟩) = p^{-1}e⟨1⟩; hence φ(e) = [p]_q^{-1}·e, matching [p]_q·φ(e) = e of PrismaticCohomologyPartII §3.9.

tests.name: BK_untwisted
tests.statement: Without the factor O⟨1⟩ the generator would satisfy φ(e′) = p·[p]_q^{-1}·e′, off by p from the integral normalization.

tests.name: BK_zero
tests.statement: O{0} = O with the identity Frobenius structure.

tests.name: BK_slope
tests.statement: Away from the Hodge–Tate locus I is trivial and O{1} ≅ O⟨1⟩, matching the dualizing complexes of 12.2 on Div¹ ∖ Q_p^HT ≅ Div^{1,dR} ∖ GSpec(ℚ_p).

targets.name: TauCeti.Prism.prismaticLogarithm
targets.statement: Let G̃_m = lim_{x↦x^p} G_m and ℤ_p(1)^sm = fib(G̃_m → G_m). Prove G̃_m ≅ G̃_m^dR ×_{G_m^dR} G_m (ALRS Lemma 4.10.2, p. 84, ALRS line 4348); construct the φ-equivariant Teichmüller map of commutative group stacks ρ: G̃_{m,Q_p^Δ} → G_m^Δ (ALRS Construction 4.10.3, p. 84, ALRS line 4355) and prove that ρ is an epimorphism with G_m^Δ = G̃_{m,Q_p^Δ}/G, G = fib(ρ), with cartesian squares relating G, (1 + D̃^{<1}) ×_{GSpec ℚ_p} Q_p^Δ and (1 + D^{<1})^Δ (ALRS Lemma 4.10.4, p. 85, ALRS line 4403). Define the prismatic logarithm as the unique φ-equivariant map of commutative group stacks log_Δ: G → G_{a,Q_p^Δ}{1} fitting in the diagram of fibre sequences with β = log ∘ pr_1 twisted by ⟨1⟩ and γ = (log)^cone ∘ μ_BK (ALRS Construction 4.10.5, p. 86, ALRS line 4454). Prove that log_Δ is †-formally étale, with a fibre square over its de Rham stack and an exact sequence 0 → G_a^† ⊗ G_{a,Q_p^Δ}{1} → G → ℤ_p(1)^sm → 0 (ALRS Theorem 4.10.6, p. 87, ALRS line 4494); that the logarithm induces fibre sequences with rows G → (1 + D̃^{<1})_{Q_p^Δ} → (1 + D^{<1})^Δ and G[1/p] → (1 + D̃^{<1})_{Q_p^Δ} → G_a^Δ, recovering on arc-stacks 0 → ℚ_p(1) → BC(O(1)) → G_a → 0 (ALRS Lemma 4.10.10, p. 89, ALRS line 4599); and that over the cyclotomic prism the section q♭ = (q, q^{1/p}, …) gives G^{Div¹~}|_{X_cyc} ≅ q^{ℤ_p^la}, the action on G̃_{m,X_cyc} with coordinate T is a·T^{1/p^n} = q^{a/p^n}T^{1/p^n}, G_m^{Div¹~/X_cyc} ≅ G̃_{m,X_cyc}/ℤ_p^la, and G_m^{Div¹~} ≅ G̃_{m,X_cyc}/(ℤ_p^{×,la} ⋉ ℤ_p^la) with (a, b)·(q♭, T♭) = (q♭^a, q♭^b T♭) (ALRS Theorem 4.10.13, p. 89, ALRS line 4622).
hypotheses: all group stacks are over Q_p^Δ, Div¹~ or the cyclotomic prism as stated

locator.where: Construction 4.10.5, Theorems 4.10.6 and 4.10.13, p. 86; ALRS line 4454

tests.name: log_q
tests.statement: On X_cyc, log_Δ(q) = log(q) = (q − 1)·e for the generator e of 9.8, and p^{-1}φ(log q) = p^{-1}log(q^p) = log q, so log_Δ(q) is φ-invariant for the twisted Frobenius; compare PrismaticCohomologyPartIII §6.10, where (q − 1)e_A = log_Δ(q^p) integrally.

tests.name: log_untwisted
tests.statement: Without the twist ⟨1⟩, φ(log q) = p·log q, so the untwisted logarithm is not φ-equivariant.

tests.name: log_Zp1
tests.statement: ℤ_p(1)^sm = GSpec(ℚ_p[T^{1/p^∞}]/(T − 1)), the locally constant functions on ℤ_p(1), and G^{dR} ≅ ℤ_p(1)^sm × D^{×,dR}_{FF,Marc(ℚ_p)}.

tests.name: log_fundamental
tests.statement: On arc-stacks ALRS Lemma 4.10.10 becomes the fundamental exact sequence 0 → ℚ_p(1) → BC(O(1)) → G_a → 0 of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals §VB3 (fundamental-exact-sequence), consistent with 7.6.

layers.title: Semilinear solid representations and decompletion by locally analytic vectors

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.semilinearGroupAlgebra
targets.statement: For a light locally profinite group Π let Rep^■_ℤ(Π) = D(ℤ_■[Π]) be the category of solid Π-representations, symmetric monoidal through the Hopf algebra ℤ_■[Π]. For R ∈ CAlg(D(ℤ_■[Π])) let Rep^■_R(Π) = Mod_R(D(ℤ_■[Π])) be the category of R-semilinear solid representations. Construct the associative algebra Λ_R(Π) with underlying solid abelian group R ⊗ ℤ_■[Π] and an equivalence Rep^■_R(Π) ≃ LMod_{Λ_R(Π)}(D(ℤ_■)) by monadicity of the conservative, limit- and colimit-preserving forgetful functor, together with algebra maps ℤ_■[Π] → Λ_R(Π) and R → Λ_R(Π) recovering the rule (a[g])(b[h]) = a·g(b)[gh] (ALRS Construction 5.2.1, p. 93, ALRS line 4817).
hypotheses: Π is a light locally profinite group; R is a commutative algebra in solid Π-representations

locator.where: Construction 5.2.1, p. 93; ALRS line 4817

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.semilinear_monadic
api.statement: Rep^■_R(Π) ≃ LMod_{Λ_R(Π)}(D(ℤ_■)), compatibly with the forgetful functors.

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.semilinear_twisted
api.statement: The algebra maps R → Λ_R(Π) and ℤ_■[Π] → Λ_R(Π) satisfy [g]·a = g(a)·[g].

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.semilinear_functorial
api.statement: Λ_R(Π) is functorial in equivariant algebra maps R → R′ and in group homomorphisms.

tests.name: semilinear_trivialGroup
tests.statement: For Π trivial, Λ_R(Π) = R.

tests.name: semilinear_trivialAction
tests.statement: For R = ℤ with trivial action, Λ_R(Π) = ℤ_■[Π], the solid group algebra.

tests.name: semilinear_matrix
tests.statement: For Π = ℤ/2 acting on R = ℚ_p × ℚ_p by swapping, Λ_R(Π) ≅ M_2(ℚ_p), a simple algebra.

tests.name: semilinear_untwisted
tests.statement: The untwisted product (a[g])(b[h]) = ab[gh] would give the commutative algebra (ℚ_p × ℚ_p) ⊗ ℚ_p[ℤ/2] ≅ ℚ_p⁴ in the previous example, which is not M_2(ℚ_p).

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.continuousRepresentations
targets.statement: Let Π^cont be the Berkovich space of ℚ_p-valued continuous functions on Π and BΠ^cont = GSpec(ℚ_p)/Π^cont. Prove that for profinite Π pullback along f: GSpec(ℚ_p) → BΠ^cont identifies D(BΠ^cont) with right C(Π, ℚ_p)-comodules in solid ℚ_p-vector spaces, that D(BΠ^cont) has a t-structure for which f^* is t-exact and is the left-completed derived category of its heart, and that if Π has finite p-cohomological dimension then f is D-proper and descendable, so BΠ^cont is D-proper over GSpec(ℚ_p); BΠ^cont is !-able whenever Π has an open subgroup of finite p-cohomological dimension (ALRS Lemma 5.2.2, p. 94, ALRS line 4860). Construct a symmetric monoidal functor Φ: D(BΠ^cont) → Rep^■_{ℚ_p}(Π) compatible with forgetful functors and natural in Π (ALRS Construction 5.2.3, p. 94, ALRS line 4906). Prove that if ℚ_p is a perfect ℚ_{p,■}[Π_0]-module for a compact open Π_0, which holds for p-adic Lie groups by the Lazard–Serre resolution (RJRC22 Theorem 5.7, p. 45, RJRC22 line 2227), then Φ has a D(BΠ^cont)-linear right adjoint Φ^R(M) = Γ(Π_0, M ⊗ C(Π_0, ℚ_p)), the unit ℚ_p → Φ^R(ℚ_p) is an equivalence, and Φ is fully faithful (ALRS Lemma 5.2.5, p. 95, ALRS line 4957; ALRS Lemma 5.2.7, p. 97, ALRS line 5072).
hypotheses: Π is a light locally profinite group; for full faithfulness ℚ_p is perfect over ℚ_{p,■}[Π_0] for a compact open Π_0, e.g. Π a p-adic Lie group

locator.where: Lemma 5.2.2, Construction 5.2.3, Lemma 5.2.5, p. 94; ALRS line 4860

tests.name: cont_trivial
tests.statement: For Π trivial, D(BΠ^cont) = D(ℚ_p) and Φ is the identity.

tests.name: cont_character
tests.statement: For Π = ℤ_p the character a ↦ (1 + p)^a (p odd) is a one-dimensional C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p)-comodule, and Φ sends it to ℚ_p with ℤ_p acting through it.

tests.name: cont_regular
tests.statement: The regular representation ℚ_{p,■}[Π] is not in the essential image of Φ, being a comodule over no C(Π_0, ℚ_p) (ALRS Remark 5.2.4(1)); for Π = ∏_ℕ ℤ_p, Φ is not fully faithful (ALRS Remark 5.2.4(2)), so the Lie group hypothesis is needed.

tests.name: cont_mann
tests.statement: On nuclear objects Φ agrees with Mann's identification of nuclear solid ℚ_p-sheaves on (∗/Π)_proét with nuclear solid representations (Man26 Lemma 10.5).

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalyticGroup
targets.statement: Let G be a compact p-adic Lie group with an open normal subgroup G_0 that is uniform pro-p, with ordered basis g_1, …, g_d, G_0 ≅ ℤ_p^d, and p-valuation; after shrinking G_0 its group law and the conjugation action of G extend to integral power series on the polydisc D^d. Let G_0(r) ⊂ G_0(1) be the polydisc of radius r ∈ (0, 1] ∩ ℚ, G_r the induced rigid analytic group ⊔_{g ∈ G/G_r} gG_0(r), G^la = ⋂_{r→0} G_r with O(G^la) = C^la_G = colim_r O(G_r), G_{<r} = ⋃_{r′<r} G_{r′} and G_{≤r} = ⋂_{r′>r} G_{r′} (ALRS §5.2.2, p. 97, ALRS line 5086; ALRS Definition 5.2.8, p. 98, ALRS line 5110). A solid representation M is locally analytic if M^la := Γ(G, C^la_G ⊗ M) → M is an isomorphism (ALRS Definition 5.2.9, p. 98, ALRS line 5124). Prove: BG^cont → BG^la is 0-proper with pushforward of O equal to O, so pullback is fully faithful; Ψ: D(BG^la) → Rep^■_{ℚ_p}(G) is fully faithful with a linear right adjoint, which for compact G is (−)^la, so the essential image is the category of locally analytic representations (ALRS Lemma 5.2.10, p. 98, ALRS line 5137); define Rep^{<r} and Rep^{≤r} as D(GSpec(ℚ_p)/G_{<r}) and D(GSpec(ℚ_p)/G_{≤r}) (ALRS Definition 5.2.11, p. 99, ALRS line 5163); GSpec(ℚ_p) → BG^la and → BG^{≤r} are 0-proper and descendable, so BG^la and BG^{≤r} are 0-proper over GSpec(ℚ_p), and both are suave, and GSpec(ℚ_p) → BG^{<r} is cohomologically smooth with BG^{<r} prim (ALRS Lemma 5.2.12, p. 99, ALRS line 5169). For a rigid analytic group G with G = G(ℚ_p) compact, G^la agrees with G(ℚ_p)^la of 3.4.
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group (non-compact G for the statements local on BG^la)

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalytic_essImage
api.statement: For compact G, Ψ identifies D(BG^la) with the full subcategory of locally analytic solid representations, and Ψ^R ∘ pullback = (−)^la.

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalytic_indEquivalent
api.statement: The ind-systems {C^r_G}, {C^{<r}_G}, {C^{≤r}_G} are ind-equivalent, so C^la_G = colim C^r_G = colim C^{<r}_G = colim C^{≤r}_G (RJRC Remark 2.1.5).

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalytic_proper
api.statement: BG^cont → BG^la is 0-proper with O ≅ s_*O; GSpec(ℚ_p) → BG^la is 0-proper and descendable.

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalytic_ND0
api.statement: The coordinates and p-valuation are those of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII §ND.0 (p-valuation, ordered-basis-chart, p-valued-analytic-structure).

tests.name: la_Zp
tests.statement: For G = ℤ_p, C^la_G is the space of locally analytic functions on ℤ_p, and the character a ↦ (1 + p)^a is locally analytic for p odd (its Mahler coefficients p^n satisfy |p^n|r^n → 0 for 1 < r < p).

tests.name: la_finite
tests.statement: For G finite, G^la = G^sm = G^cont and every solid representation is locally analytic.

tests.name: la_regular
tests.statement: The representation C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) with the regular action is not locally analytic: its locally analytic vectors are C^la(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) ⊊ C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p).

tests.name: la_LR
tests.statement: For a Banach representation B, the cohomology of the derived locally analytic vectors equals R^iLA(B) of LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups §LR.2 (derived-analytic-vectors), and agrees with RJRC22 Theorems 4.36, 5.3 and 5.5; the solid theory of §LR.3 (solid-analytic-vectors) is the κ-condensed counterpart.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.binomialAnalytic
targets.statement: Prove that for a uniform pro-p group G with coordinates G ≅ ℤ_p^d and a ℚ_p-Banach space M, a function f: G → M with binomial expansion f(x) = Σ_α c_α binom(x, α) is locally analytic if and only if there is r > 1 with ‖c_α‖ r^{|α|} → 0 (ALRS Theorem 5.2.14, p. 101, ALRS line 5314; Laz65 Chapitre III, (1.3.9) Corollaire, p. 77, Laz65 line 2873). For a uniform Banach ℚ_p-algebra Λ with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and the spectral norm normalized by |ϖ| = 1/2, define for r > 1 the ϖ-complete module C_{r,ϖ}(G, Λ°) of series Σ c_α binom(x, α) with |c_α| r^{τ(α)} ≤ 1 and → 0 (ALRS Definition 5.2.15, p. 102, ALRS line 5364), prove that it is a subalgebra of C(G, Λ°) and, for |p| ≤ 1/2 and 1 < r < 2, a Hopf Λ°-algebra (ALRS Lemma 5.2.16, p. 102, ALRS line 5379; ALRS Lemma 5.2.17, p. 102, ALRS line 5411), and define the analytic group G^Bin_{r,ϖ} = GSpec(C_{r,ϖ}(G, Λ)) and its semilinear representations (ALRS Definition 5.2.18, p. 104, ALRS line 5492). Prove that BG^la ×_{GSpec ℚ_p} GSpec(Λ) → BG^Bin_{r,ϖ} has the properties of ALRS Lemma 5.2.21, p. 105, ALRS line 5617.
hypotheses: G is a uniform pro-p group of dimension d with fixed coordinates; Λ is a uniform Banach ℚ_p-algebra with |p| ≤ 1/2 in the ϖ-normalization

locator.where: Theorem 5.2.14, Definitions 5.2.15 and 5.2.18, p. 101; ALRS line 5314

tests.name: lazard_character
tests.statement: For G = ℤ_p and p odd, f(a) = (1 + p)^a has c_n = p^n and satisfies the criterion for every r < p.

tests.name: lazard_continuousNotLA
tests.statement: f(a) = Σ_k p^k binom(a, p^k) is continuous (Mahler coefficients tend to 0) but p^{-k}r^{p^k} → ∞ for every r > 1, so f is not locally analytic.

tests.name: lazard_polynomial
tests.statement: A polynomial function on ℤ_p^d has finitely many nonzero c_α and is locally analytic for every r.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.IsDecompleted
targets.statement: For a commutative algebra R in solid G-representations with locally analytic vectors R^la, say that M ∈ Rep^■_R(G) admits a locally analytic decompletion as an R-module if it lies in the essential image of Rep^la_{R^la}(G), equivalently M^la ⊗_{R^la} R → M is an equivalence; similarly for ≤r-analytic decompletion (ALRS Definition 5.2.23, p. 106, ALRS line 5648). Prove that for G × H, M^{(G×H)-la} = (M^{G-la})^{H-la} (ALRS Remark 5.2.25, p. 106, ALRS line 5659), that descendability of an equivariant map of solid ℚ_p-algebras does not depend on the action (ALRS Lemma 5.2.26, p. 106, ALRS line 5664), and the base change and semidirect product properties of ALRS Lemmas 5.2.27–5.2.28, p. 107, ALRS line 5691.
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group; R ∈ CAlg(Rep^■_{ℚ_p}(G))

locator.where: Definition 5.2.23, Remark 5.2.25, Lemmas 5.2.26–5.2.28, p. 106; ALRS line 5648

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.isDecompleted_iff
api.statement: M admits a locally analytic decompletion if and only if M^la ⊗_{R^la} R → M is an equivalence.

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.la_product
api.statement: For G × H acting, (−)^{(G×H)-la} = ((−)^{G-la})^{H-la}.

api.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.descendable_forget
api.statement: An equivariant map A → B of solid ℚ_p-algebras is descendable in Rep(G) if and only if it is descendable as a map of algebras.

tests.name: decompleted_trivialAction
tests.statement: For R = ℚ_p with trivial action, M admits a decompletion if and only if M is locally analytic.

tests.name: decompleted_regularRing
tests.statement: For R = C(G, ℚ_p) with the regular action, R^la = C^la_G and R itself decompletes, since C^la_G ⊗_{C^la_G} R = R.

tests.name: decompleted_failure
tests.statement: For R = ℚ_p and M = C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p), M^la ⊗ ℚ_p = C^la(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) ≠ M, so M admits no decompletion over ℚ_p although it decompletes over R = C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p).

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.locallyAnalyticFunctions
targets.statement: Let X be a Berkovich space with an action of G^cont for a p-adic Lie group G. Prove that the action of a profinite group on GSpec(R) induces a continuous action on R^u and lifts, after shrinking the group, along Berkovich-étale maps, uniquely up to further shrinking (ALRS Lemma 5.3.1, p. 108, ALRS line 5763). Prove that h = h_X: X/G^cont → |X|^Betti/G^la, where G^la acts on |X|^Betti through G^la → G^sm, is 0-proper, and that pullback induces a fully faithful functor Mod_{O^la_X}(D(|X|^Betti/G^la)) → D(X/G^cont), where O^la_X := h_*O_{X/G^cont} is the sheaf of locally analytic functions (ALRS Proposition 5.3.2, p. 109, ALRS line 5814; ALRS Theorem 5.1.1(1), p. 92, ALRS line 4743). The introduction of ALRS phrases the same statement as primness of h with trivial codualizing complex (ALRS Theorem 1.19(1), p. 8, ALRS line 420).
hypotheses: X is a Berkovich space with an action of G^cont, G a p-adic Lie group

locator.where: Lemma 5.3.1, Proposition 5.3.2, Theorem 5.1.1(1), p. 109; ALRS line 5814

tests.name: laFunctions_trivialGroup
tests.statement: For G trivial, h = (X → |X|^Betti) and O^la_X = h_*O_X, recovering 2.7.

tests.name: laFunctions_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p) with trivial action, h = (BG^cont → BG^la) and O^la = O by 10.3.

tests.name: laFunctions_notIso
tests.statement: For X = G^cont with G = ℤ_p acting by translation, h is not an isomorphism: D(X/G^cont) = D(ℚ_p) while |X|^Betti/G^la = ℤ_p^sm/ℤ_p^la carries more quasi-coherent sheaves.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.classical
targets.statement: Prove that for a Gelfand ring R with an action of a compact p-adic Lie group G, the connective cover τ_{≥0}R^la is a Gelfand ring (ALRS Lemma 5.4.1, p. 109, ALRS line 5831). Call R classically decompleted if R^la is connective and R^la → R is an isomorphism on uniform completions; call a Berkovich G^cont-space X locally classically decompleted if it has a strict closed affinoid cover by GSpec(R_i), stabilized by compact opens G_i with R_i classically decompleted, and let X^la = ⋃ GSpec(R_i^la) (ALRS Definition 5.4.2, p. 110, ALRS line 5851). Prove that X^la is a Berkovich space and that analytic, finite étale and Berkovich-étale sites of R^la, R and R^u agree (ALRS Remark 5.4.3, p. 110, ALRS line 5862; ALRS Remark 5.4.4, p. 110, ALRS line 5867), that Berkovich-étale G-equivariant R → R′ decomplete as B ⊗_{R^la} R = R′ (ALRS Lemma 5.4.5, p. 110, ALRS line 5877), that GSpec_{|X|/G^la}(O^la_X) ≅ GSpec(R^la)/G^la (ALRS Corollary 5.4.6, p. 110, ALRS line 5895), the stability properties of ALRS Lemma 5.4.7, p. 111, ALRS line 5909, and hence that for classically decompleted affinoid X = GSpec(R), R^la → O^la_X is an equivalence and Mod_{R^la}(D(BG^la)) ≅ Mod_{O^la_X}(D(|X|^Betti/G^la)), with every G^cont-equivariant affinoid Berkovich-étale GSpec(R′) → GSpec(R) classically decompleted (ALRS Theorem 5.1.1(2), p. 92, ALRS line 4747).
hypotheses: G is a compact p-adic Lie group acting on the Gelfand ring R; X is a Berkovich space with a G^cont-action

locator.where: Definition 5.4.2, Lemma 5.4.5, Corollary 5.4.6, Theorem 5.1.1(2), p. 110; ALRS line 5851

tests.name: classical_cyclotomic
tests.statement: For K = ℚ_p^cyc with Γ = Gal(ℚ_p^cyc/ℚ_p), K^la = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is connective with completion K, so K is classically decompleted; this is the Berger–Colmez computation (BC16 Théorème 3.2).

tests.name: classical_trivial
tests.statement: For trivial G every Gelfand ring is classically decompleted with R^la = R.

tests.name: classical_regular
tests.statement: For R = C(G, ℚ_p) with translation action, R^la = C^la_G and its uniform completion is R, so R is classically decompleted with X^la = G^la.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.epsTors
targets.statement: For a Λ°-linear solid G-representation M define its integral binomial-analytic vectors M^{Bin_{r,ϖ}} = Γ(G, M ⊗_{Λ°} C_{r,ϖ}(G, Λ°)) (ALRS Definition 5.5.1, p. 112, ALRS line 5997). Prove that if a G-equivariant ϖ-complete solid animated Λ°-algebra A satisfies (ϵ-TORS) — there are 2 > r_0 > r_1 > ⋯ > 1, r_n → 1, with π_i(A^{Bin_{r_n,ϖ}}) ϖ^ϵ-torsion for i ≤ −1 — and a connective ϖ-complete A-module N admits maps N_{ϖ^{(d+1)ϵ}} → M ⊗ A_{ϖ^{(d+1)ϵ}} → N_{ϖ^{(d+1)ϵ}} composing to ϖ^δ with 0 ≤ δ < ϵ and M with trivial action, then N[1/ϖ] admits a decompletion by Bin_{r_n,ϖ}-analytic vectors, in particular by locally analytic vectors (ALRS Proposition 5.5.6, p. 113, ALRS line 6055); prove stability under relatively locally analytic base change (ALRS Corollary 5.5.13, p. 116, ALRS line 6203), define ϵ-TORS uniformly on G (ALRS Definition 5.5.14, p. 116, ALRS line 6213) and prove its stability under integral models of Tate-rational localizations (ALRS Lemmas 5.5.16–5.5.17, p. 116, ALRS line 6225).
hypotheses: G is a uniform pro-p group of dimension d; Λ is a uniform Banach ℚ_p-algebra with ϖ^ϵ ∈ Λ for ϵ ∈ ℚ; A is G-equivariant, ϖ-complete, solid animated over Λ°

locator.where: Definition 5.5.1, Proposition 5.5.6, Corollary 5.5.13, Definition 5.5.14, p. 113; ALRS line 6055

tests.name: eps_trivial
tests.statement: For A with trivial G-action, A^{Bin_{r,ϖ}} = A and ϵ-TORS holds for every ϵ.

tests.name: eps_d0
tests.statement: For d = 0 (G trivial) every module decompletes.

tests.name: eps_torsion
tests.statement: If for every r ∈ (1, 2) the group π_{−1}(A^{Bin_{r,ϖ}}) contains an element killed by no power of ϖ, then ϵ-TORS fails for every ϵ and ALRS Proposition 5.5.6 does not apply; strong decompletion requires the torsion bound.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.perfectComplexes
targets.statement: Prove the base change and locality statements of ALRS Lemma 5.6.2, p. 119, ALRS line 6348 and the decompletion of perfect complexes over strongly decompleted algebras of ALRS Proposition 5.6.4, p. 120, ALRS line 6444. Call an affinoid Berkovich G^cont-space GSpec(A) over Λ strongly decompleted if there are an open uniform subgroup G_0, a direct system of G_0-equivariant ϖ-complete animated Λ°-algebras A_i with A_i/ϖ discrete and A = colim A_i[1/ϖ], each A_i satisfying ϵ_i-TORS uniformly on G_0; call a locally classically decompleted X locally strongly decompleted if, for some compact open G_0, a G_0^la-equivariant epimorphism Y′ → X^la from a Berkovich space over GSpec(Λ) has pullback Y = Y′ ×_{X^la} X a disjoint union of strongly decompleted affinoids (ALRS Definition 5.6.8, p. 124, ALRS line 6730). Prove that strongly decompleted rings are classically decompleted (ALRS Remark 5.6.9, p. 124, ALRS line 6746), that for locally strongly decompleted X pullback gives Perf(X^la/G^la) ≃ Perf(X/G^cont) (ALRS Theorem 5.6.10, p. 124, ALRS line 6754), also after every G^cont-equivariant Berkovich-étale Y → X (ALRS Corollary 5.6.11, p. 125, ALRS line 6786) and after base change along filtered colimits of p-adically complete animated O_K-algebras (ALRS Corollary 5.6.12, p. 125, ALRS line 6824). The strong decompletion hypothesis is kept: the source does not know the general case (ALRS Remark 5.1.4, p. 93, ALRS line 4791).
hypotheses: X is a locally classically decompleted Berkovich space with a G^cont-action, G a p-adic Lie group, locally strongly decompleted

locator.where: Definition 5.6.8, Theorem 5.6.10, Corollaries 5.6.11–5.6.12, p. 124; ALRS line 6754

tests.name: strong_trivial
tests.statement: For G trivial the equivalence is the identity of Perf(X).

tests.name: strong_BergerColmez
tests.statement: For one-dimensional Γ and a finite-dimensional K̂_∞-semilinear representation W, the decompleted module is W^la = W^fin and K̂_∞ ⊗_{K_∞} W^la ≅ W (BC16 Théorèmes 3.2 and 3.4).

tests.name: strong_unknown
tests.statement: The equivalence is not asserted for arbitrary continuous actions; only full faithfulness (10.6) holds without the strong decompletion hypothesis (ALRS Remark 5.1.4).

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.senTheory
targets.statement: Let Λ be a uniform Banach ℚ_p-algebra with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, Γ ≅ ℤ_p with generator γ and Γ_k = γ^{p^kℤ_p}, and A_∞ = (colim_n A_n)^∧_ϖ for static ϖ-complete ϖ-torsion-free animated Λ°-algebras A_n with A_n/ϖ discrete. Assume the Tate–Sen axioms: for every k there is n_0 such that for n ≥ n_0 there are 0 < ρ_{n,k} < ϵ_{n,k} → 0 with Γ_k acting trivially on A_n/ϖ^{ϵ_{n,k}} and the cohomology of Γ(Γ_k, A_∞/A_n) concentrated in degree 1 and ϖ^{ρ_{n,k}}-torsion (ALRS Assumption 5.7.1, p. 126, ALRS line 6855). Prove that A_∞ satisfies ϵ-TORS uniformly on Γ for all ϵ > 0 and (A_∞[1/ϖ])^la = colim_n A_n[1/ϖ] (ALRS Proposition 5.7.3, p. 126, ALRS line 6875). Prove: (arithmetic) X = (1 + D̃^{<1,u}_{ℚ_p}) ∖ {1} with G = ℚ_p^× is locally strongly decompleted with X^la = (1 + D̃^{<1}) ∖ {1} (ALRS Theorem 5.7.4, p. 127, ALRS line 6930); the toric tower satisfies the axioms (ALRS Proposition 5.7.16, p. 134, ALRS line 7338); (geometric) for a perfectoid D over ℚ_p^cyc and G = ℤ_p(1)^d acting on X = D^×_{FF,G̃^{d,⋄}_{m,D}} = G̃^{d,u}_{m,ℚ_p} × D^×_{FF,D}, X is locally strongly decompleted with X^la = G̃^d_{m,ℚ_p} × D^×_{FF,D} (ALRS Corollary 5.7.18, p. 135, ALRS line 7371); and the summary: X_arith = D^×_{FF,ℚ_p^cyc} has X^la_arith = BC(O(1)) ∖ {0}, X_geo has X^la_geo = G̃^d_{m,ℚ_p} × D^×_{FF,D}, for X_mixed = D^×_{FF,G̃^{d,u}_{m,ℚ_p^cyc}} with G_mixed = ℤ_p^× ⋉ ℤ_p(1)^d one has X^la_mixed = G̃^d_{m,ℚ_p} × (BC(O(1)) ∖ {0}), and for every Berkovich-étale G^cont-equivariant Y → X_? (? ∈ {arith, geo, mixed}), Perf(Y^la/G^la_?) ≃ Perf(Y/G^cont_?) (ALRS Theorem 5.7.19, p. 135, ALRS line 7390).
hypotheses: Λ, Γ, (A_n) as stated, satisfying Assumption 5.7.1

locator.where: Assumption 5.7.1, Proposition 5.7.3, Theorem 5.7.4, Corollary 5.7.18, Theorem 5.7.19, p. 126; ALRS line 6855

tests.name: sen_mixed_d0
tests.statement: For d = 0 the mixed statement reduces to the arithmetic one.

tests.name: sen_arith_points
tests.statement: On the Hodge–Tate point the arithmetic decompletion recovers K^la = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) for K = ℚ_p^cyc (BC16 Théorème 3.2).

tests.name: sen_geo_coordinates
tests.statement: In the geometric case with d = 1 the generator γ of ℤ_p(1) acts by T^r ↦ q^rT^r, q = [ε], for r ∈ ℕ[1/p] (ALRS (5.7.10)); for r = p^{−n}, (γ^{p^k} − 1)T^r = (q^{p^{k−n}} − 1)T^r is divisible by ϖ^{1/p^{n−k}}, which is Axiom (1) of Assumption 5.7.1 with ϵ_{n,k} = p^{k−n} (ALRS Proposition 5.7.16(1)).

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.torsors
targets.statement: For a locally classically decompleted Berkovich G^cont-space X with h: X/G^cont → X^la/G^la, and a Gelfand stack Z over X^la/G^la, let β_{X,Z}: Map(X^la/G^la, Z) → Map(X/G^cont, Z) be precomposition with h and β^ét_{X,Z} its étale-sheaf version on the Berkovich-étale site (ALRS §5.8, p. 137, ALRS line 7454). Prove the permanence properties of ALRS Lemma 5.8.1, p. 137, ALRS line 7473 (stability under limits, the case Z ≅ Z^{dR/(X^la/G^la)}, Berkovich-étale locality), the comparison with arc-stacks for perfectoid X (ALRS Lemma 5.8.2, p. 138, ALRS line 7511), that torsors under groups !-locally induced by Gelfand rings are !-locally maps of Gelfand rings (ALRS Lemma 5.8.5, p. 139, ALRS line 7555), that O(T)^{G-la} = O(T^{st la}) for a decompleted H^la-torsor (ALRS Lemma 5.8.8, p. 139, ALRS line 7581), the symmetric double decompletion Y^{H-la}/H^la ≅ GSpec_{|Z|}(O^{(G×H)-la}_Z)/(G × H)^la (ALRS Proposition 5.8.9, p. 139, ALRS line 7595), and that β^ét_{X,Z} is an equivalence, when perfect complexes on all Berkovich-étale X′/G^cont admit decompletions, for Z = T^an × X^la/G^la with T perfect strongly Tannakian, Z = BU × X^la/G^la with U open in H(ℚ_p)^la, and Z = BΓ^la × X^la/G^la for a p-adic Lie group Γ (ALRS Proposition 5.8.10, p. 140, ALRS line 7627).
hypotheses: X is a locally classically decompleted Berkovich space with a G^cont-action; for Proposition 5.8.10, perfect complexes on Berkovich-étale X′/G^cont admit decompletions (e.g. X locally strongly decompleted)

locator.where: §5.8, Lemmas 5.8.1–5.8.8, Propositions 5.8.9–5.8.10, p. 139; ALRS line 7595

tests.name: torsor_trivial
tests.statement: For the trivial torsor β_{X,Z} sends the trivial H^la-torsor on X^la/G^la to the trivial one on X/G^cont.

tests.name: torsor_finite
tests.statement: For Γ finite, Γ^la = Γ^sm and Z = BΓ^la × X^la/G^la: β^ét is an equivalence by ALRS Lemma 5.8.1(2), since BΓ^sm is its own relative de Rham stack.

tests.name: torsor_notBerkovich
tests.statement: A G^la-torsor over a Berkovich space need not be a Berkovich space: for G = GL_n(ℤ_p), Y ×_{GL_n(ℤ_p)^la} GL_n is the overconvergent neighbourhood of a closed subset (ALRS Remark 5.8.6), so Lemma 5.8.5 asserts only !-local affineness.

targets.name: TauCeti.Decompletion.main
targets.statement: Let X be a Berkovich space with a continuous action of a p-adic Lie group G, i.e. an action of G^cont, and h: X/G^cont → |X|^Betti/G^la. Then: (1) h is 0-proper and h^* is fully faithful on modules over O^la_X = h_*O; (2) if X = GSpec(R) is affinoid and R is classically decompleted, R^la → O^la_X is an equivalence and Mod_{R^la}(D(BG^la)) ≅ Mod_{O^la_X}(D(|X|^Betti/G^la)), and G^cont-equivariant affinoid Berkovich-étale maps to X are classically decompleted; (3) if X is locally strongly decompleted, then every G^cont-equivariant Berkovich-étale X′ → X has a strict closed affinoid cover classically decompleted for the stabilizers, O^la_{X′} is the structure sheaf of a Berkovich space X′^la with |X′^la| = |X′|, and Perf(X′^la/G^la) ≃ Perf(X′/G^cont) (ALRS Theorem 5.1.1, p. 92, ALRS line 4738).
hypotheses: G is a p-adic Lie group; X is a Berkovich space with a G^cont-action; the hypotheses of (2) and (3) as stated

locator.where: Theorem 5.1.1, p. 92; ALRS line 4738

tests.name: main_trivialGroup
tests.statement: For G trivial, X^la = X and all three statements are tautological.

tests.name: main_arithmetic
