tests.statement: For X = D^×_{FF,ℚ_p^cyc} with G = ℤ_p^×, (3) gives Perf(BC(O(1)) ∖ {0}/ℤ_p^{×,la}) ≃ Perf(X/ℤ_p^{×,cont}), the decompletion used in 11.1.

tests.name: main_hypotheses
tests.statement: Without strong decompletion only (1) is asserted; in particular the equivalence on perfect complexes is not claimed for arbitrary continuous actions.

layers.title: The pro-étale comparison, Sen operators and torsors

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.arithmetic
targets.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p and X = GSpec(K). Prove that α_X: FF_{X^⋄} → X^{Div¹} is 0-proper with O ≅ α_{X,*}O, so that for every map Y → X^{Div¹} pullback D(Y) → D(FF_{X^⋄} ×_{X^{Div¹}} Y) is fully faithful, and that for every Berkovich-étale U → X^{Div¹}, pullback Perf(U) → Perf(FF_{X^⋄} ×_{X^{Div¹}} U) is an equivalence (ALRS Theorem 6.1.1, p. 143, ALRS line 7756). Prove that for K/ℚ_p unramified X^{Div¹} ≅ GSpec(K) × Div¹ (ALRS Remark 6.1.5, p. 145, ALRS line 7873).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is a finite extension

locator.where: Theorem 6.1.1, p. 143; ALRS line 7756

tests.name: arith_phiGamma
tests.statement: On vector bundles, Perf(Div¹)^{VB} is the category of (φ, Γ)-modules over the Robba ring, and the equivalence restricted to FF_{Q_p^⋄} recovers the cyclotomic decompletion of PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology §1.4 (cyclotomicDecompletionEquivalence) between ordinary and extended Robba (φ, Γ)-modules.

tests.name: arith_galois
tests.statement: Continuous finite-dimensional ℚ_p-representations V of Gal_K embed fully faithfully as vector bundles E_V on X^{Div¹}, with essential image those whose pullback to FF_{ℚ_p^cyc} has slope 0 (ALRS Example 6.1.7; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals §VB4 slope-zero-local-systems).

tests.name: arith_DHT
tests.statement: The pushforward of E_V|_{X^HT} along X^HT → BG_m gives D_HT(V) as a graded K-vector space (ALRS Example 6.1.7(1)).

tests.name: arith_notAll
tests.statement: On all of D the pullback is fully faithful but not an equivalence: for π: FF_{ℚ_p^cyc} → FF_{Q_p^⋄}, π_*O = O ⊗ C(ℤ_p^×, ℚ_p) with the regular action, whereas α^*α_*π_*O = O ⊗ C^la(ℤ_p^×, ℚ_p), so π_*O is not in the essential image of α^*.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.arithmeticHT
targets.statement: For K/ℚ_p finite and X = GSpec(K), prove that α^HT_X: X̂^⋄ → X^HT is 0-proper with O ≅ α^HT_*O and induces Perf(X^HT) ≃ Perf(X̂^⋄), and that L_{X^HT/ℚ_p} = L_{X^HT/X} ≅ O_{X^HT}[−1]. Using the G_m^† ≅ G_a^†-gerbe structure of X^HT → X and Cartier duality, D(X^HT) is a module over D(G_a^an), giving each M ∈ D(X^HT) its arithmetic Sen operator θ_M. Prove: (a) for M in the essential image of α^{HT,*}, viewed as a solid C_p-semilinear Gal_K-representation, θ_M is the base change along K(ζ_{p^∞}) → C_p of the derivative of the Γ-action on α^HT_*(M)|_{K(ζ_{p^∞})} = Γ(Gal^cont_{K^cyc}, M)^{Γ-la}; (b) for static M in the essential image, H*(Gal^cont_K, M) ≅ H*(θ_M, M)^{Gal_K} (ALRS Theorem 6.1.3, p. 144, ALRS line 7798). Prove Tate's computation H^i(Gal_K, C_p(n)) ≅ H^i(X^HT, O{n}) ≅ H^i(K →^{n} K), with θ_{O{n}} = n (ALRS Example 6.1.4, p. 145, ALRS line 7868).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is a finite extension; M is in the essential image of α^{HT,*}; static for (b)

locator.where: Theorem 6.1.3, Example 6.1.4, p. 144; ALRS line 7798

tests.name: sen_tate
tests.statement: For M = C_p(n): if n ≠ 0, θ = n is invertible and H*(Gal_K, C_p(n)) = 0; if n = 0, θ = 0 and H⁰ = H¹ = K, H² = 0, Tate's theorem.

tests.name: sen_classical
tests.statement: On finite-dimensional C_p-semilinear representations θ_M is the Sen operator senOperator of PadicHodgeTheory §4.4 and the labelled Sen operator Θ = log ρ(γ)/log χ_p(γ) of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.P7.2, with HT(χ_p) = +1.

tests.name: sen_sign
tests.statement: With the opposite sign θ_{O{1}} = −1 one would get H*(Gal_K, C_p(1)) computed by K →^{−1} K, still zero, but the Sen weight of the Tate twist would be −1, contradicting senOperator on C_p(1), which is multiplication by 1.

tests.name: sen_cotangent
tests.statement: L_{X^HT/ℚ_p} = O[−1]: the classifying stack BG_m^† of the band contributes the shifted dual of its one-dimensional Lie algebra.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.toricChart
targets.statement: Let X = G_m^d over ℚ_p, X̃ = lim_{T↦T^p} X the perfected torus in Gelfand stacks and Γ_d = ℤ_p^{×,la} ⋉ ℤ_p^{d,la}. Prove that X^{Div¹} ≅ X̃_{X_cyc}/(φ^ℤ × Γ_d^la) = FF^la_{X̃^{d,⋄}_{ℚ_p^cyc}}/Γ_d^la, where FF^la is glued from the spectra of Γ_d-locally analytic vectors of Γ_d-stable affinoids of FF_{X̃^{d,⋄}_{ℚ_p^cyc}}, while FF_{X^⋄} = FF_{X̃^{d,⋄}_{ℚ_p^cyc}}/Γ_d^cont, so that α_X is the natural map from the continuous to the locally analytic quotient (ALRS Remark 4.10.15, p. 90, ALRS line 4683; ALRS (1.2.1), p. 8, ALRS line 399); the Lie algebra of Γ_d acts on FF^la through (log q)q∂_q, (log q)T_i∂_{T_i}, with logarithmic poles at the Hodge–Tate locus (ALRS §4.10, p. 91, ALRS line 4704).
hypotheses: X = G_m^d over ℚ_p, d ≥ 0

tests.name: toric_d0
tests.statement: For d = 0 the statement is Div¹ = FF^la_{ℚ_p^cyc}/ℤ_p^{×,la} = X_cyc/ℚ_p^{×,la} of 9.7.

tests.name: toric_lie
tests.statement: For d = 1 the Lie algebra of Γ_1 acts by (log q)q∂_q and (log q)T∂_T, the factor log q being the derivative of a ↦ q^a; the action has logarithmic poles along the Hodge–Tate locus and is trivial modulo log q, and the residual linear action on the Hodge–Tate stack gives the arithmetic and geometric Sen operators of 11.2 and 11.5.

tests.name: toric_continuous
tests.statement: The continuous quotient FF_{X̃^{d,⋄}_{ℚ_p^cyc}}/Γ_d^cont is FF_{X^⋄}, not X^{Div¹}: already for d = 0 the pushforwards of O from FF_{ℚ_p^cyc} to the two quotients are O ⊗ C(ℤ_p^×, ℚ_p) and O ⊗ C^la(ℤ_p^×, ℚ_p) (11.1), so the two quotients differ exactly by α_X.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.geometric
targets.statement: Let D be a perfectoid space over ℚ_p and X → D a rigid smooth morphism of Berkovich spaces. Prove that α_{X/D}: FF_{X^⋄} → X^{Div¹/FF_D} is 0-proper with O ≅ α_{X/D,*}O, so pullback from any Y → X^{Div¹/FF_D} is fully faithful, and that for every Berkovich-étale U → X^{Div¹/FF_D}, Perf(U) ≃ Perf(FF_{X^⋄} ×_{X^{Div¹/FF_D}} U) (ALRS Theorem 6.2.1, p. 146, ALRS line 7921).
hypotheses: D is a perfectoid space over ℚ_p; X → D is a rigid smooth morphism of Berkovich spaces

locator.where: Theorem 6.2.1, p. 146; ALRS line 7921

tests.name: geo_identity
tests.statement: For X = D, X^{Div¹/FF_D} = X^{Div¹} ×_{D^{Div¹}} FF_D = FF_D since D^{Div¹} = FF_D for perfectoid D (8.3), and α_{X/D} is the identity of FF_D.

tests.name: geo_torus
tests.statement: For X = G_{m,D}, Γ = ℤ_p(1) acts on G̃_m by [T♭]^r ↦ [ε]^r[T♭]^r for r ∈ ℤ[1/p].

tests.name: geo_notTate
tests.statement: The localization in the proof uses rigid étale maps and not †-rational localizations of X, because the latter are completed on X^⋄ (ALRS footnote 51, p. 146); accordingly the statement is made for Berkovich-étale U.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.geometricHT
targets.statement: For D and X → D as in 11.4 prove: (1) α^HT_{X/D}: X̂^⋄ → X^HT is 0-proper with O ≅ α^HT_*O and Perf(X^HT ×_X U) ≃ Perf(X̂^⋄ ×_X U) for Berkovich-étale U → X; (2) L_{X^HT/X} ≅ Ω¹_{X/D}{−1}[−1]; (3) the BT^†_{X/D}{1}-torsor structure of X^HT → X and Cartier duality make every M ∈ D(X^HT) a Sym_{O_X}(T_{X/D}{1})-module, its geometric Sen operator θ_M, an Ω¹_{X/D}{−1}-Higgs field, which pulls back to the essential image of α^{HT,*}; (4) π_X^*π_{X,*}M is computed by the Higgs complex M → M ⊗ Ω¹_{X/D}{−1} → ⋯ → M ⊗ Ω^{dim X}_{X/D}{−dim X}; (5) every relative locally analytic orthonormalizable Banach Ô_X-sheaf lies in the essential image of α^{HT,*} and its geometric Sen operator is that of RCSen Theorem 1.0.3 (ALRS Theorem 6.2.2, p. 147, ALRS line 7976; RCSen Theorem 1.0.3, p. 2, RCSen line 64).
hypotheses: D is a perfectoid space over ℚ_p; X → D is a rigid smooth morphism of Berkovich spaces

locator.where: Theorem 6.2.2, p. 147; ALRS line 7976

tests.name: geoHT_curve
tests.statement: For dim X = 1, L_{X^HT/X} = Ω¹_{X/D}{−1}[−1] and the Higgs complex has two terms M → M ⊗ Ω¹{−1}.

tests.name: geoHT_descend
tests.statement: A vector bundle on X^HT descends to X if and only if its geometric Sen operator vanishes, the analogue of p-curvature (ALRS Remark 6.2.5).

tests.name: geoHT_point
tests.statement: For X = D the Higgs field is zero and X^HT = D.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.main
targets.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p and X a smooth partially proper rigid space over K, viewed as a Berkovich space. Prove that α_X: FF_{X^⋄} → X^{Div¹} is 0-proper and O → α_{X,*}O is an equivalence, so α_X^* is fully faithful on quasi-coherent sheaves, and that for every Berkovich-étale Y → X^{Div¹} pullback gives an equivalence Perf(Y) ≃ Perf(FF_{X^⋄} ×_{X^{Div¹}} Y); in particular Perf(X^{Div¹}) ≃ Perf(FF_{X^⋄}) (ALRS Theorem 6.3.1, p. 149, ALRS line 8082; ALRS Theorem 1.15, p. 7, ALRS line 356).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is a finite extension; X is a smooth partially proper rigid space over K

locator.where: Theorem 6.3.1, p. 149; ALRS line 8082

tests.name: main_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(K) the theorem is 11.1.

tests.name: main_empty
tests.statement: For X = ∅ both sides are empty.

tests.name: main_nonreduced
tests.statement: The smoothness hypothesis is used: perfect complexes and cohomology on FF_{X^⋄} depend only on X^⋄, which does not see nilpotents (2.8), whereas the two sides of (1.2.2) differ for non-reduced Berkovich spaces (ALRS p. 9, ALRS line 483); so the theorem is not asserted beyond smooth X.

tests.name: main_partiallyProper
tests.statement: For a smooth affinoid X the Hodge–Tate parts of the statement hold without partial properness (ALRS Remarks 6.3.4 and 6.4.2), but the statement for X^{Div¹} is asserted only for partially proper X.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.proetaleCohomology
targets.statement: For K/ℚ_p finite and X a smooth partially proper rigid space over K prove Γ(X^{Div¹}, O) ≅ RΓ(FF_{X^⋄}, O) ≅ RΓ_v(X^⋄, ℚ_p) ≅ RΓ_proét(X, ℚ_p), where ℚ_p is the topological (condensed) ℚ_p and the last isomorphism is the comparison of the pro-étale site of X with the v-site of X^⋄ (ALRS (1.2.2), p. 9, ALRS line 480).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is a finite extension; X is a smooth partially proper rigid space over K

tests.name: proet_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p), Γ(Div¹, O) = RΓ(Gal_{ℚ_p}, ℚ_p) has dimensions 1, 2, 0 in degrees 0, 1, 2, with Euler characteristic −1 = −[ℚ_p : ℚ_p].

tests.name: proet_field
tests.statement: For K/ℚ_p of degree n, H¹(Gal_K, ℚ_p) = Hom(Gal_K^ab, ℚ_p) has dimension n + 1, matching Γ(X^{Div¹}, O) through the cartesian square of 11.1.

tests.name: proet_nonreduced
tests.statement: For connected X, H⁰(X^{Div¹}, O) = H⁰_proét(X, ℚ_p) = ℚ_p, the constants.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.mixedHT
targets.statement: For K/ℚ_p finite and X a smooth partially proper rigid space over K prove: (1) π_{X,1}: X^HT → X × K^HT is a BT^†_X{1}-torsor, so every M ∈ D(X^HT) is an Ω¹_X{−1}-Higgs module, compatibly with 11.5 after base change to perfectoids over Q_p^HT, descending the geometric Sen operator to X × K^HT; (2) L_{X^HT/(X×K^HT)} ≅ Ω¹_{X/K}{−1}[−1] and L_{X^HT/X} is an extension of Ω¹_{X/K}{−1}[−1] by O_{X^HT}[−1] whose pullback to X̂^⋄ is the inverse Faltings' extension, FE^−_X{−1} = L_{X^HT/X}[1]; (3) for G_FE = T_X ⋊ G_m with dual Lie algebra g*_FE, the pullback of g*_FE along X^HT → BG_FE is L_{X^HT/X}[1]; (4) the maps X^HT → BG_FE → B(Ĝ_FE ⋊ G_FE) → B(G^†_FE ⋊ G_FE) promote every sheaf on X^HT to a module over the enveloping algebra of g_{X,FE}, the analytic Harish-Chandra (Higgs–Sen) structure, restricting along T_X{1} → g_{X,FE} to the Higgs field (ALRS Theorem 6.3.2, p. 150, ALRS line 8145). Partial properness is not needed for these statements (ALRS Remark 6.3.4, p. 153, ALRS line 8277).
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p is a finite extension; X is a smooth rigid space over K (partial properness not needed)

locator.where: Theorem 6.3.2, Remark 6.3.4, p. 150; ALRS line 8145

tests.name: mixed_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(K), Ω¹ = 0 and L_{X^HT/X} = O[−1], agreeing with 11.2.

tests.name: mixed_FE
tests.statement: For X = G_m over K, the extension class of L_{X^HT/X}[1] pulled back to X̂^⋄ is the class of FE_X computed in 9.5, inverted and twisted by {−1}.

tests.name: mixed_split
tests.statement: L_{X^HT/X} is in general a non-split extension: splitting it would split Faltings' extension, which fails for G_m (9.5).

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.torsors
targets.statement: Let X be a smooth partially proper rigid space over ℚ_p and G a p-adic Lie group. Prove: (1) Map(X^HT, BG^la) ≃ Map(X̂^⋄, BG^la) ≃ Map(X^⋄, BG), so G^la-torsors on X^HT, G^la-torsors on X̂^⋄ and pro-étale G-torsors on X^⋄ are equivalent; (2) for every Berkovich-étale U ⊂ FF^⋄_{X^⋄}, pullback gives Map(X^{Div¹}|_U, BG^la) ≃ Map(FF_{X^⋄}|_U, BG^la); (3) there is a natural map Map(X^⋄, BG) → Map(FF_{X^⋄}, BG^la) sending X̃^⋄ → X^⋄ to FF^⋄_{X̃^⋄} → FF^⋄_{X^⋄} after perfectoidization; and the analogous statements hold relative to a perfectoid base D with X^{Div¹/FF_D} (ALRS Theorem 6.4.1, p. 153, ALRS line 8321). Part (1) does not need partial properness (ALRS Remark 6.4.2, p. 154, ALRS line 8349), and Γ(X^{Div¹}, O) = Γ(G^la, Γ(FF_{X̃}, O)^{G-la}) for a perfectoid pro-étale G-torsor X̃^⋄ → X^⋄ (ALRS Remark 6.4.3, p. 154, ALRS line 8351); whether X^{Div¹} = FF^la_{X̃}/G^la in general is not asserted (ALRS Remark 1.22, p. 9, ALRS line 460).
hypotheses: X is a smooth partially proper rigid space over ℚ_p (smooth suffices for (1)); G is a p-adic Lie group

locator.where: Theorem 6.4.1, Remarks 6.4.2–6.4.3, p. 153; ALRS line 8321

tests.name: torsor_finiteG
tests.statement: For G finite, G^la = G^sm and (1) recovers the equivalence between finite étale G-torsors on X and on X̂^⋄.

tests.name: torsor_trivialG
tests.statement: For G trivial all mapping anima are points.

tests.name: torsor_Zp_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p) and G = ℤ_p, pro-étale ℤ_p-torsors are continuous homomorphisms Gal_{ℚ_p} → ℤ_p up to conjugacy, a free ℤ_p-module of rank 2, and (1) identifies them with ℤ_p^la-torsors on Q_p^HT.

tests.name: torsor_open
tests.statement: The identification X^{Div¹} = FF^la_{X̃}/G^la over BG^la is an open question (ALRS Remark 1.22) and is not a target.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.senOfTorsor
targets.statement: For a perfectoid D, a partially proper smooth rigid space X over D, a p-adic Lie group G and a pro-étale G-torsor X̃^⋄ → X^⋄ with decompletion β: X^{HT/D} → BG^la (11.9), define the geometric Sen operator θ^geo_β: g^∨_β → Ω¹_{X/D}{−1} as the shifted map of cotangent complexes β^*L_{BG^la}[1] → L_{X^HT/X}[1]; for X over K finite over ℚ_p define the mixed Sen operator θ^mix_β: g^∨_β → FE^−_X{−1} and, for X = GSpec(K), the arithmetic Sen operator θ^arith_β: g^∨_β → O_{X^HT} (ALRS Definition 6.4.4, p. 155, ALRS line 8384). Construct, for a †-formally smooth group G → S and a G^{dR/S}-torsor, the induced homomorphism of overconvergent groups (ALRS Construction 6.4.5, p. 155, ALRS line 8404), and prove that the dual of the resulting Lie algebra map Sen_β: T_{X/D}{1} → g_β is θ^geo_β and agrees with the geometric Sen operator of RCSen Theorem 1.0.4 (ALRS Lemma 6.4.8, p. 156, ALRS line 8454; RCSen Theorem 1.0.4, p. 3, RCSen line 113), and that for X = GSpec(K) and a Galois X̃ the dual of θ^arith_β is the classical Sen operator (ALRS Remark 6.4.9, p. 156, ALRS line 8471). Prove: for K_∞/K algebraic Galois with p-adic Lie group G and K^u_∞ perfectoid, β_*O = K^{u,la}_∞ is static and X^HT ≅ GSpec(K^{u,la}_∞)/G^la (ALRS Proposition 6.4.10, p. 156, ALRS line 8477); in the geometric and mixed cases, if θ^geo (resp. θ^mix) is surjective, then β_*O = O^la_{X̃̂^⋄} is static on a strict closed basis and X^HT ≅ GSpec_{|X̃|}(O^la_{X̃̂^⋄})/G^la (ALRS Proposition 6.4.12, p. 158, ALRS line 8545).
hypotheses: D perfectoid over ℚ_p and X partially proper smooth over D (geometric); X smooth partially proper over K finite over ℚ_p (mixed, arithmetic); G a p-adic Lie group

locator.where: Definition 6.4.4, Lemma 6.4.8, Propositions 6.4.10 and 6.4.12, p. 155; ALRS line 8384

tests.name: torsorSen_cyclotomic
tests.statement: For K_∞ = K(μ_{p^∞}), K^{u,la}_∞ = K(μ_{p^∞}) uncompleted, so ALRS Proposition 6.4.10 recovers K^HT = GSpec(K(μ_{p^∞}))/Γ^la as in 9.7; θ^arith is dual to the identity of Lie(Γ) = ℚ_p, the Sen operator of the cyclotomic character.

tests.name: torsorSen_trivial
tests.statement: For the trivial torsor g_β = 0 and all Sen operators vanish.

tests.name: torsorSen_notSurjective
tests.statement: For a torsor with non-surjective θ^geo, e.g. a torsor pulled back from a point, ALRS Proposition 6.4.12 does not apply and X^HT need not be the quotient of the locally analytic spectrum.

layers.title: Twistor cohomology, duality, Chern classes and the Riemann–Hilbert functor

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.shriekAble
targets.statement: Call a map f: Y → X of Gelfand stacks Δ-!-able if f^{Div¹} is !-able (ALRS Definition 6.5.1, p. 159, ALRS line 8628). A map A → B of connective ℚ_p-algebras is finitely presented if π_0(B) is a finitely presented π_0(A)-algebra and L_{B/A} is perfect, and a map of Berkovich spaces is locally †-finitely presented if locally on strict closed covers it is a composite of †-rational localizations and analytifications of finitely presented maps (ALRS Definition 6.5.2, p. 160, ALRS line 8640); call it locally †-l.c.i. if moreover the analytifications can be taken to be regular Zariski closed immersions into overconvergent polydiscs D^{n,†}_X (ALRS Remark 2.1.1(2), p. 14, ALRS line 697). Prove: (1) a †-formally étale map whose perfectoidization is arc-locally lqfd is Δ-!-able, in particular pro-Berkovich-étale maps are; (2) A¹ → GSpec(ℚ_p) is Δ-!-able with 0-affine diagonal on twistor stacks; (3) for a surjective map A → B of affinoid Gelfand rings that is of finite presentation as a map of animated rings, f^{Div¹} is 0-affine, hence 0-proper and !-able with trivialized codualizing complex; (4) maps of Berkovich spaces locally of †-finite presentation are Δ-!-able (ALRS Proposition 6.5.3, p. 160, ALRS line 8649). Smooth and rigid smooth maps are locally †-l.c.i., hence locally †-finitely presented.
hypotheses: f is a map of Gelfand stacks; in (4) a map of Berkovich spaces locally of †-finite presentation

locator.where: Definitions 6.5.1–6.5.2, Proposition 6.5.3, Remark 2.1.1(2), p. 160; ALRS line 8649

tests.name: shriek_openImmersion
tests.statement: An open immersion of Berkovich spaces is pro-Berkovich-étale with perfectoidization an open immersion, hence Δ-!-able by (1).

tests.name: shriek_closedPoint
tests.statement: The origin of the closed unit disc, the surjection ℚ_p⟨T⟩ → ℚ_p with kernel (T), has L = ℚ_p[1], perfect, so by (3) its twistor stack map is 0-affine, hence !-able with trivial codualizing complex; the same holds for the zero section of A¹ locally on strict closed covers.

tests.name: shriek_identity
tests.statement: Identities are Δ-!-able.

tests.name: shriek_nonLci
tests.statement: The singular point of the cusp y² = x³ is a closed immersion that is not l.c.i. but is covered by (3)–(4): for R = ℚ_p⟨x, y⟩/(y² − x³) and k = R/(x, y), the transitivity triangle for ℚ_p⟨x, y⟩ → R → k, in which d(y² − x³) vanishes at the origin, gives L_{k/R} = k²[1] ⊕ k[2]. This is perfect, so R → k is of finite presentation as a map of animated rings, while H^{−2} ≠ 0 puts it outside the amplitude [−1, 0] of regular immersions; a definition of (3) restricted to amplitude [−1, 0] would miss it.

tests.name: shriek_notFinitelyPresented
tests.statement: The surjection ℚ_p⟨T_n : n ∈ ℕ⟩ → ℚ_p sending every T_n to 0 is not of finite presentation: the derivations ∂/∂T_n at the origin vanish on I² for the kernel I and separate the T_n, so I/I² is infinite-dimensional and I is not finitely generated; (3) does not apply to it.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.dualityQp
targets.statement: Prove: (1) Div^{1,dR} → GSpec(ℚ_p) is cohomologically proper and cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex O⟨1⟩[2], the pullback along Div^{1,dR} = Q_p^HK → Marc(𝔽_p)^HK = GSpec(ℚ_p)/φ^ℤ of the line bundle of the isocrystal (ℚ_p, p^{-1}φ), shifted by 2; (2) β: Div¹ → Div^{1,dR} is 0-proper with 0-affine diagonal; (3) Div¹ → GSpec(ℚ_p) is 0-proper and cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex O_{Div¹}{1}[2], the (φ, Γ)-module of the cyclotomic character in cohomological degree −2 (ALRS Theorem 6.5.4, p. 161, ALRS line 8745). Prove that Q_p^Δ is cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex O{1}[2] (ALRS Remark 6.5.7, p. 164, ALRS line 8864).
hypotheses: ℚ_p-coefficients; the six-functor formalism of 2.2

locator.where: Theorem 6.5.4, Remark 6.5.7, p. 161; ALRS line 8745

tests.name: dual_localTate
tests.statement: With RΓ(Div¹, O) = RΓ(Gal_{ℚ_p}, ℚ_p) (11.7), duality pairs H⁰ = ℚ_p with H²(ℚ_p(1)) = ℚ_p and the two-dimensional H¹(ℚ_p) with the two-dimensional H¹(ℚ_p(1)), local Tate duality.

tests.name: dual_generic
tests.statement: Off the Hodge–Tate locus I is trivial, so O{1}[2] = h′^*O⟨1⟩[2] ⊗ f^*I restricts to h′^*O⟨1⟩[2], the pullback of the dualizing complex of Div^{1,dR} from (1) (ALRS Remark 6.5.6).

tests.name: dual_A1Gm
tests.statement: ω_{BG_m} = O[−1] (Verdier diagonal trick: ω_Δ = O[1]) and ω_{A¹/G_m → BG_m} = I[1], so ω_{A¹/G_m} = I, the ideal sheaf of the universal divisor.

tests.name: dual_wrongTwist
tests.statement: If the dualizing complex of Div¹ were O⟨1⟩[2] everywhere, its pullback to FF_{Q_p^⋄} would be the slope-one line bundle rather than the Tate twist ℚ_p(1) (9.8), contradicting the dualizing complex of FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)} in 6.4(2).

tests.name: tateDuality_modulusWitness
tests.statement: On the mirabolic ℚ_p ⋊ ℚ_p^×, with a acting on ℚ_p by multiplication as BC(O)^× acts on BC(O(1)) (ALRS line 4175) and K = ℤ_p ⋊ (1 + pℤ_p), the generalized index gives δ(a) = [aℤ_p : ℤ_p] = |a|_p, so δ(p) = p⁻¹, as in AnalyticStacks Conventions (4); ALRS Remark 6.5.5 (ALRS line 8819) writes the inverse |a|⁻¹_p. With δ(p) = p⁻¹ the character α^*δ⁻¹ takes the value p at p, and since the result of (1) is O⟨1⟩[2] with O⟨1⟩ = (ℚ_p, p^{-1}φ), the route must send a character χ to the isocrystal (ℚ_p, χ(p)^{-1}φ); combining |a|⁻¹_p with that dictionary would give O⟨−1⟩[2], contradicting the dualizing complex of FF_{Marc(ℚ_p)} in 6.4(2).

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.poincareDuality
targets.statement: Let d ≥ 0 and let f: Y → X be a map of Berkovich spaces, rigid smooth and of pure relative dimension d. Prove: (1) f^{Div¹}: Y^{Div¹} → X^{Div¹} is cohomologically smooth; (2) for the base change f^{Div¹/FF_{X^⋄}}: Y^{Div¹} ×_{X^{Div¹}} FF_{X^⋄} → FF_{X^⋄}, its dualizing complex is f^{Div¹/FF_{X^⋄},!}O ≅ O{d}[2d]; (3) if X is a smooth partially proper rigid space over ℚ_p then f^{Div¹,!}O_{X^{Div¹}} ≅ O_{Y^{Div¹}}{d}[2d] (ALRS Theorem 6.5.8, p. 164, ALRS line 8875). Partial properness in (3) enters only through 11.6 (ALRS Remark 6.5.9, p. 165, ALRS line 8932).
hypotheses: f: Y → X is a map of Berkovich spaces, rigid smooth of pure relative dimension d; X smooth partially proper over ℚ_p in (3)

locator.where: Theorem 6.5.8, p. 164; ALRS line 8875

tests.name: PD_etale
tests.statement: For d = 0 (f rigid étale), f^{Div¹,!}O = O: f^{Div¹} is cohomologically étale.

tests.name: PD_Gm
tests.statement: For Y = G_m over X = GSpec(ℚ_p), f^{Div¹,!}O = O{1}[2]; composed with 12.2 the dualizing complex of G_m^{Div¹} over GSpec(ℚ_p) is O{2}[4].

tests.name: PD_index
tests.statement: The statement is about the upper shriek f^! of the structure sheaf of X^{Div¹}, an object on Y^{Div¹}; the lower shriek f_!O lives on X^{Div¹} and for Y = P¹_X equals O ⊕ O{−1}[−2] (12.5), not O{1}[2].

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.properDuality
targets.statement: Prove that for a morphism f: Y → X of Berkovich spaces locally of †-finite presentation whose underlying map of arc-stacks is proper, f^Δ: Y^Δ → X^Δ (and hence f^{Div¹}) is 0-proper, hence !-able with trivial codualizing complex and f^Δ_! ≅ f^Δ_* (ALRS Proposition 6.5.10, p. 165, ALRS line 8938). Deduce that for a smooth proper morphism f: Y → X of smooth partially proper rigid spaces over ℚ_p of relative dimension d, f^{Div¹}_* preserves perfect complexes and f^{Div¹}_*(M^∨{d}[2d]) ≅ (f^{Div¹}_*M)^∨ for every perfect M on Y^{Div¹} (ALRS Corollary 6.5.11, p. 165, ALRS line 8952).
hypotheses: f is locally of †-finite presentation with proper underlying map of arc-stacks; for the duality, f is smooth proper between smooth partially proper rigid spaces over ℚ_p

locator.where: Proposition 6.5.10, Corollary 6.5.11, p. 165; ALRS line 8938

tests.name: proper_P1
tests.statement: For f: P¹_X → X, f_*O = O ⊕ O{−1}[−2] (12.5); duality gives f_*(O{1}[2]) = O{1}[2] ⊕ O, the dual of f_*O, as the formula requires.

tests.name: proper_identity
tests.statement: For f the identity the statement is trivial.

tests.name: proper_classical
tests.statement: For smooth proper X of dimension d over K and its structure map, the formula pairs f_*O with f_*O{d}[2d]; over a geometric point C this is the perfect Galois-equivariant pairing H^i(X_C, ℚ_p) ⊗ H^{2d−i}(X_C, ℚ_p(d)) → ℚ_p of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomologyPartII §5.9, ℚ_p(d) being the pullback of O{d} to FF (9.8).

tests.name: proper_openDisc
tests.statement: For the open disc over ℚ_p the underlying arc-stack map is not proper, f^{Div¹}_! ≠ f^{Div¹}_*, and f^{Div¹}_*O is not perfect.

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.chernClass
targets.statement: Construct the first Chern class c^Δ_1: BG^Δ_m → B²V(O_{Q_p^Δ}{1}) of animated abelian group stacks over Q_p^Δ as the delooping of the composite of the connecting map G^Δ_m → G[1] of G^Δ_m = G̃_{m,Q_p^Δ}/G with log_Δ[1]: G[1] → V(O{1})[1] (ALRS Construction 6.6.1, p. 166, ALRS line 8992); it gives a weak theory of first Chern classes for X ↦ D(X^Δ) on Berkovich spaces with the Berkovich-étale topology in the sense of Zav Definition 5.2.4 (ALRS Remark 6.6.2, p. 166, ALRS line 9006). Prove compatibility with pro-étale Chern classes over the region (0, p), where O{1} is the Tate twist (ALRS Remark 6.6.4, p. 167, ALRS line 9032), and with Hyodo–Kato Chern classes over (1, ∞) (ALRS Remark 6.6.6, p. 168, ALRS line 9084). Prove that for every Gelfand stack X over ℚ_p and d ≥ 1, with f: P^d_X → X, the map Σ_{k=0}^d c_1^k{d − k}[2d − 2k]: ⊕_{k=0}^d O{d − k}[2d − 2k] → f^Δ_*O{d}[2d] is an isomorphism, so that c^Δ_1 is a strong theory of first Chern classes (ALRS Proposition 6.6.7, p. 168, ALRS line 9093; Zav Definition 5.2.8, p. 45, Zav line 1949).
hypotheses: X is a Gelfand stack over ℚ_p; d ≥ 1

locator.where: Construction 6.6.1, Proposition 6.6.7, p. 166; ALRS line 8992

tests.name: chern_d1
tests.statement: For d = 1, f^Δ_*O{1}[2] = O{1}[2] ⊕ O, the second summand generated by c_1 of the universal line bundle.

tests.name: chern_point
tests.statement: For d = 0 the formula reads O ≅ f^Δ_*O for the identity.

tests.name: chern_kummer
tests.statement: On the region (0, p), c^Δ_1 of a line bundle L restricts to the inverse limit over n of the Kummer classes c_1(L) ∈ H²(X_ét, μ_{p^n}) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §9.3, inverted at p; on smooth proper X/K this is compared with the de Rham class by CohomologyComparisons §6.7.

tests.name: chern_twist
tests.statement: With values in O⟨1⟩ instead of O{1} the class would not be compatible with Kummer classes over (0, p), since O⟨1⟩ pulls back to the slope-one bundle rather than the Tate twist (9.8).

targets.name: TauCeti.Twistor.riemannHilbert
targets.statement: For a smooth rigid space X over ℚ_p prove that f̂: X^{HT^} → X^{cone^} ×_{Â¹/G_m} Q_p^{HT^} is a T^dR_X{1}-torsor, {1} the Breuil–Kisin twist, so f̂ is suave with f̂_♮1 = 1 and f̂^* is fully faithful; the same holds for the overconvergent version when X is partially proper (ALRS Proposition 6.7.1, p. 169, ALRS line 9143). Writing Q_p^{HT^} = Spf(K_∞[[t]])/ℤ_p^{×,la} and B⁺_dR = B⁺_dR(ℚ_p^cyc), prove that after base change along Spf(B⁺_dR) → Q_p^{HT^} the pullback f̂^* is fully faithful with essential image the sheaves whose pullback to X^HT_{ℚ_p^cyc} has †-nilpotent geometric Sen operators, and that vector bundles on X^{cone^/(B⁺_dR, t)} correspond to B⁺_dR-local systems on X_{ℚ_p^cyc} whose underlying Ô-bundle has nilpotent geometric Sen operator (ALRS Proposition 6.7.3, p. 170, ALRS line 9177). Construct the maps Spf(B⁺_pdR,X) → X^{pHT^} → X^{cone^} (ALRS Construction 6.7.5, p. 171, ALRS line 9223) and prove that pullback along F̃: Spf(B⁺_pdR,X) → X^{cone^}, restricted to vector bundles, is the base change along B⁺_dR,X → B⁺_pdR,X of Scholze's functor F(E) = Fil⁰(E ⊗_O OB_dR,X)^{∇=0}, the functor associatedLocalSystem of PadicHodgeTheory §7.1 (ALRS Proposition 6.7.6, p. 171, ALRS line 9237; Sch13 Theorem 7.6, p. 42, Sch13 line 1936). For X smooth over a perfectoid D with a lift X̃ to Spf(B⁺_dR(D)), prove that f^* is fully faithful from flat t-connections on X̃ relative to B⁺_dR(D), nilpotent modulo t, to B⁺_dR-local systems on X (ALRS Proposition 6.7.7, p. 172, ALRS line 9297).
hypotheses: X is a smooth rigid space over ℚ_p (partially proper for the overconvergent version); relative case: X smooth over a perfectoid D with a lift X̃ over B⁺_dR(D)

tests.name: RH_point
tests.statement: For X = GSpec(ℚ_p) and E = ℚ_p with Fil⁰ = ℚ_p, F(E) = Fil⁰(B_dR)^{∇=0} = B⁺_dR, the trivial B⁺_dR-local system.

tests.name: RH_shift
tests.statement: The functor satisfies F(E[1]) = t·F(E) (PadicHodgeTheory §7.1, shift), matching the twist by the Breuil–Kisin ideal on the formal Hodge–Tate stack.

tests.name: RH_nonNilpotent
tests.statement: For X = G_m over ℚ_p^cyc, the v-line bundle obtained from the ℤ_p(1)-torsor of p-power roots of T through a locally analytic character χ: ℤ_p(1) → ℚ_p^× with nonzero derivative has geometric Sen operator a nonzero multiple of dlog T (11.5(5)); this operator is invertible, hence not †-nilpotent, so the bundle is not in the essential image of ALRS Proposition 6.7.3.

tests.name: RH_curve
tests.statement: For any smooth X and E = O with the trivial filtration, F(E) = (OB⁺_dR,X)^{∇=0} = B⁺_dR,X by the Poincaré lemma, the counterpart of f̂_♮1 = 1 in ALRS Proposition 6.7.1.
